The walking grid let a diagonal step pass between two land cells whatever stood at the corner, so a river running corner to corner was stepped past in one step: on the M5a demo's map 522 places where a walker crossed the river too big to wade in 13 s, and 2,648 where a wadeable stream was crossed without wading; on the village of 1,000's map 1,202 and 2,310. Every slice since M1 walked that way, so the rule documented since M1, that rivers above `ford_max_discharge_m3s` cannot be crossed on foot, did not hold wherever a river ran diagonally, and the wade record of step two counted few wades because few were made. **The rule:** a diagonal step passes through one of the two cells at its corner, so it is walked no faster than the better of them allows (and no faster than its destination) and not at all when neither can be walked; route searches, travel fields and landmarks cost every step so, a straight line drawn to straighten a route is held to the same where it passes from one cell to the next by a corner, and the cells a walk is traced over (the wades it makes, the crossings it steps onto) include the corner cell it went by. Wear is traced as before. Tested on a river running corner to corner: too big to wade, no step, route, travel time or straight line crosses it; small enough, the diagonal step costs four times dry ground, as wading does, and a step alongside it past one wet corner is as dry. **What it changed** (behaviour, not saves: no schema change): the M5b demo's seed-9 world's two villages (Willowford and Willowholt) can no longer reach each other at all, and 17 % of the land within 1.5 km of Willowholt is out of four hours' reach; near the village of 1,000's hearth, 61 % of the land within 1.5 km is now over twice its straight walk away (across the river, round its end); in the M5a demo's world 12 % near Ashford is, and its villages still reach each other. A year of the village of 1,000 ends with the same 1,062 people and 238 buildings (241 before), but 308 fields, not 649: the ground households break is on their own bank. It costs 1,070 ms a simulated day against 725 (390 s a year, mostly in the first weeks after loading a save made before, while households give up places now across the river; days 31–40 ran at 732 ms). A ten-year quick look at the dashboard (five worlds of two founding groups) passed seven rows, its population green (96–114 people at year 10 from about 80 founders), food prices, firms, structural failures, accounts and regimes green; *moves between settlements* is amber because in two worlds the founding groups were placed on opposite banks (ADR-0018 §6 places groups by their land, never by whether they can walk to each other) and never met: no visits, marriages or moves. **Tests changed:** the tests of visits, buying from a neighbour, fetching to resell and diffusion that used world 3, whose two camps are now three hours apart round the river, use worlds 9 and 10, whose camps are on one bank; the test that nobody fetches what is not worth the walk keeps world 3, where that is truer still. **Not re-run:** the M5a and M5b demos and every measurement in this log before today ran with walkers stepping between river cells; their records stand for the build they ran on. Re-living them is the M5 demo's (slice AX). In worlds whose villages the trunk river parts, only a crossing joins them: slice AW's step three, a polity's crossing beyond one log, is now what could.
- **Crossings in the observer (2026-10-10, M5c slice AW, step three, first part):** no new ADR. Nothing but the chronicle showed a crossing, so a village's crossing could not be watched being built. **The wire** (1.60): the snapshot carries a crossings revision (a hash of each crossing's state, work done, day opened or failed, rot and owner; 0 with none), and `GetCrossings` lists every crossing in the order begun: its system's name, its banks' centres, its clear span and its members' length (the span and a bearing on either bank), how many members and how thick, its state, the labour it takes and has had, its quality and the share of section rot has taken, its margin over one walker now when open, its owner (a household or a polity), and the kernel's words: *Ada's household's log footbridge, being built: 25% of 72 hours of work*, *..., open since year 2: two members 20 cm thick over 2.4 m, sound; it carries a walker 19.0 times over*, *..., gave way in year 9 under someone stepping onto it*. **The map** draws each crossing's members their length, centred between its banks and along the line from one to the other, as wide as its members side by side and never thinner than about two pixels; one being built is fainter the less of its work is done, an open one greys as rot takes its section, and one that gave way is a dark wreck; the pointer readout gives the words of the one under it. The web fetches the list again only when the revision changes. **Tested:** a host test lists none in a new world, then a log being built by the first household, laid by hand, with its revision, owner, banks, members' length and words; web unit tests of the decoder, where the members lie, which crossing the pointer is on (the nearer of two, none off the members' ends), and how each state is drawn. No e2e of its own: no world builds a crossing within an e2e's time, and nothing can place one yet; the observer and earthworks e2e pass with this host. No save change; a world without crossings sends a revision of 0 and nothing else changes.
- **Crossings built together (2026-10-10, M5c slice AW, step three, second part; ADR-0013 §3, ADR-0009 §9):** no new ADR (ADR-0009 §9 gains a polity's crossing). **The issue and the law** (content API 67, `core:policy/works_crossing`): the issue `fords` is present where a household of the settlement wades a stream at a site a crossing of a system its people know could span, within the work's walk of the hearth, with no crossing standing or being built there or a cell either side (a step aside to a deck costs about what a wade saves), and whose wades, all the settlement's households' together, would repay the work over the crossing's life (step two's household rule, for the village). One weighing moves may propose a crossing at one of the three such sites their own household wades most (research 09-05 §3.3: a few packages per decision). Each household forecasts it as the food a year the walking it would save could bring, less what its equal share of the work, spread over the crossing's life, could, an hour worth the food an hour of the household's own work brings at its own costs (M3a; research 11-07 §2.3: communal labour priced at the production it forgoes): in the units of every other forecast. The template bears on autonomy (−0.5: a share of every household's hours is asked, as a common store asks a share of every harvest). A polity builds one at a time. **Passed**, the polity begins the crossing, its own; each household is asked an equal share of its work, labour asked and labour given kept apart (research 09-06), and nothing follows a share not given (as with a curfew's keeping, 09-06 §1.5; ADR-0015's labour-days obligation waits until a default can mean something). **The work:** someone who knows the law in force may work on the polity's crossing as on their household's, weighing the walking it saves their own household and, while their household has not given its share, what keeping to the gathering's word is worth to them, weighed as a levy's payment is (the norm that the gathering binds, their stance on the law, their regard for its sponsor; a new reason, *the work the gathering asked of their household*). The hours each household gave are kept with the crossing (saves 70), its members' quality drawn from its builders' skill as any crossing's, and the chronicle says the village's people finished it. Households, too, no longer begin a log a cell beside a crossing that stands or is being built. **Found while measuring, before committing** (two-year runs of the seed-9 and M5a demo worlds): (1) the forecast first priced an hour of walking at what it is worth in a choice made now (`decision.w_walk_hour`, 2 points) for every hour of a year, making an hour a year worth a fifth of a year's food in the forecasts' units: Willowford put a crossing to its gathering most weeks, its two-thirds custom turning nearly all down, and passed two; (2) a polity could begin crossings while others stood unbuilt, and sites a cell apart each counted: in the M5a world Oakholt passed about 50 and began about 40, most never worked; (3) with the hour priced at foregone production, no household's stake in a crossing reaches a stance (a few hundredths of a point against the 0.25 margin), and the template's first bearing, reciprocity +0.5, decided every vote: Oakholt passed 42 and finished 41 in two years, Willowford 22 of 22. That bearing misread the core value (reciprocity is "that what one household gives or takes from another is given back"), and was corrected once the measurement showed it decisive: NUDGE, the template now bears on autonomy alone; (4) even so, with stakes this small a crossing is proposed when the deliberator's own spread brings it up (a softmax at 0.5 points over a 0.5-point cost) and passes on regard for its sponsor, so Willowford still built 22 in two years, one at each site its people waded, until the issue was held to sites whose wades the village would repay. **Tested:** in world 4 with every household but one wading the stream about 400 times a year, no household begins a log, the village has a site there, a law to build it brings each wading household more than the one that wades nothing (whose forecast is a loss); passed by hand, the polity begins it, and its people give their shares until it opens: several households' hours, together its labour; the chronicle says the village finished it; nobody begins one beside it, and it saves, loads and goes on alike; a schema-69 save loads with no site named and no share kept; the reason codes stay unique; the full suite, clippy and the ten smoke worlds pass. **Measured (two years each, by this build):** in the seed-9 demo world Willowford (21 households) proposed two crossings, on days 241 and 269 of the run, both passed with nobody against (29–0 and 35–0), and each was built within three days by 15 and 13 of its households, most giving their share (about 4 hours) and some up to 11; no other site there repays its work, and Willowholt (9 households) had none. In the M5a demo world Oakholt (17 households) built four: three in the run's first month, each passed by about 30 to 4 and built within six days, and a fourth a year later (31 to 5); Ashford and Sedgebrook proposed none. **Not built, recorded:** a crew limit (11-07 §2.3: about five workers for a log footbridge over one to six days; here as many work at once as choose to, as on buildings, so 82 hours are done in a day or two); the trestle over the trunk river and the places reachable only across a crossing (the brief's second term), where a crossing's stakes would be large; giving up a stalled crossing (a polity's would block its next); mending one; and any consequence of a share not given. The deliberator reckoning its chance of passing by the support it expects rather than by the share its custom requires (ADR-0013 §5) is noted for the deliberator, not changed here.
- **Crossing crews (2026-10-10, M5c slice AW, step three, third part; ADR-0009 §9):** no new ADR. A bridge system names its `crew` (content API 68): at most that many choose to work on one crossing in a day, and anyone else who would is told it is full (a new reason, *as many as there is room for are already at work on it today*; research 11-11 §1.3: progress is limited by the usable work front). The core's log footbridge takes 5, the crew research 11-07 §2.3 states for a simple log footbridge's one to six working days. The day's count is kept with the crossing (saves 71). It is counted as each person chooses the work, not as they arrive: **found while measuring**, counting arrivals let everyone who chose in the morning, before the first of them got there, work, and Willowford's second crossing still took its 82 hours in two days. The chronicle's sentence for a crossing that gives way now says whose it was (the village's by its name, a household's by its elder's) and is kept with that settlement. `civ-host neighbours` now reports, each year, how each polity stands toward the others, the claims, agreements and crossings its gathering decided, and every agreement and crossing in the chronicle, and at the end every agreement with both sides' law histories and how many crossings were begun and stand open. **Tested:** with the village's crossing's crew held full four days running, no work is done on it, which fails with the limit removed (4 hours are done); no day's crew exceeds five; it took at least as many days as its crew allows; a household's crossing that gives way is named as its household's; a schema-70 save loads with no crew kept; the reason codes stay unique; the full suite, clippy and the ten smoke worlds pass. **Measured (two years each, by this build):** in the seed-9 demo world Willowford built the same two crossings (82 hours each), each finished on the fifth day after its gathering agreed to it, where before one was finished the next morning and the other the same morning; in the M5a demo world Oakholt built the same four (67 hours each), finished on the fourth to sixth day, where before three of them were finished by mid-morning of the day agreed and one on the seventh. Both now fall within 11-07 §2.3's one to six working days; the votes and sites were as before.
- **The M5a and M5b demos lived again on today's walking (2026-10-10, slice AX, the M5 demo's first part):** both demos' worlds lived their thirty years again after the fix to walking between a river's cells, on the build of slice AW step three's second part (before crews held; they would add a few days to each village crossing). **The M5a demo** (`civ-host neighbours`, seed 1, three founding groups of 40): 120 founders became 249 people (Ashford 72, Oakholt 95, Sedgebrook 82), every year's checks passed. The observer's wave of ten households (49 people) came in year 11 and founded Alderholt, which was abandoned within the year, its people moving to Sedgebrook; 25 of them lived there at the end, 16 died and 8 left the map. People moved between settlements 63 times with their households (the 48 from Alderholt among them) and 5 times on marrying, nobody to found one: no coalition gathered, where the first record had 13 households leave Oakholt to found Fernfield. Oakholt and Sedgebrook, whose people visited each other some 9,600 times and made 73 purchases between them, came to hold each other wary within thirteen years; Oakholt and Sedgebrook claimed places, 18 claims in six of the years, all passed. **No agreement was made in thirty years** (the relations report lists none), so none reached ratification. Oakholt built 14 village crossings (15 crossings begun in all, 6 standing at the end); from year 16 their logs gave way to rot, under walkers nine times, and one fall killed (Sela, year 16), the village building again at the same sites. **The M5b demo's seed-9 world** (`civ-host twin`, 30 years with trade and without): as the fix predicted, Willowford and Willowholt never met (no contact between them in either life), so neither took the other's way of roofing: the M5b demo's finding does not hold on today's walking in that world, and in its second world the villages cannot reach each other either. Instead each village splintered on its own bank: six new settlements with trade and ten in the twin, and the 35 purchases between settlements with trade were between Willowford and the villages its own people founded. Every check passed in both lives. **What it leaves the M5 demo:** M5's fourth part, a treaty failing ratification, needs an agreement to reach a gathering; none has in any run since slice AU (the funnel: villages counter-claim the places they share, so leave between them grants nothing). The time box is for that, not for enclosures.
- **The agreement funnel, and need over a claim (2026-10-10, slice AX, the M5 demo's second part; time-boxed):** no new ADR. **Why no agreement reaches a gathering:** a household holds a place its own polity claims as its own even when another polity claims it too (slice AU step one, chosen because without it two villages that both claimed their shared fishing places each abandoned them). Villages counter-claim what they share within weeks of seeing each other there, so after that neither household loses anything to the other's claim, leave between them grants nothing, the issue *claimed from us* ends, and seeking terms over shared ground never opens; agreements can come only from one-sided claims, which are rare. In M5 nothing makes a contested claim costly (force is M6's), so this is the rule's honest consequence, not a bug in the move. **Tried and not adopted:** without the exception (a place another polity claims weighed at `claimed_worth` though one's own claims it too, and the issue held for it), a test pair of villages that both claim the place they gather most agreed on mutual leave within a month, and the M5a demo world from its year-11 save saw 15 meetings in six years (none in the same years unchanged), one agreement in force (Oakholt gave Birchfield 100 kg of grain for a year's leave on its places, carried by its keeper) and a second offered. But in that life Sedgebrook, about 90 people after taking in Alderholt's wave and twice short of food, emptied into Oakholt in year 14 and by year 17 both old villages were abandoned; with need also overriding claims (below), everyone but a few ended in Ashford (172 people). From the year-21 save the change brought no meeting in six years. **A fragile village, not a measure:** the same save lived with need overriding claims alone also emptied Sedgebrook in year 14 (77 to 9 within a season, its people to Oakholt and Ashford), so three of four lives from it did, each differing only in how a household weighs claimed places, and only the unchanged life kept Sedgebrook (about 69 people). A small change tips it, and which life it gives says little about the change. The exception stands on plausibility: with no cost to contesting ground, each side holding its own claim good is likelier than both keeping off; contested claims become costly with force in M6. **Kept:** a household some of whose people are going hungry (drawing on their body's reserve) weighs no other polity's claim when choosing where to gather or dig (research 04-09 §5.3: what a breach is worth turns on the agent's needs and alternatives). Tested: two lives of a world whose outsiders' households have no food and are drawing on their reserve, one of which heard of a claim on the place they gathered most, work it alike over five days; without the rule, the one that heard works it less. **What it leaves the M5 demo:** M5's fourth part, a treaty failing ratification, has not emerged in any run since slice AU, because no terms are agreed between villages that share ground. The prior the plan offered to nudge (a negotiator's caution about thin gatherings) acts only after terms are agreed, so it cannot help; nothing was nudged. The fourth part is shown in a test world instead: two villages each claiming a place only the other's people work, where most of one village's people (all but the three the other's people know) saw the others trespass these past weeks. A negotiator predicts support by members' forecasts and regard, not their views (nobody sees another's view), so whoever of that village meets the seeker, one of the three, agrees to five years' mutual leave; the seeker's gathering passes it 7 to 2 (17 of 19 came), and the other turns it down 3 to 8 (22 of 23 came), those against all holding that the first village harms theirs. The chronicle and the observer's agreement view say so with both law histories side by side ("passed on 10 March of year 1, 7 for, 2 against, 17 of 19 came; lapsed" beside "turned down on 11 March of year 1, 3 for, 8 against, 22 of 23 came"). A ratification failing on its own in a lived world waits for contested ground to cost something.
- **The fortification kit moves to M6, and M5 is closed (2026-10-10, slice AX):** no ADR (the M5c design's amendments to ADR-0009 and ADR-0010 for enclosures are not made). **Why:** what an enclosure does without war, in the relations brief (§1.8), is that outside takers must cross at a gate or climb, slower and more often seen; but in M5 people take only from their own settlement's stores (ADR-0020 §6 leaves takings between villages to M6), so a line round a village keeps out nobody who takes, and its only effects would be its costs (the walk round to a gate, the hours, the mending). Every household's forecast of an enclosure law would be a loss, so nobody would build one and its design would go untested by use. Its purpose arrives with M6's force and sieges (research 11-11 §1.4: entry, endurance, relief and negotiation as competing processes), which should shape it: built now it would likely be rebuilt then. **Carried to M6 as designed:** an enclosure as a line of sectors 10–25 m long (11-11 §2.2), each with a ditch (an ADR-0010 earthwork, its spoil a bank inside), a palisade of ADR-0009 parts rotting at the foot by wetness, and gates; walls laid on the walking grid as decks are, by the least of ground and climbing (climbing slow and seen); a polity's law naming the line, how work is raised and whether the watch keeps a gate, households outside the line paying without its cover; and the security dilemma (13-05 §1.5), which needs force to fear. **M5 closed:** M5a (several settlements), M5b (trade and diffusion) and M5c (relations and works) are implemented: claims over wild ground, agreements ratified by each side's own custom and performed by people carrying real goods, log footbridges built by households and by villages with crews. The trestle over a trunk river, other bridge systems (rope, truss, the stone arch) and per-polity currencies are not built. Its shared demo: on the corrected walking the M5b worlds' villages no longer meet (the earlier diffusion record stands for its build), and a treaty failing ratification is shown in a test world, not lived (above).
- **M6 design (2026-10-10, plan §7):** from four briefs (`docs/briefs/m6-health.md`, `m6-fire.md`, `m6-war.md`, `m6-observer.md`), the citations ADR-0021 and ADR-0015 §8 rest on checked against the reports: 12-01 §2.1 (10–30 L a person a day for hand-carried supply, where evidence is absent) and §3.1 (oak-lined wells in the early Neolithic); 12-02 §1.1 (do not "spontaneously generate a particular infection merely because a midden becomes large") and §5.3 (groundwater as sparse, directional connections); 03-02 §1.4 (a well needs construction depth, inflow and stored water), §2.2 (geological priors, "not measured universal ranges") and §5.1 (64–128 m groundwater cells); 05-03 §1.1 (three clocks; infection is not illness), §4.3 (a closed world may lose a pathogen for good, and nothing recreates it), §7.2 (exposure integrated, not arbitrary daily rolls) and §7.6 (mortality calibrated in lived runs); 05-01 §1.3 (exceptional deaths as excess over the baseline, "not another copy of ordinary disease mortality"); 05-05 §2.2 (organized supportive care at a relative risk of 0.95, a low-confidence prior); 03-07 §1.3 (an explicit origin, natural or intervention, so interventions do not contaminate records); 12-07 §1.1 and §1.8 (the response chain; never receiving help is its own outcome); 15-01 §3.5 and 15-02 §1.1 (nearness in time is not a cause; `caused_by`, `enabled_by`, `responded_to`, `part_of` and `occurred_after` are not interchangeable). **M6 is split in three** (§7), as M5 was, because its contents are three kinds of work, each with its own part of the demo: M6a, water and sickness (the cholera outbreak); M6b, fire, masonry and floods (the great fire and its masonry code); M6c, war and conquest (the siege). **In that order** because each uses the one before: floods rise from M6a's rivers by the day, a siege's endurance turns on wells and stores, and the fire and the siege are watched in the Incidents panel M6a builds; war comes last because the fortification kit and raids need force, and force should be shaped by what a siege does to water and food (the kit's move, above). **One ADR now,** [ADR-0021](decisions/0021-water-and-sickness.md) (water and sickness), which amends ADR-0009 and ADR-0010 for wells, and an amendment to ADR-0015 (§8: incidents of every kind, episodes, typed links), as the observer brief suggested, since the incident record generalizes ADR-0015's; M6b and M6c are designed when reached, one ADR each expected. **Four slices for M6a** (§7): AY (rivers by the day, groundwater and wells), AZ (sickness), BA (what people see and do), BB (the Incidents panel and the M6a demo). **The briefs' open questions, answered.** *Health brief:* (1) the plague tool offers a menu of authored diseases (cholera and bacillary dysentery first); "plague" is the tool's name, and plague proper waits until rodents and fleas can carry it (05-03 §1.2: transmission must follow a plausible route). (2) No world gets a declared introduction on a fixed day, which would be a scheduled event; the dashboard's epidemics row is grey unless an introduction happened, until imports from off the map exist (M9). (3) Well rights: a household's well serves its own people and its kin's households, a polity's well its members, and a household short of water may draw at any source it knows (need over another's word, as with claims, above). (4) Founders know well-digging and lining (12-01 §3.1). (5) Forecasts price a believed death as `w_death` days of work, a design prior; values still weigh on top. (6) The drought tool holds the weather's slow anomaly at a dry value for 3–24 months, keeping wet-day persistence and temperature coherent. (7) Fords stay on mean discharge in M6a; M6b designs floods and changing fords together. (8) Disease deaths are excess over the Siler baseline until a disease is measured endemic in lived worlds. (9) Suspicion is held per person, a tally of their own records. (10) Tallies of contact with the sick, and quarantine, wait until a lived outbreak shows what people would need them for. (11) Blessings and curses (ADR-0016 §5) touch an episode only through its severe-stage death draws. *Observer brief:* (1) the Takings panel becomes one Incidents panel. (2) Coverage ships *could reach* and *did come*; probes on copied worlds come later. (3) The chronicle is the observer's and may tell truth, as it tells takings (ADR-0015 §7), but an outbreak's entries count cases and deaths and never name a source as their cause: what fouled a source is in the episode page's truth column, beside what people know. (4) The plague tool targets a person only: a source as its target would make "traced to a well" the observer's doing. (5) Satisfaction is dropped from plan §5.4's dashboards: nobody in the world states one, and grievances against a provider are already ADR-0016's. (6) Destructive tools are always offered, each use an `Influence` record marked as the observer's wherever it shows. (7) ADR-0015 is amended (above). (8) Charts stay SVG, as the market panel draws them, until a panel needs more. (9) Flood water on the map and (10) the siege page are M6b's and M6c's. Weather visuals and fake interiors go to the Unreal track (§7). **Bench, not yet clean:** a year of 3,000 people in three settlements of 1,000 at Max took 1,461 s on this build, against slice AL's 1,179 s, but it ran while four agents built on the same container; slice AY measures it again alone before adding daily water work.
- **Water under the ground and rivers by the day, as built (2026-10-10, M6a slice AY, step one, ADR-0021 §1–§2):** no new ADR. **Measured first:** the 3×1,000 bench alone on the container (`bench_village --people 1000 --groups 3 --size 1024 --seed 2 --known --max`): a year in 1,286.5 s, against slice AL's 1,179 s on the same arguments, about 9 % slower after M5's additions; the ten-minute budget stays unmet, as recorded at AL. The design's 1,461 s ran on 768 cells while four agents built, so it compared with neither. **What the soil cannot hold:** the reference soil's daily surplus, until now clamped away, is kept (`DayWater.surplus_mm`), with its long-run mean over the landscape's 300 climatology years (`Climatology.surplus_mm_per_day`: 0.52 mm a day, 191 mm a year, in the temperate valley). **The aquifer** (`civ_land::water`): one head per habitat patch (128 m, inside research 03-02 §5.1's 64–128 m), on 03-02 §1.3's storage equation: recharge, exchange with the four neighbouring patches at the harmonic mean of their transmissivities, and exchange with the river, lake or sea in a patch at its transmissivity times twice its channel's length over the patch's side, at most four (a design prior: the water lies about half a patch from the middle); a patch of water alone is held at its water's level, which is the mean of its river beds, lake levels and the sea's; a head that reaches its patch's lowest land cell stops there, the rest seeping out. Each day is lived in explicit sub-steps sized from the patch that empties fastest (1–3 on the measured worlds). **Units of ground** (content API 69, the land profile's `[groundwater]`): first match by habitat, each drawing its conductivity evenly in its logarithm and its specific yield evenly once a world, within 03-02 §2.2's priors: alluvial sand under water, wet margins and floodplain (0.1–100 m/day, 0.15–0.30, 10 m thick, from 03-02 §1.4's worked well), silty slope deposits under the lower-slope woodland (0.001–0.1, 0.03–0.15, 10 m), weathered rock under the rest (0.001–10, 0.005–0.05, 15 m), as the health brief §1.2 proposed; the thicknesses are design priors. Half the surplus recharges, the rest runs off at once (`recharge_share`, a tuning value: the research gives no partition for this landscape). **Settled, not spun up:** when a world is made (before the year a new world lives first) and when a save from before schema 72 loads, the heads go by projected over-relaxation to where the mean recharge would hold them for good (100–307 sweeps, under 0.03 s for 4,096 patches). ADR-0021 §2 said "spin up over some years of the landscape's climatology"; the steady state under the mean is what such years average toward, at a fraction of the cost, and the year a new world lives first gives it a season. **The runoff store:** what ran off, what groundwater gave the water net of what the rivers lost to it, and what seeped out enter one store for the world, which lets go `1 − e^(−1/3)` of what it holds a day (`recession_days` 3, tuning); its outflow against the mean surplus is the day's flow factor (`Land::flow_factor`), which scales every reach's mean discharge, derived from the saved store. **Springs** are derived from the heads: a patch off the water whose head stands at its lowest ground, where what flows to it from the patches round it at today's heads is at least `spring_min_m3_day` (0.5 m³, a design prior: 25 people's 20 L), rising at that lowest cell. **Saved:** the heads (doubles) and the store in the land section (`Land.water`, schema 72); the aquifer is derived from the map, the content and the seed. **Tested:** 03-02 §4's storage test (50 mm of net recharge raises a closed aquifer of specific yield 0.2 by 0.25 m); every cubic metre accounted for day by day on a wet slope over a river; settled heads hold under the mean and the store then lets go the mean; a dry spell lowers heads and flow, a storm's runoff passes at once; a spring where recharge from a high patch meets a low one; open gravel (1,000 m a day) stepped stably; a new world's water table under its ground; splitting an advance changes nothing. **Measured** (probes on the river-valley preset at 1,024 cells): over thirty years of seed 1's weather the accounts close (in 376,660,763 m³ against out 376,263,424, the aquifer +516,002 and the store −118,664), and the mean flow factor is the surplus's against its mean (0.988 against 0.99; seed 2, 0.919 against 0.92); single years run from 0.16 to 2.2 of the mean flow with their weather. The rivers are flashy: below a quarter of their mean on 172–355 days a year, because the silty lower slopes (42–73 % of the patches on the seeds measured) hold almost nothing and give their recharge back as seepage within days. Homes on the valley floors stand above a water table 0.7–3.6 m down at the median and at most 2.2–5.7 m, on four seeds, steady through the year where a river holds it (03-02 §2.3: a Chilean sample of dug wells ran 1.48–10.1 m, prehistoric Yangtze wells mostly under 3 m). Springs are plentiful: 500–1,560 a map, 8–24 a square kilometre, where heads meet the ground in valleys too small for a mapped river. A day's water costs 0.03–0.08 ms. **Nothing in the world reads it yet:** forty days of the village of 1,000 lived on from one schema-71 save by the build before (in its own worktree, with its own content) and by this one are the same in every section but the content and the land. Fords stay on mean discharge (§9, "M6 design"). **Not yet:** sources people choose and use that flexes (step two), wells (step three), the observer's view (step four).
- **Sources people choose, and the water they use, as built (2026-10-10, M6a slice AY, step two, ADR-0021 §1):** no new ADR. **Measured first:** with walks taken from each settlement's hearth (the routing field is the settlement's since slice AL), founding bands settle 0–89 m from a river or lake on eight river-valley seeds, and a spring could rise nearer than the river at only two of them, so springs nearer than the river will be rare until something besides the walk weighs (suspicion, slice BA). **Sources:** the settlement's routing field keeps, besides the nearest cell at fresh water, every patch's lowest ground off the water that it reaches nearer than that cell, nearest first; when a person weighs fetching water, the nearest of those whose patch is a spring today (`Water::spring_at`: the head at its lowest ground, at least `spring_min_m3_day` flowing to it) and has a load left today is the place, else the river or lake. **A spring gives what flows to it in a day:** loads drawn at each spring are counted for the day (`SpringDraws`, saved in the places section, let go at the day's turn), and once less than a load is left nobody sets off for it; someone already on the way still draws. **Draws are uses:** every load is logged as a use of its source (`Place::Source`, the cell people stand on), so households know where they draw and whom they meet there; no polity may claim a source (`Place::claimable`), so it raises no issue of outsiders and no trespass. **Use follows the walk** (content API 70, the people profile's `water_use_by_walk_min`): each household keeps the litres each of its people use a day, set when water is brought home from the walk to where it was drawn, interpolated on `[[15, 20], [30, 10]]` (one-way minutes, litres), a tuning curve within research 12-01 §2.1's prior of 10–30 L for carried water and its benchmarks (up to 20 L at 5–30 minutes of collection, often under 5 L beyond); every use of a household's water rate reads it. Saves 73 (`Household.water_use_l`, 0 for the profile's; the places section's draws). **Tested:** a spring made nearer than the hearth's river (seed 6) gives its 500 L to the first 33 loads and the rest of the village goes to the river, households then using 20 L, and the next day it gives again (the draw cap checked by breaking it: 690 L were drawn); a spring whose head stands a metre below its ground is left for the river; draws at a spring save, load and go on alike for a day; the curve's interpolation; sources are never claimable. **Measured:** forty days of the village of 1,000 lived on from one schema-71 save by step one's build and this one differ only in the content, the households (their water rate) and the places (draws logged), at the same speed (825 ms a day); a year of three villages of 100 drew 149,072 and 151,149 loads from rivers on seeds 1 and 2 and none from springs, and on seed 3 98,957 loads from three springs and 49,972 from rivers; no household anywhere walked far enough to use less than 20 L. **Not yet:** wells (step three), the observer's view (step four).
- **Wells, as built (2026-10-10, M6a slice AY, step three, ADR-0021 §1 and §3):** no new ADR. **A well is its own record** (`civ_land::wells`), as a crossing is: the ground its digging took (no plot, field, pit or heap may be laid over it), its depth and target, the labour and skill put into it, its lining's quality and the share rot has taken, the water standing in its shaft and when, what was drawn from it since midnight, and its state (being dug, open, given up, fallen in); saves 74 (a wells section; target kind 15, chronicle kind 45). **Content API 71** brings well systems as a content kind: the core's timber-lined well is dug 1.5 m across and lined 1.2 m inside (research 12-01 §2.2), the digging at the profile's 8 h a cubic metre (ADR-0010 §2; 14 h a metre) and the lining at 16 h a metre (a design prior: some 19 m of split plank a metre at about a metre an hour), dug a metre below where its diggers expect water and at most 10 m deep (03-02 §2.3: dug wells of 1.5-10.1 m, prehistoric Yangtze wells mostly under 3 m), refilling over a 50 m radius of influence (03-02 §1.4), hauled up at 0.15 minutes a metre of lift (a design prior), its lining rotting 0.05 a year on ground of wetness 1 (a design prior beside 11-07 §2.4's 10-20 years for untreated log bridges), with room for two to work. Founders know well digging (12-01 §3.1: timber-lined wells in the early Neolithic), learned at the age of the work; work on a well is gated by it, so the young learn beside a knower. *Found while measuring:* nobody knew the technique at first, because founders learn each technique at the age of the work it gates and nothing yet counted a well system's work; `Catalog::work_age` now does, and a technique only a bridge or well system names gates work (E3005). **The yearly review** (on each household's keyed day, one well's work at a time): beside its home plot, on the nearest claimable ground in front of it, a well a metre below the water level its people expect, from the water standing in the nearest well of its settlement, or below the floor of one given up dry (its depth becomes what others expect), or else the water they draw from now (the lowest water beside the bank, or the spring's ground); begun when the walk from home to that water and back, and its lift, less the walk to the well and its lift, for every load its people use, over the years its lining would last at the quality its people would lay it, is more than the hours to dig and line it. A household whose lining rot has taken half of what its quality left weighs relining it the same way (the lining's hours), and its quality is drawn again. **The work:** a session as on a crossing, but each hour weighed by the walking a year of the well would save for it. Counted over the lining's whole life, as for crossings, a session of digging outscored hunger (40-120 points against hunger's 20 at most), and in a probe people dug while their stores ran down; a year's return sets it beside useful work (a design prior, with the store review's three-year horizon as precedent). At its target a shaft meets water where the water table stands above its floor, its lining's quality drawn from its diggers' average skill (ADR-0009 §6), or it is dug a metre deeper, or at the deepest given up; the chronicle tells each. **Water:** an open well's column refills toward the water table of its patch at Thiem's rate over the column (03-02 §1.4); a load takes from the column, or what it holds of one; people draw at the well that takes least time there and back with its lift, among their own, their close kin's households' and, while their household holds less than half a day's water, anyone's (ADR-0021 §1, rights v0; the half day is a design prior), when that is no longer than the spring or bank; what each well gave is taken from the water table under it at midnight (patches of open water excepted). **Rot:** monthly, by the habitat's wetness and the month's rain against its usual, as for posts' feet; a lining whose rot has taken all its quality left falls in. Wells pass with a household's plots and buildings. **Tested:** the column's refill, its never falling below the floor and 03-02's 2.26 m³ in 2 m; a household beside its home plot weighing and beginning one, then busy, its people digging it in sessions no larger than its crew; meeting water where the table stands above the floor; a dry shaft deepened to the deepest and given up, after which every well begun expects water below its floor; drawing at one's own well, and a twin with nothing drawn holding the water table exactly that much higher at the next midnight and the same elsewhere; rights for strangers, the short of water and kin; relining past half and falling in; saves exact before and after a day; the session's weight in a decision unit test; the content kind's ranges. **Measured** (three villages of 100 on the river-valley preset, two years, seeds 1-3): 44, 72 and 62 wells begun by about 70 households each, 25, 59 and 55 of them open by the second year's end, none given up or fallen in yet (the river's level, which households expect with no well to go by, lies below the water table under their homes); open wells 1.0-8.5 m deep, medians 5.3, 4.3 and 1.5 m (03-02 §2.3's sample: 1.5-10.1 m, mean 4.8), 54-115 hours of work each on average; wells gave a sixth, a half and a half of all loads drawn over the two years. One of seed 1's settlements, its homes 28-30 m above its river, digs none: its people expect water too deep. Without the lift, and with each session counting the lining's life, it was 45, 72 and 71 wells. *Not established:* seed 2's Stonebank has a famine in its second spring with or without wells; on six runs without them it had 71-96 people at day 511 (mean 84), on five with them 62-94 (mean 72; identities differ run to run). Its harvest, farm hours and the day its food ran short were the same in both, and well work was about 1 % of hours, so the difference is not labour taken from food; it is to be watched in longer runs. **Speed:** forty days of the village of 1,000 lived on from the same schema-71 save as step two took 855 ms a day, against 806 ms by step two's build on the same machine (+6 %; wells give it 0.022 hours of work a person-day by then). Choosing a well first passes over others' wells that could not beat the household's other water at the fastest walk, before anyone's kin is looked up; that changed no choice (the same digests in every section) and took little off. The rest is mostly new trips, to wells, to route. **A flake found on the way, older than wells:** `a_watcher_chooses_once_what_to_do_with_a_taking_they_saw` (`tests/crime.rs`) fails about once in 30-40 runs (1 of 40 on step two's build, 1 of 30 on this one) at `law.watch.cases == brought` (5 against 6). Its world draws a fresh identity each run (`Sim::create`), so only some histories reach it; the watch's count of the cases it brought can miss one its officer brought. Open: find the cause in the watch's bookkeeping. **Not yet:** the observer's view of sources and wells (step four); covers, curbs and silt (slice BA, with contamination); a polity's well by law (slice BA); pits that met water as knowledge.
- **The observer's view of water, as built (2026-10-10, M6a slice AY, step four, ADR-0021 §1-§3):** no new ADR. **Wire 1.61:** the snapshot carries a water revision, which changes whenever a well is begun, dug deeper, opens, rots, is relined, given up or falls in, and with each day lived while the world has wells or ground where a spring may rise (0 when neither), so the observer reads the water again when a well changes and otherwise once a day; `GetWater` lists every well (its system, centre and dug radius, state, depth and target, the water standing in its shaft now and how far down, its lining's quality and rot, its household, and all that in words: "Ada's household's timber-lined well, open since year 2: 4.1 m deep, 1.8 m of water standing 2.3 m down; rot has taken a tenth of its lining"), every spring flowing today with what flows to it and what was drawn there today, the cells at a river's or lake's edge drawn at today with how many times people came there, and the rivers' flow today against their mean; the person inspector gains where their household went for water today, from the day's logged draws ("Their household went for water 6 times today: 4 times to its own well, twice to the water's edge; each of them uses 20 L a day, and it holds 85 L"). The water standing in a well is read through `Land::ground_water`, the one rule the kernel's wells use, so the observer cannot drift from the world. **The map** draws each shaft at its dug radius (never under about two pixels): fresh earth fainter the shallower it still is against its target, blue while water stands in it, brown once given up dry, dark once fallen in; springs as small blue dots, brighter when drawn at today; the places drawn at the water's edge as pale dots by how often; the readout names the one under the pointer, and over a river or lake says how it flows today ("flowing at 40% of its mean today"). Nothing is drawn as coverage: the Water lens, with *could reach* and *did come*, is slice BB's. **The dashboard's water row** is grey, reported and not graded: loads drawn over the run by the kind of place (counted as drawn, not saved: `Population.water_draws`), wells at the end by state, and the litres people use a day; what each uses follows the walk on a tuning curve set inside research 12-01 §2.1's prior of 10-30 L, so that prior cannot judge it. **Tested:** the host reads the water with no world (an error), a new world's (no wells, a flow), and a well and draws set by hand (the well's state, system, water standing and words; two trips at one bank cell; the inspector's line in order of trips); the web decodes the water and builds its query, and draws, finds and words wells, springs and banks; end to end, a world lived 60 days serves the water to the map and the inspector's line to a selected person; the row's words and totals. **Measured:** the dashboard lived its five worlds two years at 512 cells (a quick look, not the dashboard): 432,333 loads, 37 % from wells (2 % of them short of a load), 3 % at springs, 60 % at the water's edge; 71 wells open and 19 being dug at the end, none given up or fallen in; every household's people using 20 L a day, as step two found (nobody walks far enough to use less); the dashboard passed in 72 s. **Slice AY is complete.** **Not yet:** coverage of water per home (the Water lens, slice BB); what people know of others' draws and suspect of a source (slice BA).
- **Diseases, infections and the plague tool, as built (2026-10-10, M6a slice AZ, step one, ADR-0021 §5 and §8):** no new ADR. **Diseases are content** (content API 72, `kind = "disease"`): their routes (water, household), their own clocks as lognormals of a mean and standard deviation (research 05-03 §7.3: infection to symptoms, how long before symptoms shedding starts, how long it is shed and how long after illness, how long the ill are ill), the share of infections with symptoms, the share of the ill severely so by age, the chance a day of dying while severely ill (05-03 §7.6: a hazard by stage, never a fate drawn at infection), how long an infection protects, and the hazard a day a shedding member puts on each other member of a household. The core's cholera takes 05-03 §2.1's clocks (symptoms in 12 hours to 5 days, shed 1-10 days including by the silent, protection 3-10 years) and bacillary dysentery its own (symptoms in 1-2 days, ill about a week, shed up to two weeks after; protection half a year to two, since 05-03 §2.1 warns against lifelong immunity to the genus); the share with symptoms (0.25 and 0.7), the severe share (0.4 and 0.2, flat by age: 05-03 §3.3 finds no defensible age matrix), the death hazards (0.2 a day, killing about half of cholera's severely ill untreated, 05-03 §3.2's "can reach approximately 50%" taken for the severe; 0.03 a day, about 4 % of those ill with dysentery, under the 15 % benchmark among hospitalized *S. dysenteriae* type 1 patients) are design priors, and the household hazards tuning values. **An infection is an episode** (`civ_agents::sickness`, saved, schema 75): who, which disease, the day it came and how (its acquisition record: the observer's influence, or a household as the source, never one member, 05-03 §7.4), its course drawn when it comes (when shed, when ill, whether severe, when it stops protecting), and how it ended (recovered, died, or gone: died of something else or left the world while it ran). **Each day's turn**, after the life table's deaths: the severely ill die of it or not, each by a draw of their own (a blessing or a curse moves it, ADR-0016 §5); a course that has run ends; then everyone exposed by any route sums their hazard and draws once (05-03 §7.2), nobody infected today shedding before tomorrow. Step one has the household route only. **The ill keep to their beds** (`Facts::ill`, `Reason::Ill`): they sleep, eat and rest at home, and do nothing else (05-03 §1.1: illness and work capacity apart from infection). **Deaths** are `Cause::Disease`, excess over the Siler baseline (05-01 §1.3; ADR-0021 §5); the chronicle names the disease ("died of cholera, 34") and so does the inspector. **The plague tool** (`Sim::plague`): the observer brings a disease to one person, as if they took it elsewhere, an `Influence` of a new kind whose subject is the disease; the infection names the record; refused while it runs in them or protects them. No world has a disease until then. **Tested:** a lognormal keeps its mean and spread; a course runs in an order the body allows (nothing before the next day, shedding through the illness, the shares drawn as authored); protection while it runs and until its day after; no introduction, no case in twenty days; the observer's infection, its record, the refusal, its course run and its protection after; the ill asleep, eating or resting every half hour of their second day ill; a household all taking it on the first day a member sheds, and nobody outside it; a severe case dying on its first day ill, the record and the chronicle naming cholera; saves exact with infections running, and three days after alike. **Measured** (30 introductions each into one lived village of 99, household route only): cholera reached 9 of 96 household contacts and made 7 ill in all, one of whom died, each outbreak gone within about a week; dysentery at a household hazard of 0.06 reached 81 of 96 (84 %, the whole home almost every time, shed some 13 days), so it was lowered to 0.02, at which it reached 44 of 96 (46 %), 54 ill and 4 dead, running 18 days on average. Neither left its household: the water route is step two. **Nothing changes without an introduction:** forty days of the village of 1,000 lived on from the same schema-71 save by step four's build and by this one are the same in every section but the content (two diseases), the influences (which now keep the diseases' ids) and the new, empty sickness section, at 861 ms a day against 851. **Not yet:** loads in middens, the ground, wells, reaches and stored water, and the water route (step two); tending and fluid replacement; illness incidents, outbreak episodes and the chronicle of outbreaks (step three); the observer's view and the plague tool in the observer (step four).
- **What people shed, moved through the ground and water, as built (2026-10-10, M6a slice AZ, step two, ADR-0021 §4):** no new ADR. **Loads** (`civ_agents::contagion`, saved, schema 76) are kept per disease in each household's heap (beside its home), each well, each river reach (what passes it today) and each household's stored water by where it was drawn, with loads soaking through the ground on their way to a well or river until the day they arrive. They are counted in doses, an amount that, drunk, is a hazard of one (research 12-02 §5.4's exponential, its rate taken into the dose), so a disease authors what one shedding person adds to their heap a day, ill and silent, and the share that dies a day outside a person (content API 73: `shed_ill_per_day`, `shed_silent_per_day`, `decay_per_day`). Nothing makes a load but someone shedding (12-02 §1.1); a disease that does not pass by water sheds nothing into the heap. **Each day's turn**, after deaths and recoveries and before anyone is exposed: what passed the rivers yesterday has gone downstream; every load decays; what soaked in arrives; whoever sheds adds the day's shedding to their household's heap; the day's surplus (what the soil could not hold) washes `wash_per_mm` a mm of each heap, at most `wash_max`, to the open wellheads and banks within `runoff_radius_m` whose ground lies no higher, split by nearness (none there, it soaks away), and a river carries what reaches it to every reach below it that day; `seep_per_day` soaks in, of which `capture_share` reaches the wells and rivers within `link_radius_m` and no higher, split by nearness, after 03-02 §1.6's travel time d·n/(K·i) through the unit of ground under the heap (its conductivity and specific yield as the world drew them; the water table taken to follow the ground over so short a way, at a slope of at least `min_gradient`), less what dies on the way (12-02 §5.3: sparse links, each with a travel time and a capture share before a separate decay, never the whole load sent to each). **Drawing:** a load drawn at a well takes the share of its load the draw takes of its water, and one at a bank what its litres hold of the reach's day's flow (its mean discharge times today's flow); either goes into the household's store by where it was drawn. **Drinking:** each person drinks `drink_l_per_day` of their household's water, a dose of the store's load over its litres, and the share the household uses in a day goes with the water. The dose is summed with the household route and drawn once; an infection by water names the well or reach most of the store's load came from (05-03 §7.4: a mixture, not one person). **The record:** each day's moves along one way (shed, washed off, soaked in, arrived, drawn) are one record, kept 400 days; a load or move under a thousandth of a dose is let go. All of `[contamination]`'s numbers (0.01 a mm, at most 0.5, 30 m, 0.02, 30 m, 0.1, 0.005, 3 L) and the diseases' shedding (cholera 2,000 doses a day ill and 20 silent, half-life about five days; dysentery 2,000 and 200, half-life about two) are design priors and tuning values, each marked in its file. **Tested:** loads add, take and decay, and a store keeps its sources; a day's moves along one way are one record; a wet day of 20 mm washes a fifth of a heap to the well below it and whatever else lies within reach, all of it delivered and recorded, and what a river takes passes every reach below it; the well's household carries its load home draw by draw with nothing lost or made in the day, and nobody holds any of it who did not draw it; what soaks in arrives on its day, whole, sooner and less decayed through ground ten times faster (by e^(−kΔτ) exactly), and through the slower ground nothing has arrived by then; a household whose water holds a heavy load from a well all take it at midnight, each record naming the well; a world where nobody sheds has no load anywhere; saves exact with loads, stores, loads underway and moves, and four days after alike. **Measured** (a village of 106 lived two years, 24 wells open, 90 days after each introduction): twenty cholera introductions infected 153 (94 by a well, 39 at home, none by the river, since no heap lay within 30 m of it), 42 ill and 12 dead. Six outbreaks reached 14 to 43 people, each when the person it was brought to fell ill and shed thousands of doses a day into a heap above a well others drew from (up to 908 doses in one well); the other fourteen went no further than a home or two. Twelve dysentery introductions infected 286 (216 by wells, 58 at home), 186 ill and 6 dead: four outbreaks reached 41 to 69 people, since it is shed for weeks after the illness; recorded, not tuned (a small infectious dose makes high attack rates plausible where a village shares unprotected wells). The largest outbreak kept 1,643 moves, 93 KB saved. **At the map's 8 m grain one step of ground decides** whether a heap reaches a well: in the test village the household's own well lay 5 cm above its home, so its own heap never reached it, while two neighbours' heaps 16 and 21 m away and about a metre higher did; the tests use the nearest heap above the well. **Nothing changes without an introduction:** forty days of the village of 1,000 lived on from the same schema-71 save by step one's build and by this one are the same in every section but the content and the new, empty pathogen section, at 873 ms a day against 861. **Not yet:** shedding where people work rather than at home (ADR-0021 §4); less runoff into a covered, curbed well; lakes as receptors and sources; hands, food and vessels; tending and fluid replacement, illness incidents and outbreak episodes (step three); the observer's view (step four).
- **Tending, fluid replacement and outbreaks, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice AZ, step three, ADR-0021 §5 amended):** **Tending is chosen work** (behaviour `tend`, `core:activity/work_tending_the_sick`, its id sorting after every older activity's): an adult or child of ten or more whose household has members ill at home still owed a day's care sits with them for a session, worth `w_tend` 6 points for each severely ill member owed a whole day's care and half for one ill but not severely, in proportion to what is still owed (research 05-05 §1.1: care is someone else's labour); its hours are shared among those ill there. Each episode records its care: the first day someone came and who (an incident's "help came"), the hours given on the last day tended, the least relative risk a treatment that carer knew brings, and the hours over the illness. **What care does:** the day's death draw of the severely ill is now made at the midnight after the day, for the day just lived, so that day's care counts; its hazard is multiplied by 1 − (1 − rr) × the share of a day's care given (a disease's `care_h_per_day`, 2 h, 05-05 §2.2's 1-4 caregiver-hours a patient-day), rr being the disease's `care_rr` (0.95, 05-05 §2.2's prior for supportive care) or a treatment's that a carer knew, whichever is less: an effect only of care actually given. The first build gave care all or nothing at 2 h, and a probe found deaths on days of 1 h of care in households where five others were ill; proportional care replaced it. **Fluid replacement** (`core:technique/fluid_replacement`) is a far technique: nobody brings it, tending counts 1 % of its hours toward finding it at 100,000 hours for half, it is learnt in 20 hours of tending while a member of the household knows it, and children learn it at home from ten, the youngest age of tending (the work a treatment is practised in, as building is a program's); cholera names it as a `[[treatment]]` at 0.05, so about 4 % of the severely ill die with a day's care (05-05 §2.1: 3.6 % among 3,703 refugee patients in 1971, 1 % in a demonstration unit). Dysentery names none (05-03 §1.4). A technique named only as a treatment now satisfies the check that a technique gates something (E3005), and the knowledge checks no longer run when a technique failed to compile: in that error path the indices recipes resolved against no longer matched the catalog's, so a fixture with two land profiles reported hearth baking as gating nothing once fluid replacement was inserted before it. **Outbreaks** (ADR-0021 §5 as amended; ADR-0015 §8 leaves the rule there): the cases of one disease among the people of one settlement; a case taken while one is open there is `part_of` it, one taken while none is begins one and its acquisition record is the cause; it ends at the first midnight when none of its cases has run for the disease's incubation mean and three spreads (cholera five days, dysentery three). The chronicle tells each when it begins ("Cholera came to Ashford: Ada took it.") and when it ends with its counts ("Cholera has left Ashford: 14 took it over 21 days; 5 fell ill and one died."). Saves schema 77 (care on each episode, its outbreak, the outbreaks; 76 still loads, with none). **Tested:** care lowers the day's risk by the share of a day's care given and a treatment a carer knew; a severe case lives through its first day and dies at its end without care that counts; with care that takes away all the risk the household tends them and they outlive the illness, the record naming the first day and a member of the household, saved exactly; where a day's care asks a thousand hours they die; whoever of the household tends knowing fluid replacement brings the risk to nothing, and nobody knowing it does not; one who tends beside a household that knows it learns it in exactly 20 hours; an outbreak begins with its first case, gathers the household's cases, saves exactly, ends five days after its last case ended with a sentence giving its counts, and a later case begins another. **Measured** (the village of 106 lived two years, twenty cholera introductions, 90 days each): every one of the 23 severely ill was tended, 340 hours of care in all; 9 of the 41 ill died (22 %) against 12 of 42 before tending, within noise of RR 0.95. With fluid replacement given to everyone first, 2 of 41 died (4.9 %), with 167 infected against 166: care changes deaths, not cases (the M6 health brief's validation target). Some runs had two outbreaks, a late case by water after the first had ended. **Nothing changes without an introduction:** forty days of the village of 1,000 from the same schema-71 save lived by step two's build and by this one give the same time use (to the thousandth of an hour), ties, standing, fields and buildings; the sections that differ are the content, the knowledge, people, receipts and firm sections, which encode the catalog's activity and technique tables (one more of each), and the sickness section's new empty outbreaks; 851 ms a day against 873. **Not yet:** tending by kin or neighbours from other households, and the carer's own exposure by care (step one's household route stands for the household's); remedies other than fluid replacement; the observer's view (step four); a dashboard row for outbreaks.
- **A well dug together by law, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice BA, step four, second part, ADR-0021 §7):** no new ADR. **A household's walk to water, as walked:** each household now keeps the minutes of the one-way walk to the water its people last brought home (`Household.water_walk_min`), set where its use of water already followed the walk. **The issue `water_far` (appended):** a household of the settlement walks far for water, so far that its people use less water for the walk (from the first point of the people profile's `water_use_by_walk`, 15 minutes: research 12-01 §2.1, up to 20 L at 5-30 minutes of collection and often under 5 L beyond), and a well dug together beside the hearth would save the settlement's households more walking over its lining's life than its work, as fords make a crossing an issue. *Found on the way:* without the first condition a 1.4 m well beside the hearth repaid its 41 hours for households walking 25 seconds to the river (six hours of walking a year saved over a 17-year lining), so every ordinary village proposed one in its first week and six tests of gatherings changed; walks that short are not "far", and the rule as households weigh their own wells still decides whether one repays its work. **The policy `dig_well` (appended; `core:policy/works_well`, answering `water_far`, bearing autonomy −0.5 as a crossing built together does):** the well is weighed as a household weighs its own: beside the hearth (sunk within 8 m of a 4 m square at it, a design prior: the gathering place), a metre below where its people expect water (the settlement's wells, else the water they draw from now), of the system its people know whose walking saved over its lining's life most exceeds its work; each household would save, for every load its people use a year, its last walk there and back, as walked, less the walk to the well and back and its lift. Recorded with the law when proposed (`Polity.wells`), begun once passed, the polity's (`Well.polity`; a polity's well holds the polity's id as its household), one at a time. **Each household's stance** is its own forecast, as for a crossing: the food a year the walking it would save could bring, less what its share of the work, spread over the lining's life, could, each hour at what an hour of its work brings (research 11-07 §2.3). **The work** is offered to the polity's people who know the law, as a crossing's is: each session weighs the walking a year the well would save their household for each hour of the work, and, while their household has not given the equal share asked, what keeping to the gathering's word is worth to them (the custom that a gathering binds, their stance and their regard for its sponsor); what each household gives is kept (`Wells.shares`; research 09-06: labour asked and labour given apart), and nothing follows a share not given. When it meets water the chronicle says so ("Hazelstead's people finished the timber-lined well their gathering agreed to dig beside the hearth, Ada digging the last of it: 3.2 m deep, it met water"). **Drawing by right:** the polity's people draw at its well as at their own household's (ADR-0021 §1, rights v0), and count it among the wells they know in weighing their own; its words, a suspicion of it and the water frames name it as the settlement's ("Hazelstead's well"). Nobody relines or covers a polity's well yet: it rots and falls in. Saves 83 (a household's walk, a well's polity, the shares given, a polity's well sites; issue code 12), content API 79. **Tested:** having walked under a minute, no well dug together; walking a quarter of an hour each way, a well beside the hearth that repays its work, every household gaining by it; the review proposing it with the issue `water_far` and its words ("a well 1.4 m deep beside the hearth, each household doing its share of 41 hours of work"); begun once passed, the settlement's in the well's words; one household's hours kept as its share and the well dug deeper; another's finishing it where water stands above its floor, told in the chronicle; someone of the settlement drawing at it by right; all of it saving and loading exactly. **Measured (a probe, not kept):** three villages of 100 (river-valley seeds 1-3) for a year as they live: no polity proposes a well (no household walks far), households dig 18-24 wells of their own, 48-52 ms a day. The same villages with every household's last walk held at 15 minutes each morning (a what-if; their water stays where it is): each polity proposed a well on day 136-143 and passed it, 22-46 for and 0-5 against of 53-65 present; it met water 70-90 days later at 1.9-3.2 m (one, dug dry at 1.3 m, a metre deeper), its 56-97 hours given by 9-16 of 22-27 households; households still dug 18-26 wells of their own, 50-53 ms a day. In ordinary worlds this step changes nothing: founders settle within about 90 m of water. **Step four is complete.** **Not yet:** relining and covering a polity's well; ending a closing once nobody suspects its source; the drought tool and the observer's view of suspicion (step five).
- **The drought tool and the observer's view of suspicion, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice BA, step five, ADR-0021 §8):** no new ADR. **The drought** holds the weather's slow anomaly (the monthly AR(1) that carries wet and dry spells, ADR-0012 §1) at a dry value of 0 to 3 standard deviations for 3 to 24 months (`Weather.hold`, the first day it no longer holds kept with it). The anomaly's monthly draw is still made and still consumes its deviate, and the hold then overrides it, so every other draw of the weather is the one the world would have drawn: wet-day persistence, the gamma amounts and the temperature anomaly are untouched, and the dry value acts only through the anomaly's existing terms (fewer wet days, lighter ones, warmer summers by `slow_warmth_c`). When it lets go, the anomaly drifts back from the held value at the next month's draw as from any dry spell. In the temperate valley 1.5 sd brings about three-quarters of the usual rain and 3 sd about half. The rivers, the water table, springs, wells, fields' water and wild plants feel it only through the rain, as research 03-07 §1.3 asks (natural events and god tools share consequences). **Its origin is kept** (03-07 §1.3, ADR-0021 §8): each month it touched is marked `held` in the weather's record, so statistics can leave it out, and its use is an `Influence` of an appended kind (`Drought`, code 7) whose target is the first settlement, with its months as its subject; using it again while it holds refreshes the same record. The chronicle says "One recorded influence: the observer held back the rain: for 12 months the weather runs dry, until 1 March of year 3." **The observer** holds it back from the map's tools (months and depth chosen from menus); the host answers in words, the weather panel tells it while it holds ("The observer holds back the rain, 2.0 standard deviations dry, until …") and marks each month held, and asks for the weather again at once rather than waiting for the next day. **The inspector's view of suspicion** lists the sources a person holds sicken, with when they came to hold it and the counts of their latest tally ("Holds since 3 May of year 2 that the water at Bo's household's well sickens: of 5 households they know that draw there, 3 had sickness lately, against 0 of 6 that draw elsewhere"): what they believe, which may be wrong. Saves 84 (the hold and the months marked), wire 1.63 (the `Drought` command, `WeatherMonthInfo.held`, `WeatherReport.drought`, `PersonInfo.suspicions`), content API unchanged at 79. **Tested:** the hold in the weather alone (the anomaly held each day, about two-thirds of the rain against the same draws unheld, the months marked, letting go on its day and differing afterwards only by the held value's memory); the tool in a world (refusals out of bounds, the record and chronicle, a repeat refreshing the record, the months held exactly those it touched, drier than the same world's weather unheld, the water table lower, saving and loading exactly mid-drought); the host's command, its refusals and the weather report; the inspector's words for a suspicion; the observer end to end. **Measured (a probe, not kept):** three villages of about 105 people (river-valley seeds 1-3) lived 15 months, with and without a 12-month drought at 2 sd from early spring of the first year: 713-785 mm of rain fell against 873-1,450 mm unheld (1,056 usual); the first year's harvest came to 3%, 13% and 26% less grain, every field limited by its season; at the end the stores held 71, 42 and 37 days of food against 95, 73 and 115; the water table stood 0.4-0.6 m lower on average and households dug a well fewer or none; nobody went short, moved or left, and deaths were no higher, within the window (the next harvest after the drought falls beyond it). Research 03-07 reports national cereal losses of about 9-10% in drought disasters and warns that local fields can do far worse; these villages lost what a single dry year with full granaries would. **Slice BA is complete.** **Not yet:** a drought over one settlement only (the weather is the world's, so it falls on every settlement of the map); relining and covering a polity's well; ending a closing once nobody suspects its source.
- **One Incidents panel, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice BB, step one, ADR-0015 §8):** no new ADR. **One query, every kind in one shape** (wire 1.64, `GetIncidents`): takings (ADR-0015 §1) and cases of illness (each infection, ADR-0021 §5) are rows of one shape, keyed by when each began (a taking to the minute, an infection to its day), its kind and its number, newest first, a page at a time (50 by default, at most 200) from a cursor the page before gives; each kind keeps its own store and the query only reads them. **Each row keeps the three layers apart, in the kernel's words**: what happened, after the name of whoever it begins with ("took cholera on 3 May of year 2 in water drawn at Bo's household's well; ill 4 days, severely; died of it on 7 May of year 2"; "took 12 kg of grain from the household of Rilla on 4 May of year 3; seen by Bram"); what people know ("Known to 12 people as sickness in Bo's household, from 1 first-hand account", from the sickness claim its household made while they were abed; "Nobody knows of it: they were never ill"; for a taking, those who believe they know who took and from how many accounts, and what the household taken from chose); and what the polity knows and did (a taking's case; for a case of illness, the law that would close the source its water came from, or "No law names Bo's household's well"). A layer with nothing in it says so and is never filled from the truth. **Totals by kind** count first, over all time in the scope asked: all of them, those someone in the world knows of, those before a polity, and the observer's share (a case of an outbreak whose first case the observer brought counts as the observer's: 03-07 §1.3, 15-05 §6). **Outbreaks** are listed with their counts ("Cholera at Hazelford, from 3 May of year 2: 14 took it, 9 fell ill, 2 died; it runs"). **An incident's page** (`GetIncident`) has its stamped steps (12-07 §1.1; for a case: took it, shed it, fell ill, seen abed by their household, tended, ended; for a taking: went to take, seen, loss noticed, told, answered, before the gathering, decided), a step not reached saying so in words and a step known only to its day never given an hour (15-02 §1.9); its typed links, recorded when they happened (15-02 §1.1): `caused_by` the observer's influence, the household it was caught from or the source its water came from, and `part_of` its outbreak; and its three layers in lines. **An outbreak's page** (`GetOutbreak`) has its counts, how it began (its first case's own link, "Began with Ada, brought by the observer, as if they took it elsewhere (one recorded influence)"), its cases by the day they took it and the day they fell ill (an SVG curve, outlined against filled), how its cases took it ("9 in water drawn at Bo's household's well; 4 at home, from those who shed it; 1 brought by the observer"), and every source its cases drank from or its settlement's people suspect, each with the truth (of the households that drew there since it began, as their own records of their draws say, how many had a case and how many cases, against the rest; and what fouled it, from the moves the kernel keeps for 400 days: "Fouled from 1 May of year 2: 120 doses washed from the heap of Bo's household; 30 seeped through the ground from …") beside what people hold ("3 people suspect it, the first since 9 May of year 2") and what the polity did (each law to close it with how it was decided). This is the brief's "cholera outbreak traced to a well" as the kernel recorded it, with whether anyone in the world made the same link shown apart. **The snapshot** carries `incidents_rev` (id 21), which moves when an incident or outbreak opens, moves on or ends, or what people know or a polity did changes, and with each day while a case runs. **Saves 85:** each infection keeps the household it began in (an older save's falls back to where its bearer lives now), so a case of someone since dead still has its home and its household's word. **The observer** replaces the Takings panel with the Incidents panel: a choice of kind (every kind, takings, illness), the totals, the takings' sentence and encounters as before, the outbreaks, and rows with their layers labelled ("What happened", "What people know", "What the polity knows and did"), "(the observer's)" where it started one, "More" for the next page, and "Open" for an incident's or outbreak's page with a way back. **Tested:** the kernel lists every case of an outbreak the observer began that then spread through a fouled well, newest first, all the observer's, paged one at a time to the same list, and none in another settlement's list; a case's page has its six steps in order with the right ones reached and its links; the outbreak's page traces the cases to the well with the moves that fouled it, says nobody suspects it, then that 1 person does once someone comes to; every page reads the same after a save and load; the revision moves on while a case runs; a taking brought before the gathering lists among the takings and its page has seven steps through the decision; the host decodes the three queries and answers them, `NotFound` for what is not there; the web decodes the rows, pages and curves, builds the queries, and words the totals and steps; end to end, the panel shows the case the observer brought with its layers, opens its page and its outbreak's, and the takings and M4b demo views read the new panel. **Found on the way:** the knowledge end-to-end test still expected the 11 founding techniques of before wells, and the founders bring 12 since slice AY (well digging); it now expects 12. The smoke worlds fail now and then: in 14 runs, twice the world `ria_coast` seed 5 ended its month with "1 households have no water", every other world and run passing; the same world lived alone, with and without the save first, showed no dry household in 60 tries, so it turns on something the smoke harness does differently (the world's drawn identity, the full save-load-save before the month, or worlds lived in parallel). It predates this step, whose changes nothing in the world reads. Two candidate causes: a household emptied when its people moved into a new couple's household (the check counts households with nobody in them), or a new household whose share of water ran out before anyone fetched. **Logged for investigation; not yet fixed.** **Not yet:** links from the chronicle to an incident or outbreak (step two), the Water lens (step three), the epidemics row (step four).
- **Chronicle links and the epidemics row, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice BB, steps two and four, ADR-0015 §8, plan §4.7):** no new ADR. **The chronicle names its incident** (wire 1.65: `ChronicleEntry.incident_kind`, `incident` and `at`): an entry telling a taking names that taking, found by its minute and the person who took; an outbreak's beginning names the outbreak that began that day with that person's case first, and its end the one of that settlement that ended that day; a death of disease names the case that ended in it that day; and the observer's bringing a disease names the case it began. These are the same event recorded twice, the entry and the incident, matched by stamp and person; nothing is linked because it came soon after something else (15-02 §1.1), and an entry with no record behind it (an older entry, or one whose record is gone) names none. The entry carries where it happened when its event has a place.
