The observer's chronicle offers "Open" on such an entry, which opens the incident's or outbreak's page in the Incidents panel, and "Locate", which centres the map there. **The epidemics row** (`civ-host dashboard`): each outbreak is judged in the month after it ends, while the moves it reads are kept (400 days), or at the run's end if it still runs. Its households are its settlement's households with people at the time and every household one of its cases began in (so a household it emptied counts); the source is the one most of its water cases took it at; those that drew the disease there from the day it began to its end, by the drawing moves the kernel recorded, are set against the rest, each side as households, those with a case and cases. By households, as Snow's water-company comparison was (research 12-02 §4: about 315 against 37 deaths per 10,000 houses, eight- to ninefold; 05-04 §3.2: a validation of source-linked outbreak geography, not a universal multiplier). An outbreak with 5 cases by water or more and households on both sides is judged; it clusters when the drawers' share with a case is at least twice the rest's (any share, against a rest with none). Green when every judged outbreak clusters, amber when some do, red when none; grey, with its counts, when none can be judged, and grey saying why when nothing brought a disease, which is every dashboard world until imports from off the map exist (ADR-0021 §8; plan §9's M6 design). 5 and 2 are tuning values, the 2 a lenient line under Snow's contrast. The row's text lists each judged outbreak ("Cholera at Ashford, from … to …: 6 of 8 households that drew it at Bo's household's well had a case (75%), 1 of 20 of the rest (5%)"); the JSON report keeps each world's infections, those brought by the observer, ill, dead and taken by water, and every outbreak's split. **Found on the way:** step one's outbreak page counted the households "that drew there since it began" from each household's record of the places it uses, but that record is reckoned forward to today every day (its fading kept current), so every household whose record still held the source counted, up to about two years after its last draw (half-life 180 days, let go below 0.05 days). The page and the row now read the drawing moves instead: "Of 12 households that drew cholera in its water since it began, 7 had a case (9 cases); of 30 that did not, 2 had a case (2 cases)", "No household drew cholera in its water since it began; …" for a source nobody drew the disease from (a spring, or a suspected well that was clean), and "from 3 May of year 2, the earliest still recorded" when it began before the moves kept. A draw too slight to record (under a thousandth of a dose) is not counted as drawing it. **Tested:** the outbreak test draws the disease from the well into one household's store and finds that household with every case but the first against the rest with only the observer's, in the page's words and in the row's split, and no split for an outbreak that is not there; the chronicle links the observer's bringing it to the case and the outbreak's beginning to its page, and every taking's entry to its incident with its place; the row is grey without a disease and with too few water cases or households on one side only, green, amber and red as judged, and words each outbreak; a world lived 75 days at Max after the observer brought cholera counts it and judges its outbreak as the dashboard does; the web decodes the links and places, and end to end the chronicle's entry of the disease brought opens its case's page.
- **Fix: a watcher named after telling of a taking chose about it again (2026-10-11, M4b slice AC, M4c slice AI):** the full suite failed once (`a_watcher_chooses_once_what_to_do_with_a_taking_they_saw`, then 10 of 10 reruns passing): a watcher was found to have looked away from a taking that someone had learnt of from them. Every day the telling pass goes over every taking anyone saw; someone who saw one before the village named them to the watch (a further watcher, M4c slice AI) told those taken from as anyone would, and on the next pass after they were named made the watcher's choice about that same taking, looking away from what they had already told. Now someone who has already told those taken from (a member of that household holds it from them) saw it as anyone would and chooses nothing; a choice already made stands. **Tested:** a witness who told the household taken from, then named to the watch, makes no choice about it in the two days after (it made one before the fix); the crime, faction, regimes and polity tests pass.
- **The Water lens, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice BB, step three; the observer brief §1.3; research 12-07 §1.8, 15-01 §3.1):** no new ADR. **One lens at a time, read per home** (wire 1.66, `GetCoverage {settlement, lens}`, lens 1 water; 0 for every settlement): each household with people, at its home, with two layers, named as 12-07 §1.8 names them. **Could reach:** the walking minutes from the home on the walking grid, on the paths as last surveyed (the kernel's own travel field, so a river without a crossing is the barrier it is), to the nearest water of any kind (an open well with water standing in it now, a spring flowing today, or the edge of a river or lake), and, when that is not one its people may draw at by right (their own well, their polity's, or their kin's households'), to the nearest that is: access is kept apart from permission, as the brief asked, since anyone short of water may draw at any well (ADR-0021 §1). The search tries 2, then 10, then 60 minutes' walk, so most homes cost a small field; a home with nothing within an hour says so and is drawn hollow, never as zero (15-01 §3.1: unknown, not applicable and zero drawn apart). **Did come:** where the household's people drew water on each of the past 30 days, today included, each well and spring apart and the water's edge as one, from their own record: each place a household uses now remembers exactly which of the last 64 days its people worked there (`PlaceUse.recent`, a bit a day, reckoned forward with the record each day; **saves 86**; nothing in the world reads it), with today's draws not yet folded in. An older save's places hold no such days, so the lens begins empty and fills as days are lived. **In words** (the kernel's): each home's two lines ("Could reach: Ada's household's well, less than a minute's walk (another's: its people may draw there only when short of water); by right, the water's edge, 1 minute's walk"; "Did come: in the past 30 days its people drew at the water's edge on 29 days"), and each layer's counts over the homes ("Could reach: of 8 homes, 8 have water within a minute's walk, 0 within 5 minutes, 0 within 15, 0 farther within an hour, 0 none within an hour; for 3 homes, the nearest is another's well"; "Did come: in the past 30 days, of 8 homes, 1 drew at their own well, 0 at a well by right, 0 at another's well, 0 at a spring, 8 at the water's edge"). **The observer:** a lens control on the map (no lens, water: could reach, water: did come); *could reach* draws each home as a disc by fixed bands (within a minute, 5, 15, farther within an hour; hollow for none within the search) with a line to its nearest water; *did come* draws a line from each home to each source drawn at, as strong as its share of the 30 days, coloured by how the home stands to it (its own well, a well by right, another's, a spring, the water's edge), each home by the one drawn at most and hollow where the record holds no draw; the legend names the title, scope ("Every settlement: 8 homes"), the layer's period ("now, on the paths as last surveyed"; "the past 30 days, today included"), the denominator (homes) and the classes, with the counts; pointing at a home puts its two lines in the readout. It is read again when the water changes and each day, and only while a lens is shown. **Not built:** *would come* (dry probes, 12-07 §6.2), which the M6 design left for later; lenses for help at a fire, the watch or a healer (M6b and after); a settlement chooser for the lens (it shows every settlement). **Tested:** the record of days worked keeps exactly the days of the last 64, reckoned on, marked late and let go; in a village with an open well lived three days, every home has water within reach, never nearer by the grid than in a straight line at the fastest walk, a nearest by right only when it differs and never another's well, and a draw on at least one day; the well's household given draws on two days of the last 30 and one long before reads its own well on 2 days and nothing else; on the wire, every home, the periods, scope and counts, and no lens for an unknown number; the host decodes the query and answers it, `BadRequest` for an unknown lens; the web decodes it (a walk outside the search reads as unknown), bands walks on the fixed scale, draws both layers and the legend; end to end, a world lived 40 days shows each layer with its legend, a home's lines under the pointer, and no legend without a lens. **Seen** (that world, seed 3, eight households beside the river): every home within a minute of water; three homes' nearest was a neighbour's well, yet all eight drew at the water's edge, one also at its own well, which is what rights v0 says they should do.
- **The M6a demo, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice BB, step five; plan §7's M6 demo, first part):** no new ADR. **The world** (civ-sim's `cholera_world` example, run by `web/e2e/m6a-demo.spec.ts` with `TCE_DEMO=1`): river valley seed 1 at 768 cells, a band of 100, lived 540 days at Max so households dig wells, then a day at a time to the first day the soil cannot hold 5 mm (at most 120 days more). Then the observer brings cholera to one person: the eldest-listed member of the household whose home's heap lies within reach of (30 m) and no lower than the open well the most other households drew at in the past 30 days. **`NUDGE`s, logged:** whom (the observer's sight of the truth chooses a heap above a shared well; the plague tool targets a person, never a source, ADR-0021 §8) and when (a wet day: slice AZ's outbreaks grew where rain washed an ill person's heap into a well). The first version brought it on the 540th day, 24 August of year 2, at the end of a dry summer: in four worlds it reached 1, 1, 4 and 1 people and none in water; with the wet day, the first world made was kept. Then 90 days are lived and the world is saved; up to six worlds are made, keeping the first whose outbreak had 5 cases by water. Nothing else is set. **What happened** (the recorded run; each run draws its own identity, and the three runs made agreed closely): 18 wells open after 623 days; on 15 November of year 2 (12.2 mm the soil could not hold) the observer brought cholera to Soren, whose home's heap lay 21 m from a well two households drew at. In 90 days 44 people took it, 41 in water, 15 fell ill and 4 died (Bryn, 19; Maren, 21; Freya, 6; Dorran, 9). **It went from heap to well to household to heap**: in this village nearly every household had dug its own well beside its home, and a household's heap lay within washing reach of its neighbours' wells, so Soren's heap fouled three neighbours' wells by 18 November, their sick fouled four more by 13 December, and the outbreak's cases took it in water drawn at seven wells (8, 7, 6, 6, 6, 4 and 4 cases), 2 at home and 1 brought by the observer. Each page names what fouled each well ("Fouled from 18 November of year 2: 359 doses washed from the heap of Yorick's household; 275 … from the heap of Norrin's household; …"). Each well was drawn at by its own household (one or two drew the disease there), so each source's split is thin: at Lark's well 1 of 1 household had a case against 8 of 21 of the rest, which the dashboard's row would call clustered. **What people made of it:** nobody suspected a well. Bryn, then Norrin, came to suspect the spring: "of 16 households they know that draw there, 4 had sickness lately, against 0 of 5 that draw elsewhere"; most households drew there as well as at their own wells, so their tallies pointed at it, and no case drank there. Bryn proposed closing it and nobody came to the gathering (0 of 59: only those who heard a gathering called come, and many were abed or tending, Bryn among the dying); Norrin proposed it again and the gathering closed it, 43 for and 5 against. The outbreak page shows the spring beside the wells with the kernel's truth ("No household drew cholera in its water since it began; of 22 households, 9 had a case") and the polity's two proposals: the trace to the wells is the observer's alone, as plan §7 says to report. The Water lens's *did come* showed 18 homes drawing at their own wells and 4 at the water's edge in the last 30 days, none at the closed spring. **Found on the way, and fixed:** (1) *An outbreak was closed while its wells were fouled.* It ended once no case had run for an incubation's spell, so in one run it ended on 18 January and the cases from 24 January began a second outbreak, not the observer's (40 of 64 cases counted as the observer's in a world where nothing else brings a disease), and the chronicle said "Cholera has left Hazelstead" while its wells held it. An outbreak now also waits until less than a dose of its disease is left with its settlement's households, in their heaps, stored water and wells and their polity's, and on its way through the ground to them (`OUTBREAK_LEFT_DOSES`, a design prior: drunk whole, less than a dose is a hazard under one); rivers carry theirs off by the next day. (2) *A source a law named but nobody now suspected was not on the page:* the page lists the sources its settlement's polity was asked to close since the outbreak began. (3) *"0 known to someone"* for an outbreak the gathering acted on: word of sickness fades as news does, so the illness totals now say "known to someone now". (4) *"0 doses seeped …"* and "1 doses": a load reads "less than a dose", "1 dose" or its doses. **Not established:** whether people would ever pin an outbreak on a well where each household draws at its own: a tally compares households at a source with the rest, and one household per well gives it nothing to compare; a village drawing at shared wells would be the test. **Tested:** the outbreak test ends only when five days have passed and less than a dose is left (it ended later than the five days alone, on the first day both held); a closing law for water nobody drank from puts that water on the page with what the polity did; doses in words; the web's wording of what is known now; end to end, the demo's run above. Slice BB and M6a are complete.
- **M6b design (2026-10-11, plan §7):** from the fire brief and the observer brief (`docs/briefs/m6-fire.md`, `m6-observer.md`), with research 12-03 (urban fire), 11-09 (building codes) and 11-08 (building materials) read in full and the brief's other citations checked where the design rests on them: 07-05 §3.1 (organized stone construction, L3, and sun-dried earthen units, E1, both documented in the early Neolithic) and §3.3 (lime burning, B1, Pre-Pottery Neolithic); 12-03 §2.2 (twenty dwellings 1–2 m apart in 4.2–6.9 m/s of wind, four lit, all involved within about 5 minutes; 36 kW/m² at 1 m falling to 5 kW/m² at 4 m) and §2.5 (1–100 unintended household fires per 1,000 household-years as a log-scale prior, 10 as an order-of-magnitude reference; 0–3 minutes to notice awake, 5–30+ asleep; 5–10 L a vessel); 11-08 §2.5 (char about 0.8 then 0.6 mm/min; a 200 mm member keeps a 128 mm core after an hour, about 26 % of its section modulus); 11-09 §1.7 ("never rebuild the entire city when a law passes"), §1.5 ("a rejected stringent proposal followed by an affordable partial rule is a valuable emergent outcome") and §5.2 (a requirement to achieve a property kept apart from one naming a technique). **One ADR,** [ADR-0022](decisions/0022-fire-floods-and-storms.md) (fire, floods and storms), amending ADR-0012 (dryness and a daily wind, each from its own key so no existing draw changes), ADR-0021 §1 (walking fords on the day's flow, which M6a left on the mean), ADR-0009 (frame grammar version 2, `MassWall`, tile coverings, char as loss) and ADR-0010 (banks and ditches as lines, a ditch's intake beside water, drainage changed openly). **Six slices** (§7): BC (a building burns), BD (fires people start and fight), BE (masonry, brick and tile), BF (floods and storms), BG (banks and ditches), BH (building rules and the M6b demo). **In that order** because: in BC only the observer's fires burn, so lived worlds do not burn before their people can fight a fire (BD brings ignitions and fighting together); a rule needs a technique people know, so masonry comes before rules; and the demo closes the milestone, as M6a's did, with every hazard's issue already in the world. **The fire brief's open questions, answered.** (1) Lightning waits until a source gives a rate. (2) A daily wind is added to the weather, speed and direction, an AR(1) about the land profile's prevailing direction from its own key; the storm day's wind is the storm's. (3) Founders bring rubble walling and mud brick (07-05 §3.1); firing brick and tile and burning lime come by finding, contact or the knowledge tool, so a masonry code is possible from the start and a code for roofs that do not burn needs someone to have found tile. (4) Three templates in M6b: roofs that do not burn within a set distance of another building (a property), walls of named kinds (a technique), a least gap (separation); keeping water and a ladder, no unattended fire and caps on loft loads wait. (5) Compliance is chosen, as for `Curfew`; the watch seeing a noncompliant roof and bringing a case waits for courts (M7). (6) A person may pull down their own household's building, or another's with leave from one of its people who is there; no law grants the power in M6b. (7) Fire gets a dashboard row of its own (ignitions put out at once, escaped fires, buildings lost, conflagrations, deaths, each with the observer's share), apart from structural failures, and floods one too. (8) M6a owns the runoff store (slice AY built it); M6b adds stage and extent. (9) No drowning in M6b: water deeper than wading cannot be walked into; a cause `drowned` waits until someone can be caught. (10) A bank's work is asked in equal shares, as a crossing's; that those who benefit and those who pay differ (12-08 §1.2) is the world's to show. (11) Drains wait with terraces: nothing waterlogs (ADR-0012 §7). (12) People remember a god's fire or flood as any other; statistics leave it out by origin. **The observer brief's remaining questions:** (9) flood water is a kernel raster of depth by day, sparse cells sent when they change; (10) the siege page is M6c's. **Plot guards:** ignitions come only from fires in use and the observer, floods only from routing; no rate, timer or count is read to steer. A village that burns too often is answered through response and spacing (12-03 §5.7's order: ignition and reporting, one building, pairs, task times and water, then settlement losses), never by holding spread below the evidence. If no lived world shows a great fire within a time-boxed week of BH, the demo uses the fire tool, with its where and when logged as `NUDGE`s. Whether it spreads, and whether a rule is proposed and passes, stays the world's. **Left to the slices:** dryness's time constant and equilibrium, the wind's prior, the exposure function's shape and each covering's threshold are tuning values, set and logged as each slice measures them.
- **Wind and dryness, as built (2026-10-11, M6b slice BC, step one; ADR-0022 §2):** no new ADR. **The wind:** each day's mean wind is a vector whose components along and across the land profile's prevailing direction are each an AR(1) anomaly about its mean (research 03-03 §1.4: vector components, with a separate gust), drawn from a key of its own (`[weather stream, wind, day]`), so every rain, temperature, slow-anomaly and storm draw is as it was: a test lives two years under wind of a wholly different kind and finds every other figure of the weather identical. The day keeps its speed, the direction it blows from (degrees clockwise from north, the map's top) and its strongest gust (the speed times `gust_factor`). On the month's storm day the wind is the storm's when its gust, from its load on a roof by q = ρv²/2 (03-07 §2.2 C), is stronger than the day's: the storm's gust over `gust_factor` as the mean, from a direction drawn about the prevailing one (`storm_veer_deg`) from a key of its own. **Dryness:** the water exposed fuel such as thatch holds, as a share of its dry mass (12-03 §1.5: fuel moisture follows recent weather, rather than flipping between wet and dry): each day it drifts toward where a dry day of that day's warmth settles it (25 % at a mean of 0 °C, 8 % at 25 °C, linear between), most of the way within `fuel_days` (3), and takes up 0.05 of its mass a millimetre of rain or snow at once, up to 60 %. (Step two revised these figures to 20 %, a day and 0.015: see "A building burns, as built".) The landscape's climatology keeps its long-run mean, the yardstick of an average day's dryness. **The figures are design priors** (content API 80, the land profile's `[weather]`), flagged as such there: the reports give no valley's wind or thatch's moisture. A prevailing wind from 250° (west-south-west), a mean along it of 2 m/s, a spread of 2.5 m/s in each component and a day-to-day persistence of 0.6 give a mean wind of 3–5 m/s. **Saves 87:** the day's wind, gust and dryness and the two anomalies; a save from before draws today's wind afresh from no anomaly, and its dryness where a dry day of today's warmth settles it, with nothing else of the weather changed. **Wire 1.67:** the clock's day carries the wind, its direction, the gust, the dryness and an average day's, and the kernel's words for them ("a gentle breeze from the west-south-west, gusts to 7 m/s; thatch drier than usual"), shown on the clock after the day's weather. Nothing in the world reads the wind or dryness yet: fires read them from step two on. **Tested:** the wind drawn apart leaves rain and warmth as they were; over twenty years the mean wind comes from within 10° of the prevailing direction, at 3–5 m/s, calm days and gales each rare, its day-to-day correlation 0.6, and every storm day's gusts at least its load's; fuel is never dry on a day of rain, takes it up whenever it was not already soaked, is drier in summer than in winter, and a dry warm spell dries it below the landscape's mean; the words; kept exactly across a save and lived on alike, and drawn afresh from a save that holds none.
- **A building burns, as built (2026-10-11, M6b slice BC, step two; ADR-0022 §4–§6, §13, §14):** no new ADR. **The model** (`civ_agents::fire`, all design priors in the people profile's `[fire]` unless cited): a fire's covering is alight for `involve_minutes` (1; 12-03 §2.2: a dwelling passed 1,000 °C within about a minute), the building is then fully involved for `involved_minutes` (30), then burnt out; its covering is gone within `covering_minutes` (15). A fully involved building puts heat on a surface by the gap between roof edges, falling exponentially through 12-03 §2.2's measured 36 kW/m² at 1 m and 5 kW/m² at 4 m; a covering still only alight puts half. The wind shortens a gap downwind and lengthens it upwind as `gap·exp(−0.1·wind·cos θ)`, the cosine read from centre to centre, so firebrands and leaning flames are one route. Each roofed building within `reach_m` (10) keeps an exposure store that moves toward the summed heat on it within about a minute and cools as fast. Its covering catches by a hazard of one per minute for each multiple of its threshold the store stands above it (12-03 §1.4: accumulated exposure, not distance alone), drawn from a key of building and minute. **Dryness moves the threshold:** a good's `catch_kw_m2` (thatch 10, below wood's piloted ignition at about 12.5) holds at `reference_moisture` (0.12), falls toward drier fuel and rises without bound toward `extinction_moisture` (0.35), above which a covering does not catch at all. The first version scaled from the landscape's mean dryness, and that mean (0.40) stood above extinction: every threshold collapsed to about 1 % of its figure and huts 8 m apart in a calm all caught. A fixed reference keeps a good's figure meaning the same in every climate. **The weather's dryness was revised** with it: step one's figures (25 % on a cold dry day, three days to dry, 0.05 a millimetre of rain) left the thatch above extinction on 56 % of days. Now 20 % on a cold dry day, 8 % on a warm one, most of the way within a day (a thatch's surface is fine fuel), and 0.015 a millimetre: on the core valley a year averages about 0.2, a summer day's middle 0.14, and about one day in twenty is too wet to catch (measured over ten years). **Damage:** the covering's loss follows the minutes burned, failed once gone. Posts, rafters and other timber char from every exposed face while fully involved, `36·(t/60)^0.813` mm (11-08 §2.5: about 0.8 mm/min at first, 0.6 over the hour), counted as loss of their smaller section from both sides; a 200 mm member keeps a 128 mm core after an hour. Half the infill goes when it burns out (the wattle burns, the daub stays). When it is fully involved, the goods its household keeps under that roof burn by their `fire.burns` share (grain and seed grain half, groats 0.8, flour, provisions and dried foods all), each building holding its share of the household's goods by its room as the structural checks reckon it. They are lost from its stores on a new ledger channel, `Lost`. Goods that take no room under a roof (tools, firewood, fresh food, thatch bundles) lie in the open and do not burn here; the content check refuses a `burns` share on such a good. When it burns out, its household's buildings are weighed again against what they carry. **People:** anyone inside who is awake gets out at once and does nothing at home until it is out (`Reason::HomeAfire` in the why-not list). Anyone asleep inside is woken when it becomes fully involved around them, and half of them (`CAUGHT_ASLEEP_DIES`, a design prior standing in until slice BD's noticing: ADR-0022 §6 wakes sleepers after a draw of 5–30 minutes, and §5 has those never woken die) do not get out and die of `Burned`, drawn from a key of person and fire. **Records:** each fire keeps its building, household, settlement, where, when it began and ended, how it was kindled (the observer's influence record, or the neighbour fire it caught from with the gap, the wind, its direction against the gap and the dryness), the conflagration it is part of, the goods it burned and who died. A fire caught from another joins that one's conflagration, begun when the source was burning alone. Each spread also keeps the buildings it weighed, with the most exposure each stood and its threshold, for step three's page. **Stepping:** one `Fire` event a minute while anything burns and none otherwise, so lived worlds are unchanged: nothing but the observer's hand sets a fire until slice BD. **The chronicle** tells the observer's hand ("One recorded influence: the observer set alight the hut of Wren's household"), a lone fire burned out with its losses, and a conflagration's spread and its end with how many buildings it burned. **Saves 88** keep every fire, conflagration, exposure store and weighing exactly; content API 81 adds the `[fire]` section and goods' `[fire]` tables. **Measured** (twenty huts in a block, four lit on the west edge): 1.5 m apart in 5.5 m/s of wind, all twenty within the quarter hour (12-03 §2.2: all involved within about five minutes); 3 m apart, all twenty in wind or a calm, the heat of several neighbours together being enough; 5 m apart in wind, all twenty; 8 m apart in a calm, only the four lit; 3 m apart in wind with thatch at 0.34, only the four lit. Over eight worlds, 44 people were asleep at home when it was set alight at 2 a.m., and 18 of them died. **Tested:** heat by gap and wind, exposure and threshold by dryness, char, stages, gaps between outlines, the block experiment, wider gaps and wetter thatch losing fewer, and half-minute steps converging, in the pure model; in worlds, the block burning within minutes with every fire's cause and conflagration, fewer lost to wider gaps, still air or damp thatch, a hut's stages, damage, goods and chronicle, sleepers getting out or dying and nobody staying in a burning home, and a world saved mid-fire burning on exactly as if never saved. **Not yet:** the observer's tool on the wire and in the web, burning and burnt buildings on the map, fire incidents in the Incidents panel and chronicle links (step three); fires from fires in use, noticing, shouting and fighting (BD); tile and masonry (BE).
- **The observer's view of fire, as built (2026-10-11, M6b slice BC, step three; ADR-0022 §13, §14):** no new ADR. **Wire 1.68**, all additive. A `SetFire` command takes a building; the host answers "The observer set alight the hut of Wren's household" and refuses a building with no roof, one already burning, or one whose covering is gone. Each building on the map carries how it stands to its latest fire: none (or its covering since mended), its roof alight, fully involved, or burnt out. It also carries that fire's number and the kernel's words ("fully involved since 02:15, caught from the hut of Bo's household 1.5 m away, downwind of it in a gentle breeze, its covering holding water 12% of its dry weight"; "burnt out at 02:45 on 3 May of year 2"). The buildings' revision moves each minute while anything burns. **The Incidents panel** gains a fourth kind, a building's fire. Its row begins with the building's name and tells when it burned, what started it and what it took. The layer of what people know says that who saw or heard of a fire is not yet recorded: that is slice BD's, and the layer is never filled from the truth. The polity's layer says no gathering was told of it. Its total counts the fires and the observer's share (a fire of a conflagration the observer started counts as the observer's, as an outbreak's cases do). A fire's page gives its steps ("Caught", "Fully involved" with the goods that burned, "Burnt out"). Its links are typed: caused by the observer's influence, or by the fire it caught from, and part of its conflagration. Its truth tells the char on its timber, its covering and infill lost, the sleepers who did not get out and, for a lone fire, the buildings its heat reached that held, each with the most heat it stood against what its covering needed. **A conflagration** has a row in the list and a page (`GetConflagration`, `ConflagrationInfo`): how it began, the wind and dryness when it first spread as the catch recorded them, its fires in the order they caught, and what held. **The chronicle** links its entries (incident kinds 4 a fire and 5 a conflagration), found from the records rather than by nearness in time. A lone fire burnt out is found by its building's place and minute. A conflagration's spread is found by its first fire's place while it burned, and its end by that place and minute. A death by fire is found by the fire that killed them, and the observer's hand by its place and minute. **In the web**, the Set alight tool arms like the other map tools and Esc cancels it. A roof alight is drawn between thatch and flame, a building fully involved in flame, and one burnt out as charred posts and walls with no roof; the legend names both. The readout appends the fire's words. The Incidents panel offers Fires among its kinds, lists fires that spread, opens a conflagration's page and links a fire's cause and conflagration. A fire's name finds it on the map. **Tested:** in the kernel, a block burning shows each stage on the map, every fire listed as the observer's with its page's three steps and typed links, the conflagration's page with its fires and weather, a lone hut's page with what held, and every fire entry of the chronicle linked; in the host, the tool's answer and refusals, the list and the page; in the web, the decoders for every new table, the drawing and readout of a burning and a burnt hut, and the totals; end to end, the tool sets a hut in a sixty-day village alight from the map, the map draws it burning, the chronicle and the Incidents panel tell of it with its page, and a day on it is drawn burnt out.
- **Fires from the fires people use, as built (2026-10-11, M6b slice BD, step one; ADR-0022 §3):** no new ADR. **Measured first,** as the slice asked: the 3×1,000 bench alone (seed 2, 1,024 cells, a year at full detail) took 1,447.4 s, against slice AY's 1,286.5 s, its slowest day 308 at 18.1 s with 3,164 people; the step adds one pass over the buildings at midnight and a handful of events a day. **Fires in use** (`civ_agents::fire`, design priors in the people profile's `[fire]`): a household's hearth, lit while any of its people is awake within its home's outline and banked otherwise (embers kept), escapes at `hearth_lit_per_hour` (2×10⁻⁶) or `hearth_banked_per_hour` (10⁻⁶), and each of its people there making by a recipe that burns fuel (baking, firing pots) adds `worked_per_hour` (4×10⁻⁶). Each rate holds at the reference dryness and is scaled by `(1 − m/x)/(1 − ref/x)`, the threshold's own terms turned over: more on drier days, none at the moisture of extinction. A household in a home all day and banked all night gives about 15 escapes per 1,000 household-years at the reference and about 10 at the valley's mean dryness (0.2), ADR-0022 §3's anchor. **Keyed by building and day, not by hour:** at midnight each roofed home with people draws a Poisson count of candidate minutes for the day ahead at the most its fires could give (the hearth's greater rate and a worked fire for every member), scaled by the day's dryness, from a key of building and day. At each candidate minute, a draw keyed by building and minute keeps it by the rate of what burns there then, against that bound (thinning), and says which fire it came from. This is the same property the ADR asked of an hourly key (the same day lived at any speed starts the same fires) at one draw per home a day rather than 24, and the candidates sit in the event queue so a save keeps them. The day's dryness is the day just lived (the land lives a day at its midnight), as the catch's threshold reads it. **Most die at once:** anyone awake in or within `beside_m` (3 m) of the building, the nearest then the lowest id, puts it out and only the count records it (12-03 §1.2's first counter). So a lit hearth's or a worked fire's escape is always put out, since someone awake is there by definition. Only a banked hearth's escape, with nobody awake near, grows: its covering catches as any fire's does, and the fire records the escape it was kindled by. **Records:** each escape keeps its building, household, settlement, minute, fire, dryness, who put it out, or the fire it became (saves 89, with candidates pending saved as events; a save 88 loads with none for the day it was saved in). Its fire's words say "caught from its banked hearth, with none of its people awake at home" and its typed link names the household (`caused_by`). **Measured** (three worlds of 120 days with every rate a thousand times, scaled back): per 1,000 household-years, 15.2, 10.0 and 6.8 escapes in all (lit hearths 6.1, 7.9 and 5.1; banked 4.8, 2.1 and 1.7; worked fires 4.3 in the first world and none in the others), of which 3.9, 1.8 and 1.4 caught a covering; the rest were put out at once. It lies inside 12-03 §2.5's prior of 1–100, and the sweep over it waits for the step that lets people fight a fire, since what an escape costs depends on that. **Tested:** the scale by dryness in the pure model; in worlds with homes' rates raised, the same escapes and fires lived in five days at once or in uneven steps, lit hearths always put out, fires kindled by escapes, some put out and some caught; a world saved with escapes pending lives on exactly as if never saved. **Not yet:** fires worked in a workshop rather than a home, noticing by sight, waking and the watch, the shout, and fighting (the next steps); until then a banked hearth's escape burns as the observer's fires do, and a fire caught from it spreads as any.
- **Noticing a fire and the shout, as built (2026-10-11, M6b slice BD, step two; ADR-0022 §3, §6, §7):** no new ADR. **An escape grows before the roof** (12-03 §1.2: an ignition is locally controlled or growing before the building is involved). Step one caught the covering in the minute a banked hearth escaped. Now an escape with nobody awake near grows inside for `grow_minutes` (2 to 15, drawn evenly from a key of building and minute; a design prior, as no source gives the time for an early house). It is stepped a minute at a time with the fires: anyone awake who comes within `beside_m` (3 m) of the building puts it out, as does the first of those asleep inside to wake to it, each waking after their own draw in `wake_minutes` (5 to 30, 12-03 §2.5's figures for the sleeping, keyed by person and escape). Left alone for its minutes it reaches the covering, which catches if it can; the fire begins then. **Noticing:** each minute anything burns, anyone awake within `sight_m` (150 m) of a burning building's outline comes to know of it: inside it if they are within it and not walking, otherwise seeing it. The watch needs nothing of its own: a watcher on rounds is awake and out, and sees what their round passes within sight. Those still asleep inside when it is fully involved are woken by it, and `CAUGHT_ASLEEP_DIES` stays the design prior for how many of them do not get out. **The shout:** whoever comes to know of a fire, or of a conflagration they did not know of, shouts once: those who see it in the minute they see it, those who hear the minute after. Everyone within `earshot_m` (60 m) of a shout who did not know of that conflagration hears, wakes if asleep, and stops what they are doing to decide again, so the alarm travels a hop a minute through a village. Someone carrying a load goes on to set it down where it was going (nothing holds goods on the ground). The observer's hand is noticed in the minute it sets a roof alight, as an escape reaching the roof is. **Knowledge is people's** (§7): each is a record of a person (the fire, when, how: inside, woken, saw, heard; and whether they have shouted), kept per fire for those who were in or saw it, and per conflagration for hearing. Hearing a shout names no building, so someone keeps from home (`Reason::HomeAfire`) only once they were in, woke to or saw their household's building burning; until then they may walk home, and see it on the way. **Records and saves:** an escape keeps the minutes it grows and when it ended (put out, caught or gone out); saves 90 keep these and every record of who knew, a save 89 loading every escape as ended when it happened and nobody's knowledge. Content API 83 adds `grow_minutes`, `wake_minutes`, `sight_m` and `earshot_m`. **The fire's page** now fills its knowledge layer from those records alone: "Seen burning by 11; 14 heard the alarm", who knew first and how ("First to know: Kellan, who saw it burning at 12:00"), who saw its roof catch or that nobody saw it start ("to those who know of it, it was found burning"; its cause is in the truth layer only), and how far the alarm went by when. No wire change. **Measured** (eight worlds with a hut at every home, 120 days, every rate a thousand times and scaled back): 7.1 to 13.9 escapes per 1,000 household-years (mean 9.9); of them 7.6 put out at once, 1.0 put out while they grew and 1.0 catching, in the mean. Of 233 escapes, 158 came from lit hearths, 56 banked and 19 from fires worked at home. The 26 fires were known to 35 people each on average, and 29 people died in them, all of them asleep inside when their hut was fully involved: at night, with nobody awake to see a roof catch, the share `CAUGHT_ASLEEP_DIES` decides most of a hut fire's toll. That figure is high, and 12-03 §4 warns that deaths follow warning and getting out rather than what burns; it is left for the calibration sweep once people can lead their households out. **Tested:** a hut set alight at noon is seen by exactly those awake within sight and heard by exactly those within earshot of them, each stopped and awake, its household kept from home only by those who saw it, the alarm's next hop heard from within earshot, and its page's knowledge; at night, those of a household who woke to their burning hut were the only ones woken by it, and their shout woke neighbours; escapes grow their minutes before catching, some are put out while they grow, the same at any speed with the same records; and a world saved with escapes pending lives on exactly. **Not yet:** choices at a fire (leading out, water, stripping a roof, carrying goods out, pulling down, keeping away), fire seen and told at the hearth and fire caution, the dashboard's fire row and lens, and the calibration sweep.
- **Water carried to a fire, as built (2026-10-11, M6b slice BD, step three; ADR-0022 §6):** no new ADR. **The choice:** a new behaviour, `douse` (content: "Carry water to a fire", PAR 4.5, ages 10 to 70, not daylight-only, exempt from a curfew as the watch is). It is offered only to someone who knows of a fire burning now: a record of theirs of any fire of a conflagration (or lone fire) still burning. Its targets are the roofs the heat of a fire burning now reaches (the exposure stores), up to three, each worth `w_save` (20 points, above a day's hunger) times whose it is (their household's 1, a close kin's household's `kin_share` 0.5, anyone else's `neighbour_share` 0.25; ADR-0022 §6: kin and their own property weigh) times how near its exposure stands to what its covering needs to catch (capped at 1), less the walk at the decision weights' `w_walk_hour`; the best is the option weighed against everything else, so carrying water competes with sleep, food and work as any choice does. **The water** (§6: drawn first on household stores, then the nearest source): their household's store when it holds a load (`carry_water_l`, 15 L), else the source they would fetch from (`water_source`, passing over a source they suspect or a closed one): a well, as much of a load as its column holds, or a load at a spring or bank, counted as a draw there as fetching is. The activity walks to the water, draws (a minute and any lift), walks to the roof and throws it (a minute), then they decide again; its target (`Target::Douse`, saved) names the roof and the source. **On the roof:** `water_stays` (0.5; 12-03 §1.7's η) of each load stays; the rest runs off or misses. Each minute the heat on a wet roof boils its water off first, at 2,257 kJ a litre over the roof's plan area (a wet covering cannot pass the boiling point until it is dry), and only the heat its water could not take reaches its exposure store; water also runs off at `wet_drains_per_minute` (0.03), and roofs are dry again once nothing burns. A roof of 30 m² under 10 kW/m² boils about 8 L a minute, so a carrier's load holds it a minute; it takes several carriers to keep a roof wet. **Not built: dousing a burning roof.** ADR-0022 §6 has water above an authored rate put out a burning covering, but a covering is fully involved within the minute it catches (`involve_minutes` 1, from 12-03 §2.2), before a load can arrive; water thrown on a burning roof is spent. **Records:** each load thrown keeps the fire it was thrown against (the first of its conflagration), the roof, who, when, the litres and where it was drawn; saves 91 keep these, the water standing on roofs and the new target kind; content API 84 adds the activity and `water_stays`, `wet_drains_per_minute`, `w_save`, `kin_share` and `neighbour_share`. **The observer:** a fire's page (or its conflagration's) adds to each roof that held the litres thrown on it, and "Water was carried against it: 16 loads, 240 L, by 9 people, 6 of the loads from their households' stores"; the inspector names the roof someone carries water to. No wire change. **Measured** (unpaired worlds, five seeds each): in a village as founded, homes 6 to 18 m apart, a lone hut fire at noon in wind spread to one neighbour of 40 huts with or without water, and few loads were carried (14 in fifteen fires); in a block of six huts 3 m apart beside the village in a 5.5 m/s wind, all 30 of 30 burned with nobody carrying water, and 20 of 30 with it (122 loads, 1,830 L); 3.5 m apart, 10 of 30 either way; 2.5 m apart in 3 m/s, all 30 either way. Spread can outrun a bucket line (12-03 §4): where roofs crowd, water carried keeps some; where a fire outruns the carriers it keeps none. A first block placed across a river from the village showed carriers walking 300 m around to a ford: water comes where people can walk. **Tested:** a roof holding water catches well after a dry one, or not at all; people carry water to the roofs of a burning block, each load at most a carrier's, against the fire burning then, and fewer huts burn than when nobody cares to (seeds 4 to 6, paired from one save); the conflagration's page tells the water; the same carrying at any speed and across a save. **Found in passing:** two worlds made from one seed diverge within hours because the scheduler's tie-break stream is seeded from the world's random identity (so equal claims are not won by scheduling order); this is by design, and probes that compare worlds now pair them from one save. **Not yet:** stripping a threatened roof, carrying goods out, pulling a building down, fire seen and told and fire caution, the dashboard's fire row and lens, and the calibration sweep.
- **Stripping roofs and carrying goods out, as built (2026-10-11, M6b slice BD, step four; ADR-0022 §5, §6):** no new ADR. **Two new behaviours** (content: "Strip a threatened roof", PAR 5, ages 14 to 65, a five-minute session; "Carry goods out of a fire's way", PAR 4.5, ages 10 to 70), offered from the same facts as carrying water: the roofs the heat of a fire burning now reaches, to someone who knows of one. Both are exempt from a curfew. **Stripping:** allowed on their household's own roof, or another's with leave of one of its people awake within `reach_m` of it (ADR-0022 §6's rule for pulling down, applied to stripping). It is worth `w_save` times whose it is times how far the roof's nearness to catching stands above `strip_cost` (0.5: the covering is lost either way, the rest of the building is not), so only a roof more than half-way to catching is worth stripping. Each minute of work tears `strip_m2_per_minute` (1 m²) of covering from it, as loss on its covering groups; once all is gone the covering has failed and the roof has nothing to catch. Nothing is restored: the household rethatches it as any lost covering. **Carrying goods out** (§5: goods carried out survive): allowed from a threatened roof of their own household's, worth `w_save` times `salvage_share` (0.5) times nearness times how much of a load (`carry_kg`, 20 kg) of goods that burn lies under it. They walk there, take up a load (the goods that burn, most first, less what was already carried out), walk 15 m out of the fire's way and set it down. The goods stay the household's stores; when that roof's fire is fully involved, what was carried out against its conflagration is not under it to burn. **Records:** each stretch stripped (fire, roof, who, when, m²) and each load carried out (fire, building, who, when, good, kg), saved in schema 92; content API 85 adds the activities, `strip_m2_per_minute`, `strip_cost` and `salvage_share`. The fire's page adds "Covering was torn from 2 roofs to save them: 14 m²" and "Goods were carried out of its way: 40 kg, by 2 people". **Measured** (a block of six huts 3 m apart beside the village in a 5.5 m/s wind, five worlds, paired from one save with stripping costing all and goods worth nothing): with water at hand people chose to carry water almost every time, since water costs the household nothing and a strip costs its roof. No roof was stripped, and two loads of goods (40 kg) were carried out; the goods burned were the same either way, the roofs they came from having held. Stripping and salvage are offered and weighed; what makes them chosen (no water near, a roof already doomed) is for the calibration sweep to find. **Tested:** in the paired worlds, nothing is stripped or carried out where they are worth nothing; where they are, any roof stripped is of the block, stripped against the fire burning then, and its covering the poorer; goods carried out are the household's own, a load at most; and between them something was done. The same at any speed and across a save (the carrying test compares every fire record). **Not yet:** pulling a building down, which needs a crew and leave; fire seen and told, fire caution, the dashboard's fire row, the lens and the calibration sweep.
- **Closing a suspected source by law, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice BA, step four, first part, ADR-0021 §7):** no new ADR. **Issues (appended):** `sickness`, when someone of a household of the settlement lay sick at home lately, as its members saw (a member holds the news of their own household's sickness), which brings that household's elder to the review; and `source_suspected`, when someone holds, from their own tally, that a source the polity does not close sickens, which brings them to the review and opens moves to them alone, as `overruled` does. Neither weighs toward anything. **A policy (appended):** `close_source` (`core:policy/works_source_closed`, answering `source_suspected`, bearing security +0.5 and autonomy −0.5, an authoring judgement): one move for each source its sponsor suspects and none in force closes, the source recorded with the law when it is proposed (`Polity.closed`). **Each household's stance is its own forecast in today's units:** a household whose people would draw there, their suspicions aside, and that knows somewhere else to draw, would walk to that other source for every load (its members' litres over a load, at the trip's walk and lift there and back) over the days sickness stays news (30), each hour worth the food an hour of its work brings (research 11-07 §2.3, as for a crossing); against that, its people's own tally of the source, how much likelier a household drawing there was to have sickness lately than one drawing elsewhere (the largest among its members), times what a case costs it: `case_days` (8) and its believed share of a death (`case_death_share`, 0.2) at `w_death` days of work (1,000), each day of work the farm's working hours at that worth. Design priors (content API 78): research 05-03 §3.2 has untreated clinical cholera killing up to about half and prompt rehydration fewer than one in a hundred, neither the share of everyone who takes it. A household that suspects nothing believes nothing avoided, so one that draws there and suspects nothing loses by it, and one that draws elsewhere neither gains nor loses; what people hold dear weighs on top. **Kept by each person's choice, as a curfew is** (research 09-06 §1.5): someone who knows of a closing in force passes the source over while they know another when the custom that a gathering binds, where they stood on it and their regard for its sponsor weigh above nothing; with nowhere else they know, they draw there still. Drawing at a closed source breaks it, knowing of it or not (the law's `broken` and `broken_unaware`, as a curfew's). **The law in words:** "the closing of Odessa's household's well: nobody may draw there, because they hold that the water there sickens", naming the source as its people know it, in the chronicle and the government panel. **Found while measuring, and changed:** a home knew one edge of the water, the nearest; with it suspected or closed, a household knew no other stretch of the river and fell back on its own well or the closed edge. In the probe below, closings of two wells and of the settlement's edge of the water all passed, and the households of both wells kept drawing at them out of need: 875-1,215 knowing breaches each in 90 days. A home now also knows up to three further stretches of the water's edge in reach, each at least 100 m from the nearer ones (both engineering choices), nearest first, and goes to the nearest not passed over; with nothing passed over it draws exactly where it did. Saves 82 (the closed sources; issue codes 10 and 11), content API 78. **Tested:** someone of another household suspecting a well, its own household (which draws there) losing by its closing and the suspecting household neither gaining nor losing; one of the well's own household suspecting it, their household gaining, and the review putting its closing to the gathering in their name with the issue and the words above, told in the chronicle; the closing saved and loaded exactly; passed and the suspicion let go, the sponsor passing the well over and someone of their household who had not heard of it drawing there; a draw there counted as broken by one who knew and by one who did not; a household passing over its suspected sources in turn uses more than one stretch of the water's edge. **Measured (a probe, not kept):** the ten cholera introductions of step two into the same village (106 people, 27 households, 23 wells): the same two spread (37 and 38 infected, 10-11 ill in at least five households; 11 took it at Odessa's household's well). In each, three closings were proposed and passed, 29-35 for and 3-8 against of 48-55 present: Tova's household's well (suspected wrongly, as in step two), Odessa's household's well (where they took it) and the settlement's edge of the water (where nobody took it). With further stretches of the water known, nobody broke any of them. They came late: the introduction was on day 789 and 16 infections on day 800; the closings passed on days 810, 824 and 831, and 14 infections followed between days 826 and 845. 61-66 ms a day for the village. **Not yet:** a closing stands until a founding body repeals it, and nothing proposes ending one once nobody suspects its source; `water_far` and digging a well together (step four, second part).
- **A lid for a suspected well, and moving away from sickness, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice BA, step three, second part, ADR-0021 §4, §7):** no new ADR. **A lid and curb:** at the day's turn a household whose people suspect its own open well, and which owes no relining, owes `cover_h` hours (8: a plank lid over the 1.5 m mouth and a raised ring of earth, a design prior), worked as relining is, by the same chosen work; when done the well is covered and the chronicle says so ("Ada's household made their timber-lined well a lid and curb"). **Runoff:** a covered mouth takes `covered_runoff` (0.1, a design prior; research 03-02 §1.4 lists cover, apron and drainage under a well's construction and §4 that mending a wellhead changes what its users drink while the ground is unchanged; neither gives a share) of the runoff an open one would; every other place below takes the same as before, and what the lid turns away soaks away. Seepage through the ground is unchanged. The well's words say it is being made a lid and curb, or has one. **Reconsidering where to live:** the move weighing (ADR-0018 §5) gains `w_sickness` (3, set as `w_grievance`; research 05-06 §5.1 counts safety among what moves people) for the share of the settlement's households whose sickness its members hold as news, its own among them; it knows of none elsewhere. A death of sickness at home, and the first of a household to suspect the water it draws, put the household to that weighing at once (`review_due`). Saves 81 (a well's lid and the hours owed for it), content API 77. **Tested:** a household suspecting its own well owes the lid, works it and has it, told in the chronicle and the well's words, and is not owed it again; a covered mouth takes exactly the content's share of the runoff the open one took while every other place takes the same; three households' sickness heard of at home raises the worth of every place a household knows by `w_sickness` times their share. **Step three is complete.**
- **Passing over a suspected source, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice BA, step three, first part, ADR-0021 §7):** no new ADR. **Where a household fetches water** (its nearest spring that flows, else the water's edge, or a well it may draw at if nearer with its lift) now leaves out any source one of its people suspects while it knows another: a suspected spring or well is skipped, and a suspected edge of the water leaves any well it may draw at in its place, however far. When every source it knows is suspect, it draws where it would have. With no suspicion it chooses exactly as before. **The chronicle** tells it when the first of a household comes to suspect a source the household draws at ("Ada came to suspect the water their household draws at Wren's household's well: of 9 households they know that draw there, 6 had sickness lately, against 1 of 11 that draw elsewhere"), `ChronicleKind::Suspicion` (appended; saves 80, no new state). **Tested:** a household's own well suspected and passed over for the water's edge, each source it then goes to passed over in turn once suspected, never for one already suspected, and back to the well once every source it knows is suspect; the chronicle's sentence with its counts.
- **Who draws where, and suspicion, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice BA, step two, ADR-0021 §6):** no new ADR. **Who draws where:** each household's record of a source of water (a well, a spring, a cell at the water's edge, as draws were already logged) also holds the other households it saw drawing there the same day, fading at the places' half-life (180 days) and let go when faded or gone. **The tally** (`civ_agents::suspicion`, a pure function): the households someone knows to draw at each source are their own household where it has drawn for `draws_min_days` (2, faded), those it saw drawing there as often, and the household of each person they know at least `known_min` well (a tie's familiarity, 0.3) at that household's usual source; who had sickness lately is the households whose sickness they hold as news. A source is suspect when at least `min_households` (3) draw there, at least `min_sick` (2) of them had sickness, and their share is at least `ratio` (3) times the share of the rest they know, counted with half a sick household in one more so that a source everyone draws at is never suspect (research 12-02 §4: Snow counted houses; his 8.5-fold contrast orients the ratio and is not a target). All design priors (content API 76, `[suspicion]`). **Who tallies:** an adult holding news of a household's sickness or a suspicion, on first hearing of sickness and every `review_days` (7) on their household's day; nobody tallies in a world without sickness, so such a world lives as before. **A suspicion** is held per person with the counts of its latest tally and let go when a tally no longer finds it; the first time it is held its holder says so as a claim (`ClaimKind::Suspicion`, appended) with the source and the counts, told at home and at the hearth as sickness is, for 30 days. Nothing acts on it yet: households' responses are step three's. A source is the place as logged, so cells at the water's edge are told apart and rarely reach the minimum count. Saves 79 (suspicions, a claim's source and counts, the households seen drawing water). **Tested:** the tally (a contrast found; too few, nothing to compare and a household at two sources); the fold of households seen at a source; someone whose known households at a well fell sick suspecting it with the exact counts, saying so at first hand, word of it going round, the suspicion let go when the news is gone, and all of it saving and loading exactly; a world without sickness holding none while its households know who draws beside them. **Measured (a probe, not kept):** ten cholera introductions into the step-two base village (106 people, 27 households, 23 open wells, nearly one a household): eight stayed small (1-7 infected, none ill); two spread to 20-23 infected, 7-8 ill in at least four households, through four wells. In each, one person came to suspect a source: both times Tova's household's well (2 sick of the 3 households they knew to draw there, against 0-1 of 21 elsewhere), where nobody took it; the well 8 took it from was not suspected. With a well for nearly every household, and kin drawing at each other's wells, few households share a source and a shared kin well confounds the contrast: the brief's "nothing to trace" risk, measured and not tuned (any nudge is the demo's, time-boxed). 64-69 ms a day for the village.
- **Sickness seen and told, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice BA, step one, ADR-0021 §6):** no new ADR. **A claim kind** (`ClaimKind::Sickness`, appended): someone of a household lay sick from a day, its subject the household. At each day's turn every household with someone abed (ill today, not merely infected) makes one, unless it made one no more than `sickness_spell_days` ago (14, a design prior), and its members hear it at first hand (the account beginning with themselves); nobody else sees inside a home yet, since no one but its members enters one. **At a death of it** the dead's living parents, children, brothers and sisters, wherever they live, learn of it at first hand too (ADR-0021 §6: "the household and its kin know a death"). **Told as any word is** (ADR-0016 §3): members tell each other at home with `share_home`, and companions at the hearth tell each other with `share_sickness` (0.4, the low end of research 09-16 §2.2's 0.4-0.9 for urgent, personally relevant news), each draw keyed by the household and the day it was first seen, never the claim's number; someone who has heard it is never told it again. It stays news, and counts as lately, for `sickness_days` after it was first seen (30, a design prior), then is let go; while news the observer may whisper it to someone outside the household. Saves 78 (no new state; an older build refuses the new claim kind cleanly), content API 75. Nothing yet acts on it: suspicion is step two's. **Tested:** a claim's pruning and lookup; a household's members seeing their sick at first hand and nobody else, word of it going round from those told, and its letting go after thirty days; a child in another household learning of a parent's death of it on the day. **Measured (a probe, not kept):** three introductions into a village of 100 at one hearth; where two households had someone abed, 99 of 100 people had heard of each within twelve days, 91-94 of them told; nothing changes in a world without an introduction (the draws of gatherings keep their keys). **Smoke:** one run failed `ria_coast` seed 5 with "1 households have no water" and the next two runs of the same build passed: each smoke world takes a random identity, which changes how it lives, and the smoke does not print it, so the dry household cannot be replayed yet. Open: print a failing world's identity and look at the dry household (a household formed that day, one whose water ran out at the instant of the check, or one that cannot reach a source).
- **The observer's view of sickness, as built (2026-10-11, M6a slice AZ, step four, ADR-0021 §5 and §8):** no new ADR. **Wire 1.62:** the welcome lists the content's diseases (`DiseaseInfo`: id, name, and how it passes in words, "by water and between those who share a home"), the menu the observer brings one from; the `Plague` command names a person and a disease by its place in that list and is refused for nobody (`NotFound`), for a disease the content lacks and for someone in whom it runs or whom one lived through still protects (`BadRequest`, in the kernel's words: "Ada cannot take cholera now: ..."); the reply says "Ada has cholera, as if they took it elsewhere", and the influence and the chronicle entry are step one's. **The inspector** gains a person's infections in the kernel's words, latest first and at most five, for the living and the dead: where it stands ("Took cholera today and is not ill", "Ill with cholera since yesterday, severely, day 2 of 4", "Died of cholera 3 days ago", "Had bacillary dysentery 40 days ago, ill 6 days, protected for 120 days more"), how it was taken ("brought by the observer, as if they took it elsewhere", "took it from those who shed it at home", "took it in water drawn at Bo's household's well"), the care given ("tended 14 hours in all, first by Wren yesterday, 6 today, by one who knows a treatment") and the outbreak it is part of ("one of 7 cases so far of the outbreak at Hazelford"; "the only case so far of an outbreak at Hazelford" when alone). This is the kernel's truth, which nobody in the world knows; what people see and suspect is slice BA's. **A well's readout** adds what fouls its water ("Its water holds cholera: about 120 doses, a dose in every 14 L"; nothing when under half a dose), the litres being the water standing in its shaft times its dug area. **The observer's hand** gains *Bring* with the content's diseases and *Bring it*, beside *Tell of*. **Tested:** the host brings cholera to someone once (the reply, then refusals for a second time, for nobody and for disease 999) and its inspector line; the contagion tests check a fouled well's words and that a household that drank from a well is told the well; the web decodes the diseases, the sickness lines and a well's fouled words and builds the command; end to end, the observer brings cholera to an adult of a world lived two days, the inspector tells it and the outbreak, the observer's hand lists it, the chronicle records it, and a second time is refused with the kernel's words. **Slice AZ is complete.** **Not yet:** the Incidents panel and a map of outbreaks (slice BB); what people see of sickness and suspect of a source (slice BA).
- **The save-and-load flake, found (2026-10-08):** a rare failure of the save-and-load continuation tests (about 1 run in 100, first seen in `tests/values.rs` during slice AH) was reproduced by living one world (river valley, seed 3, 512 cells) forty days from 200 fixed identities: two continued differently a day after a load, and only in decision receipts. Traced, one step at a time: the chosen option and every listed total matched, but the chosen option's probability did not; of all the options, breaking new ground scored differently, at another site. A household's candidate new ground is found once a day and kept in a cache the save does not hold. A world lived straight on reused the site found earlier in the day; one loaded found it afresh after a neighbour had marked out a field or plot, so its search saw other land. The cached site is now kept only while what the search reads (the fields, plots and earthworks laid out, and the homes and hearth it keeps clear of) is unchanged. A household therefore also no longer holds to a site that a neighbour's new field has since covered. Afterwards 600 identities (400 of seed 3, 200 of seed 4) continued alike. **Recorded, not changed:** the cache of the building a household would begin (`home_sites`) has the same shape and also reads the household's stores, which change all day; no world showed it, and keying it on its inputs would undo the cache.
- **Revolts, as built (2026-10-08, M4c slice AI step one, ADR-0017 §4):** no new ADR (ADR-0017 §4 decided that a revolt replaces the body through officeholders' own choices and has no roll). **The program:** a faction whose members blame the gathering holds one: of the bodies the content's amendment templates offer that differ from the custom and admit its organizer, the one under which the decisions its members' households were at, under the present custom, would have gone most their way, at each household's stake in each decision (slice AF's test, research 09-02 §3.7; a faction with nothing to gain from any body has no program). Unlike an amendment it may be any body, not only one change away. **Calling** (ADR-0017 §4): at the organizer's monthly review, when neither a petition nor a refusal is called, and when nothing of the faction's own waits or stands, no revolt stands at its settlement and none of its own was called within `petition_days`, its organizer weighs calling on everyone to stand with that body in place of the gathering's. It is worth what a petition is, less `revolt_cost` 0.75 and less what the norms the organizer holds weigh, since the custom itself is what it breaks. **Word** goes from the organizer to its members, then by word of mouth (a fifth claim kind, `revolt`, let go when it ends), and the chronicle records the call. **Sides** (research 04-10 §5.3, 09-11 §2.5: in a crisis people decide daily): each midnight, each adult of the settlement who has heard of it takes a side: with it, with the gathering, or with neither, from their grievance against the gathering, belonging to the faction or else regard for its organizer, the share of those they know who stood with it the day before (for some, more adds less), less what the norms they hold weigh and `w_exclusion` 1.0 for one the new body would leave out (09-11 §1.6); a side needs the points past the gathering's stance margin. **Holding** (09-11 §1.5, §2.2): it holds once the store's keeper and the watch, if any, stand with it and more adults stand with it than with the gathering, for `hold_days` 7 together; then its body decides from now on, a version of the custom *taken* (its `seized_by` names the organizer, no law made it), any amendment in force is superseded, and the chronicle says those who stood with the organizer took the deciding from the gathering, not by its procedure. It comes to nothing when its organizer or faction is gone, or after `revolt_days` 60. Losers keep their wealth, ties and grievances; nothing else changes hands. **The first prior was wrong, as the refusal's was:** with `revolt_cost` 1.0 an organizer all of whose members held the grievance fully, where nobody held the norm, was 0.65 against a threshold of 0.78; at 0.75 (above a refusal's 0.5) it is 0.82. **A finding from the test:** the first test village, with a decision lately gone against the faction, amended its custom by its own procedure (to two-thirds) before the organizer's review, and the old decision then no longer counted, so no revolt was called: the legal route came first, as it should. The test instead gives the village an elders' custom, under which no body one change away would have decided otherwise; there the organizer called a revolt, every one of the 27 who heard of it stood with it, and it held a week later, making a gathering of all the adults, half of whom must come. A second test lets a revolt's time run out: it comes to nothing and the elders' custom stands. Both save and load exactly. **The ten-year smoke passed all 10 worlds** on the first run, with no revolt called: the gathering binds is held about 0.55 on average there, and of the three villages with factions, all petitioned (four petitions, all granted). **Boundary:** saves schema 44 (each custom version's `seized_by`; revolts with their sides in `factions`; 43 still loads), wire 1.43 (each polity's revolts in the Government panel, in kernel words; a version of the custom taken is told so in its history), content API 48 (`revolt_cost`, `revolt_days`, `hold_days`, `w_exclusion`). **Gates:** Gate B and the notables' gate passed. **Not built:** founding after a revolt (the new body deciding which laws and offices stand: step two), a watch of several and coups (step three), and force, damage and violence (step four); an organizer weighing whether others will stand with it before calling (they weigh only their faction's grievance and belonging).
- **M4b design (2026-10-08, plan §7):** from the M4 crime brief, its citations checked against 04-09, 12-04, 09-07 and 09-09. One ADR, [ADR-0015](decisions/0015-incidents-cases-obligations.md): incidents (the kernel's truth), cases (what a polity knows) and beliefs (what people know) are kept and saved apart, and no choice reads an incident; taking is a scored choice behind a moral filter; every sanction is an obligation with a debtor, a beneficiary and a default rule. Four slices, AA to AD (§7). The brief's open questions, answered: **a summary decision by the gathering or an office counts as "no courts"** (plan §7; cases are shaped so that M7 can put a forum between identified and sanctioned). **No corporal punishment or execution** in v0 (settled in the M4a design). **The watch is an office named by a law**, as the storekeeper is: its holders keep watch unpaid, since office pay is not built; a rotating household duty waits for it. **Releasing the store's grain** is relief, built in M4a. **People take only from other households' stores** in v0: not from their own household, standing crops or workshops; whether kin are spared is left to the objection and regard, not a rule. **Sanctions are weighed in days of the household's food**, the scale `Ask` and the levy already use. **A prohibition needs no new good:** a law can close a place or an activity, such as a grove for firewood (AD). The briefs are now kept in the repository (`docs/briefs/`), since the scratch copies were the only ones.
- **Theft and what was seen, as built (2026-10-08, M4b slice AA, ADR-0015 §1–§3, §5, §7):** **Taking** is `Behavior::Take` (appended; `core:activity/take_food`, from 12), weighed only when the household is short, like `Ask`: the food a load would carry against the walk, the person's objection (20 points for a full one), the chance they believe a taker runs of being seen times 10 points (scaled by `exp(−0.3 × risk)` for their risk-taking) and 5 points for full regard for the household's elder. An objection of 0.8 or more rules it out before anything is weighed, with its own exclusion in the receipt (04-09 §5.3). **Objection** is a per-person value, its log-odds drawn as N(2.5, 1.2) for founders (about one in six falls below the filter) and pulled toward the parents' for a child with heritability 0.5, each by a keyed draw of its own so a birth's other draws are unchanged. **The perceived chance of being seen** starts at 0.5 and moves as p̂ ← (1 − α)p̂ + αs: α = 0.3 from one's own attempts (seen or turned back 1, unseen 0) and 0.1 from what one hears (word of a taker 1; a loss found that nobody saw 0). Research 04-09 §5.4 gives no figures for any of this: all are tuning values. **The target** is found as asking finds a giver: the households of the settlement within reach from which a load would carry the most food it wants, the nearest after a walk weighed against regard. **Arrival settles guardianship** (04-09 §1.1, 12-04 §1.4): a member of 10 or more home and awake turns the taker back; so does anyone of 10 or more within 30 m whom the taker notices (0.7 each); a grown sleeper at home wakes with chance 0.25 and the taker flees, seen; otherwise they carry off what they can on a `take` channel, and those about whom they did not notice, and younger children, see them. One who turned back or fled waits 6 to 18 hours (drawn) before weighing it again. **Incidents** (the truth: who, from whom, when, how it ended, what was carried off, who saw) are saved and no choice reads one. **Beliefs** are saved per holder with their source (saw, told, found the loss) and the witness the account began with, so several people repeating one witness are one source. A household finds a taking at the next midnight; a witness tells the household taken from unless they are of the taker's household or regard the taker more than its elder (12-04 §1.2); members share what they know; and at the hearth people tell what they know of takers outside their own household. Beliefs are kept two years. Four tie acts (`took_from_us`, bad provision 3; `took_from_others`, 1; `restored`, good word 1; `refused_restitution`, bad word 2). **A household refuses the asks** of someone it believes took from it, or from a household whose elder a member regards at 0.5 or more. **Responses:** a household that learns who took from it lets it go or demands the food back (a logistic: a point per day of its food taken, less 3 for full regard for the taker); a demand is an obligation due in 30 days, which the taker's household answers once (a logistic: 4 for the share of its settlement's households that believe the taker took, 2 for regard for the household owed, less 0.5 a day of its own food paying costs) and pays from food beyond three days' need each midnight, on a `restitution` channel. It ends met, refused, unpaid when due (the rest an arrear; an award never creates goods) or lapsed. The chronicle tells a taking or an attempt someone saw, and how a demand ended, plainly (06-10 §4). The Takings panel (wire 1.30) shows the latest 60 incidents as what happened beside what people believe and chose, in separate tables joined only by the incident's number. **Deviations from ADR-0015, recorded:** an objection is not yet moved by what the person lives beyond their upbringing (04-09 §1.1's social learning beyond the household waits for M4c's opinion and norms); telling is a rule of ties, not a scored choice, and reporting waits for slice AB, so a household taken from chooses only between letting it go and a demand; and a loss is found at the next midnight rather than at the next use of the store. **Found on the way:** in the first lean-spell probe the taker turned back only for a member at home, so takings made in the evening, with the household at the hearth 20 m off, were "seen" by 33 to 38 people, and the same few people went back to a guarded store dozens of times a day. Research 12-04 §1.4 (an offender may notice a guardian and abandon, or change their timing) and 04-09 §1.1 (capable guardians) gave noticing, the wait and the guardian's age. With a fixed 12-hour wait every retry fell at dawn and in the evening, when households are up, and none of about 170 attempts in 30 days succeeded; the wait is now drawn. **Measured:** in a test's shared shortage (river valley 4 at 512 cells: half the households with nothing, the rest six days' food, every other hungry adult below the filter), one 30-day run saw about 190 attempts by 8 people and at least 4 takings, the rest turned back; takings were seen by neighbours and children; 3 households learnt who took and 2 demanded the food back, unpaid because the takers' households had nothing to spare. The integration test checks the moral filter, that goods are conserved, that every belief naming a taker traces to someone who saw it, that a demand meant to be paid is paid from what can be spared, and an exact save and load. **The ten-year smoke passed all 10 worlds**, twice. On the final build seven had no attempt to take. On the coast, seed 2's village (24 adults) saw 18 attempts by 3 people and 5 takings (82 kg), each seen and known to the household taken from: 5 demands to give it back, 4 met, and 1 ask refused to a taker. Seed 3's 10 attempts by 4 people brought one taking of 3 kg, seen and demanded back; and seed 5's struggling village (11 adults) made 26 attempts by 6 people, none taken. An earlier build's run, with the same rules, had 6, 9 and 17 attempts on three coast worlds and no taking (worlds draw their own identity each run, so runs differ). Gate B passed (20 runs in 1.6 minutes), with no attempt to take in either fixture's third year; takings are reported by run and not graded, since a mean's relative tolerance cannot hold a rare event.
