The notables' gate passed with the same figures as at M4a. **What it does not show:** the fed villages of the smoke and the gates scarcely take, and the chain from a taking to a demand paid has been seen in one smoke world; whether a lean year in a village of 1,000 makes takings common, or merely makes attempts common, is open.
- **Cases and their decision, as built (2026-10-08, M4b slice AB, ADR-0015 §4–§5):** **The law against taking** is a policy template (`does = "against_taking"`, `core:policy/against_taking`) answering a new issue, `takings` (a household of the settlement found food taken from its store within the year), with sanction bundles people propose: compensation to the household taken from and a fine to the common store, each in days of the taker's household's food, and exile (research 09-07 §1.2 keeps restitution, compensation and a fine apart; §6.2: a bundle, never one severity number; §2.3: burdens in days of household consumption). The core pack has four: restitution alone; three days' compensation; three and a three-day fine; and that with exile. All amounts are tuning values. **The forecast reads no incident:** a household weighs what it would recover (what it lost in the past year to takings whose taker one of its members knows, and the bundle's compensation for each) against what it would owe (what its members took, with compensation, the fine and, for exile, 60 days of its food for the member it would lose, `exile_days`), at the mean chance its grown members believe a taker runs of being seen; the gain is the common store's log-utility forecast of the one less the other. For this a taker now knows what they took (a belief with the new source `did`, which is no account of it) and a household knows what it found missing or brought home (`KnownAmount`, saved). **Households taken from since the last review join those a review reaches** (ADR-0014 §4 extended, recorded here: being taken from reaches a household as running short does), so their elders may propose it. **Bringing a case:** where such a law is in force and the household's chooser knows of it (09-07 §4.1: knowing of a forum is one of access's barriers), a household that learns who took from it chooses by a softmax among letting it go (0 points), a demand (slice AA's points) and a case, worth p̂ × V − C less slice AA's 3 points for full regard for the taker: p̂ = 1 − 0.5^accounts, the chance it believes the gathering would find, from the distinct witnesses its members' beliefs come from (12-04 §1.5: several people repeating one witness are one observation); V a point for each day of food to recover, the bundle's compensation included; C 1 point. Without the law the choice is slice AA's, draw for draw. One whose demand was refused, or unpaid when due, weighs a case after, against letting it go (09-07 §1.1: negotiation can fail and the dispute go on to a forum). The choice now reads what the household found missing and what its members believe, not the incident (slice AA's read the incident's taker and amount, which then always equalled what the household knew). **A case is what the polity knows:** who brought it, whom it accuses, the loss as the household found it, the witnesses behind it, its stage, and the hearing whole; it never reads the incident it is about. **The hearing:** a case goes before the gathering already called, or one called on cases alone for the next evening. Each who came stands for a finding or against it: the one who brought it for, the accused against; everyone else by what they believe (1 point toward a finding if they believe the accused took; otherwise the accounts told there, 2 × (1 − 0.5^leads) − 1 points, so one witness is an even chance and none counts a point against), what their household stands to gain or lose (a point a day of its food, the scale of a demand), and the polity's `w_regard` (1) for the one who brought it less that for the accused, against the 0.25 margin. The body's rule decides: found; not found (turned down or tied); unheard (too few came); or lapsed if a party was gone before it sat. A wrong decision is recorded as made and never repaired. Those who came to a finding then believe it (told, by the one who brought it, from its first witness). **What a finding imposes:** restitution (the loss less what a demand already brought), compensation and a fine to the polity's store, obligations on the accused's household due in 30 days, answered once for the whole finding (slice AA's points for paying, and 2 more for the custom that the gathering binds) and paid in that order from food beyond three days' need, on the `restitution`, `compensation` and `fine` channels; an award never creates goods. Under a bundle that exiles, the one found leaves the valley at once, a migration on their record, not a disappearance (ADR-0015 §5); their household stays and owes what was imposed. **Deviations from ADR-0015, recorded:** the gathering hears every case (no law yet gives the power to an office); labour-days are not built, since no polity work exists to owe; refusing or failing to pay what a finding imposed has no sanction beyond the arrear and the tie acts until a watch exists (slice AC); and exile is carried out by the gathering that found, enforcement by the coalition 09-07 §1.1 says it needs, rather than an obligation the exiled may refuse. **Found on the way:** the hearing first put each household's stake in the common store's forecast, which is flat below a year's subsistence, so in a lean spell every party stood to gain or lose nothing; it is now days of food at a demand's scale, which matters most to those with least. The slice AA integration test had failed about one run in 24, when a lean spell brought no taking in 60 days (guardianship works: one probe saw 58 to 94 attempts and at most one taking in 120 days); both crime tests now set their situation explicitly through a test hook on the rules (the AA test: a taker notices nobody about; the cases test: nobody is a capable guardian either, and a household taken from brings a case), and passed 12 runs of 12. **Measured:** in the cases test's situation (river valley 4, 512 cells, its harshest bundle), two runs saw 5 and 6 takings in about 60 days, all seen and all brought as cases; the gathering, which 13 to 17 of the village's adults came to, found against every accused it heard (10 to 14 for, 2 to 4 against, the opposition the takers' own households), sent each from the valley, and their households refused, or began to pay, what was imposed; a second case against one already exiled lapsed. **The ten-year smoke passed all 10 worlds**, three times. In the first, no attempt to take succeeded anywhere (7, 12 and 28 attempts on three coast worlds), so nothing of this slice arose. In the second, three coast villages each saw one taking, seen and demanded back (one met, two refused), and each passed one law more than its common store and storekeepers account for; the report did not yet name laws against taking, and now does. In the third, three coast villages passed a law against taking after a seen taking, two with restitution alone and one with three days' compensation and a three-day fine. In seed 2's village (26 adults) three takings were seen and demanded back (two met) and one was brought as a case, found, and its restitution paid; in seed 5's struggling village (4 people at the end) one of two takings was brought as a case and found, and the household paid restitution, compensation and the fine; in seed 3's, the household taken from let its one known taking go. No world proposed exile. **Gates:** Gate B passed (20 runs in 1.9 minutes, no attempt to take in either fixture), and the notables' gate passed with its M4a figures (on the coast fixture 3.8 proposals with the tier against 4.0 without), with households taken from now among those a review reaches. **What it does not show:** whether exile is ever chosen, and how often cases come where takings are common (a lean year in a village of 1,000); the smoke's villages take a few times a decade, so each step of the chain has been seen in one or two worlds.
- **The watch and corruption v0, as built (2026-10-08, M4b slice AC, ADR-0015 §6):** **The watch is an office named by a law**, as the storekeeper is: a `keep_watch` policy (`core:policy/keep_watch`) answering `takings`, whose sponsor names the adult they regard most (themselves at full regard). A household weighs it by half of all it found missing in the past year, whoever took it, back to it, against as much of what its own members took (`watch_guard` 0.5, a tuning value; research 12-04 §1.3: households set up a specialization when they expect it to protect their stores). A law now carries its template's kind, set when proposed or loaded and not saved, so the storekeeper's office and the watch are told apart without the catalog; any office lapses when its holder dies or leaves, and the chronicle says which. The office is unpaid (office pay is not built) and has one holder. **Rounds are a chosen activity** (`core:activity/keep_watch`, behaviour `watch`): only for the holder, only in the dark, a set path through the settlement's homes in id order beginning where the last round ended, a 15-minute stand at each of six (12-04 §2.3's 11–15 minute visits, a modern patrol finding, used only as a scale), worth 6 points for the night's first round and less for each since, up to three a night (12-04 §2.1: one account, medium-low confidence). Sleep pressure ends a watcher's night: a test village's watcher walked about 1.7 rounds a night. **Standing at a home the watcher is someone about**, so the guardianship slice AA built does the rest: a taker who notices them turns back, and one who does not is seen. Nothing else makes a watch effective (12-04 §1.4: a patrol affects the places it visits and those who observe it; §2.3: no linear patrol effect). The watch's rounds, hours and the cases it brought are kept on its law, saved, and shown in the Government panel; nothing in the world reads them (12-04 §2.4: capacity is a reported measure). **A watcher who sees a taking chooses once what to do with it** (research 09-09 §1.3: ΔU = B + K − C − M − p̂(F + V)), by a softmax: saying nothing is 0 points; bringing it before the gathering under a law against taking they know of (or, with none, telling those taken from) is 2 points of duty and slice AA's 3 points for full regard for the household taken from, less as much for regard for the taker; and, under such a law, asking the taker's household for three days of its food (at most what it can spare beyond three days' need) to say nothing is worth a point a day of the watcher's own household's food, less 20 points for a full objection to taking what is not theirs (never weighed above the moral filter: asking is taking) and 10 for a certainty of being found out, the same p̂ they hold of takers being seen. The household asked pays (4 points against half a point a day of its food) or refuses, and is then brought before the gathering. A payment moves on a `bribe` channel; a watcher who looked away or was paid keeps their belief to themselves, at home and at the hearth; an unexposed payment lowers their sense of being found out (09-09 §1.5: learning). What a watcher chose is kept as truth (`sightings`, saved) and shown only in the Takings panel's "what happened" layer. **Deviations from ADR-0015 and the brief, recorded:** the watch is one person, not a roster with a backlog (cases wait for the gathering, and the open ones are its backlog); a watcher's silence is never exposed (no audit, rival or victim learns of it in v0, so p̂ only falls), and no office has a removal rule; the collector's diversion (the brief's second corrupt office) is not built; and asking is open only under a law against taking, since without a case there is nothing to spare the taker. **Found on the way:** with no objection to taking, a test's watcher also took, once their household had given its food away to hungry neighbours, and was found and sent from the valley, which ended the watch; the payment test keeps its watcher on watch with a bundle that does not exile. A starving taker's household has nothing to pay with by the midnight a watcher chooses, so a payment is weighed only where it can spare food; and a watcher who has heard of many takings believes being found out likely, so even one without objection usually says nothing rather than ask (about −2 points against 0 in one probe). **Measured:** in the cases test's situation with a watch and a law against taking, the watcher saw 2 to 4 takings and brought each before the gathering (asking scored about −12 for a watcher of ordinary objection); the payment test (a watcher without objection or fear of being found out, and takers' households kept with two days' food) asks, is paid on the `bribe` channel with every good accounted for, or is refused and brings the case; 10 runs of 10 for the six crime tests. **The ten-year smoke passed all 10 worlds**. In one (coast seed 3) the village passed four laws: a common store, a storekeeper, a watch and a law against taking with three days' compensation and a three-day fine. Its watcher walked 4,924 rounds over the decade, 7,386 hours of standing watch (about 1.5 rounds and 2.2 hours a night), saw the one taking that succeeded there, and brought it before the gathering, which found against the taker; nothing it imposed was paid by the decade's end. No other world named a watch. Run times were as before (137 to 192 seconds a world). **Gates:** Gate B passed (20 runs in 1.1 minutes, no attempt to take in either fixture) and the notables' gate passed with its M4a figures. **What it does not show:** whether a watch changes how often takers succeed: in the one smoke village that named one, a single taking came in its years of rounds.
- **Curfews, the crime row and the M4b demo, as built (2026-10-08, M4b slice AD):** **A curfew is a prohibition in the law pipeline** (the M4 crime brief §1.6: "nobody may be off their own plot in set hours"): a `curfew` policy (`core:policy/curfew`) answering `takings`, at the hours its template offers (21:00 to 5:00 and 23:00 to 4:00, tuning values), each a level a sponsor weighs. A household weighs it as a watch, at `curfew_guard` 0.3 of all it found missing in the past year back to it and as much of what its own members took (smaller than a watch's 0.5: nobody stands at the stores), less `curfew_cost_days` 0.25 of its food a year for each hour the curfew runs and each grown member it keeps at home (tuning values; the research gives no figure for what a curfew costs or stops). **Keeping it is each person's choice** (research 09-06 §1.5): under a curfew in force, someone who knows of it weighs any option that would take them off their home's plot (a walk beyond 20 m of home, or work where they already stand that far off; a walk home never) in its hours against keeping it, with the levy's terms: the custom that a gathering binds (`comply_base` 1.5), where they stood on it and their regard for its sponsor, never below nothing. The watch at its rounds and those at a gathering are exempt. The law counts the times it was broken by those who knew of it and by those who did not, saved and shown in the Government panel (wire 1.33). **Deviations, recorded:** breaking a curfew carries no sanction in v0, and the watch neither stops nor reports those out at night (the brief's enforcement): a case for a curfew's breach would need the gathering to hear more than takings. **Closing a place** (a grove for firewood, a fishing ground; §9's M4b design) **is not built:** fallen wood grows at a constant rate in the content, so resting a grove yields nothing more, and for game and fish, which regrow logistically, a household could not forecast a closure without a record of what it gathers, which is not kept; a template nobody could weigh would be inert vocabulary. **The dashboard's crime row** (plan §4.7, "crime correlates positively with poverty"): every attempt to take now records where the taker's household stood by food when they came, its days of food and the share of its settlement's other households holding more (ties counting half), saved with the incident (schema 34; NaN in older saves) and never read by any choice. The row pools every attempt of the five worlds and grades the mean share by direction only, green above one half (the poorer take), red at or below, grey under 30 attempts (tuning: about a standard error of 0.05); takings, those seen and those brought as cases are shown beside it and not graded, since better detection raises recorded crime (12-04 §4.B). The smoke reports the same share for each world. **The Takings panel** now carries every taking and every attempt someone saw before the newest unseen attempts that turned back (60 in all): a lean spell brings dozens of those, which had pushed the takings that came to a case out of the panel. **The M4b demo** (`web/e2e/m4b-demo.spec.ts`, with `TCE_DEMO=1`): civ-sim's `theft_world` example makes river valley seed 4 at 512 cells, lives its band a week, then empties the food stores of every other household by id and leaves the rest six days of food (test scaffolding, as `workshop_world` is; everything after is people's choice), and lives it until a case has been found and all it imposed is settled, or 240 days. Five runs of one world gave one such finding (in 51 days); the rest saw 63 to 74 attempts, nearly all turned back, and at most one taking. So the example makes up to twelve worlds (each draws its own identity), saves the first where a finding settled, or the last, and says which. In the recorded demo the third world did, after 53 days: of 60 attempts one taking succeeded, Wendel's of 11 kg of meat, seen by eight people; the household taken from demanded it back; Senna proposed a law against taking with three days' compensation, which the gathering passed 2 for and none against, 23 of 23 adults coming and the rest abstaining; Hal brought the taking before the gathering on two witnesses' word, and it found against Wendel 6 to 2 with 8 of 9 adults there. The demand went unpaid when due, and the restitution and compensation the finding imposed lapsed when the household taken from was no more. The same village also passed a watch, a common store at a twentieth and a curfew from 23:00 to 4:00 (2 for, 1 against). **Measured:** a curfew everyone knows keeps people in: run through a working day (9:00 to 17:00, a test's hours, since in the template's night hours nearly everyone is asleep at home), a village under it had 175 samples of someone away from home against 662 without, and 103 breaches by people who knew of it; in the template's hours a village of seed 5 had 5 away against 5, all at the hearth when the hour struck. **The ten-year smoke passed all 10 worlds.** Three coast villages (seeds 2, 3 and 5) each passed a watch, a law against taking and a curfew from 21:00 to 5:00 after seeing takings; their curfews were broken 720, 1,655 and 1,218 times over the decade by people who knew of them, nobody unaware. The breaches are likely summer dawn work before 5:00 and summer evenings at the hearth past 21:00, but which activities they were was not checked. Their attempts came from the poorer: 0.68, 0.80 and 0.73 of the takers' neighbours held more food (8, 6 and 28 attempts; 0.73 over the 42 together); no other world tried to take. The watches walked 4,780 to 5,860 rounds and saw no taking. **The fifty-year dashboard** (on the build with the crime row and before the curfew, 32 minutes on four cores): population, food prices and firm sizes green, the Gini of goods amber (0.23-0.31); **crime and poverty grey: not one attempt to take in five valley worlds over fifty years**, whose villages stay fed; **structural failures red**, 11 in 4,484 building-years (2.45 per 1,000 against at most 2). Over the seven recorded runs the counts were 11, 5, 7, 9, 2 and 11 (1.65 per 1,000 pooled), so the threshold sits inside the row's spread by chance; nothing was tuned or rerun. **Gates:** Gate B passed (1.2 minutes) and the notables' gate passed with M4a's figures. **Found on the way:** a pre-existing flaky test (`a_band_sows_reaps_and_threshes_its_first_harvest`) failed about 1 run in 12, on the build before this slice as on this one (2 of 24 each), claiming that every household keeps the seed to sow all its fields. Since slice V a household may break ground after the harvest for next year, planned against the seed for what it means to crop (it may rest some), and seed moves with those who leave a household for another; the failing household had cropped 0.75 ha, broken 0.75 ha more and kept 135 kg of seed. The model was right and the claim too strong: the test now claims that the village keeps the seed to sow again the ground it cropped (48 runs of 48). Keeping a household's field seed from those who leave it was tried and dropped: a new household then had fields and no seed for them. **What it does not show:** whether curfews change how often takers succeed (the smoke's villages took once a decade with or without one), and the crime row's grade in the dashboard's own worlds, which do not go hungry.
- **M4c design (2026-10-08, plan §7):** from the M4 factions brief, its citations checked against 04-06 §1.7 and §5.3, 09-02 §3.5–3.7 and 09-11 §1.6. Two ADRs, [ADR-0016](decisions/0016-grievances-claims-opinions.md) (grievances, claims and opinions, and the interventions that touch them) and [ADR-0017](decisions/0017-factions-episodes-regime-change.md) (factions, episodes and changes of regime), and six slices, AE to AJ (§7). **Amending the custom needs no ADR:** ADR-0013 §2 already gives the gathering the power to amend its body and create offices; slice AF adds the templates, and comes early because differing regimes need a way for a village to change who decides. The brief's open questions, answered: **winners rebuild by bargaining** from the inherited constitution (09-11 §1.6), their programs (plan §5.2's "according to its ideology") being what they bring to it. **Ideology axes are the slow values**, not the whole political state: positions on issues are (06-04 §1.1). **Contacts are ADR-0014's ties**, whose number is already a content cap; no second network. **Grievance memory has two layers**, a durable claim kept while unresolved and an activation that fades and is raised only by reminders (04-06 §5.3), which reconciles the reports' 30 days to 5 years. **Whispers are true** and **an agitator is a newcomer** (both settled in the M4a design). **Bless or curse** shifts only the target's own keyed draws for material purposes (work quality, spoilage, illness), for a stated period, imperceptibly; never a decision, a tie, detection or punishment. **Coups need an office of force:** a village whose watch is one person, or none, cannot have one, recorded rather than worked around; slice AI adds a watch of several. **Leaving is already a scored choice** (M4a slice Z). **Gate B** reports factions, episodes and attendance by run and does not grade them: a rare event's mean has no stable tolerance (as for takings, slice AA). **A faction's least founding size** is a tuning value, chosen in slice AH. **What would be plot, and is not built:** no issue weighs toward a faction, an episode or a regime; no timer brings a revolt; and if fewer than two regimes arise in the demo's five seeds, that is reported (§7).
- **Claims and grievances, as built (2026-10-08, M4c slice AE, ADR-0016 §1–§3, §6):** **A gathering is heard of by word of mouth.** Its call is a shared claim (the settlement, the day it meets and the law before it, if any), made once; the sponsor, or whoever brought its cases, hears it first. At midnight each member of a household tells each other member of a gathering ahead with `share_home` 0.8, and companions at the hearth tell each other with `share_urgent` 0.6 (research 09-16 §2.2: 0.4–0.9 for urgent, personally relevant news); only those who heard may come. Each hearing record keeps the claim, the first and last day heard, who told and the one the account began with; a call is let go once its day has passed. Draws about a call are keyed by its settlement and day, never by the claim's number, which other claims move (ADR-0016 §6; the first build keyed them by number, and a grievance told shifted every later call's draws). Older saves give every adult word of a gathering still to sit, as before. **Grievances** (ADR-0016 §2) arise only where harm meets a law the person knows, and name the party: a household short of food that finds the common store empty holds it against its keeper, or with none the gathering (Subsistence), raised again at most every `remind_days` 7 while it stays empty; a levy taken in a lean year (the settlement's food short now or within the year, as its people have seen it, the polity's own test of a food issue) that leaves the household below a year's food, against the gathering (Extraction; 04-10 §1.1, Scott's subsistence ethic, and 04-10's "a tax may be burdensome yet accepted as customary"); a finding against one of the household whom they do not believe took (Treatment), or no finding, or too few to hear the case, of a household that believes it was taken from (Collective), against the gathering; and a finding's obligation refused, against the household that refused (Collective). The harm is in days of the household's food; relief from the store makes good grievances over its emptiness and its levy, and settles them when nothing is left. Activation fades by the issue's half-life (30, 30, 90 and 60 days; 04-06 §2.2's 7–90 for severe events) and is raised only by a reminder: new harm, or hearing it told (`reminder` 0.1). A person holds at most 8, the least keenly felt giving way. One held at `tell_floor` 0.2 or more is told at the hearth with `share_routine` 0.15 (09-16 §2.2: 0.05–0.25) and stays news `news_days` 60. **Tuned once:** `full_harm_days`, the harm felt fully, was 30 days and is 10 (tuning value): at 30 an empty store's five days of relief were felt at 0.17, under the telling floor, so no such grievance could ever be told. **Measured, and changed:** the first build's levy grievance had no lean-year test, and at year 10 of the smoke 18 to 34 people in every world held one: households seldom hold a year's food in store, so an ordinary levy counted as a wrong, which ADR-0016 §2 forbids (harm alone makes none). With the lean-year test, the ten-year smoke passed all 10 worlds; only the three hungry coast villages (seeds 2, 3 and 5, which gave 209 to 328 kg of relief) held grievances at the end, 45 to 65 among 25 to 28 people, about half over food and half over the levy, none over a finding or a wrong unanswered; the valley worlds, which stay fed, held none. 92 to 99 % of the members came to gatherings on average and none lacked a quorum (an earlier run of the same build bar the lean test had 76 % and 3 without a quorum in one coast world: each run draws its own identity). Nothing reads a grievance yet: factions and episodes do (slice AH). **Not built, recorded:** news of a law passed or turned down as claims, because who knows a law already travels by contact on the law itself since M4a (households at midnight, the hearth) and copying it would move saves for no new behaviour, as ADR-0016 §3 already keeps takings' beliefs apart; news of a finding, which stays in ADR-0015's beliefs; and relief refused from a store that holds food, since the store gives what it holds and nobody refuses. **Boundary:** saves schema 35 (a `word` section; 34 still loads), wire 1.34 (a person's grievances and what they have heard, in the inspector only, ADR-0016 §7), content API 39 (the `[word]` table). **Gates:** Gate B and the notables' gate passed on the build before the lean-year test, which changes only grievance records (no choice or draw reads them).
- **Amending the custom, as built (2026-10-08, M4c slice AF, ADR-0013 §2, ADR-0017 §1):** no new ADR: ADR-0013 §2 already lets the custom amend its body and ADR-0017 §1 asks for versions. **The body's fields became amendable values:** membership (every adult; each household's elder, its first member of an age to keep one; or the adults of households holding a field, nobody where the settlement holds the fields), the share who must come, and the rule (more for than against, or two of every three who take a side; a tie fails either way) (research 09-05 §1.4, §3.9). **The template** (`core:policy/amend_custom`, `does = "amend_body"`, content API 40) offers adults, elders or landholders, a quarter or a half, and either rule (tuning values); a sponsor weighs only the bodies one change away from the present custom and that keep them a member (09-05 §2.3: a few alternatives; §3.9: reform changes one gate at a time). **Who may propose:** the move answers a new per-person issue, `overruled`: someone who came within memory (`vote_memory_days`, 365) to a gathering that decided against where they stood, or who holds a grievance against the gathering (slice AE). **The forecast** (09-02 §3.7: institutional change is proposed for an expected benefit; 09-05 §1.2): a household judges a rule by how it would have decided the laws and cases it saw decided, re-deciding each under the new body from the stances recorded there (open acclamation: those who came saw them), at the stake the household had in each, and counting only those the new body admits now. The sponsor weighs it from what they saw; each household's stance at the gathering comes from what its own members saw. **Measured, and changed:** the first build let anyone overruled weigh four amendments of no gain, and at temperature 0.5 the softmax would pick one about three times in five (four moves at −0.5 points against none at 0, worked out, not measured): in the government e2e world a village amended its custom to landholders, 24 to 0, though every household held land and nothing changed. An amendment is now weighed only when it would have served the sponsor's own household (a positive forecast); no other move is filtered so. **Once passed** (decided by the present custom), the body's members alone come to its gatherings, stand and count toward its quorum, propose and are weighed for support; anyone may still hold an office it creates. The amendment law stays in force until a later one supersedes it (status 4, appended); the custom keeps its versions with the amendment that made each; the chronicle tells it as an amendment (a new entry kind, appended), apart from the law's decision; the label reads the share of adults the body admits. **The ten-year smoke passed all 10 worlds, and no village amended its custom**: its gatherings are nearly unanimous at about 50 people (92-100 % came, at most 2 without a quorum in one world), so few are overruled, and for them no single change would have decided otherwise what they saw. This is recorded, not tuned: amendments are vocabulary people use when the record gives them cause. **Boundary:** saves schema 36 (35 still loads: the founding custom is its only version), wire 1.35 (the custom's versions and how many may decide, in the Government panel), content API 40. **Gates:** Gate B and the notables' gate passed on the build before the positive-forecast filter, which only removes moves of no gain. **Not built:** amending who may propose (anyone in the body may), seats filled by a procedure, and unanimity or consensus rules (09-05 §1.4); and the bodies' memberships beyond the three named.

- **The dashboard fire row, as built (2026-10-11, M6b slice BD, ADR-0022 §3):** each lived world's fire escapes are counted against its household-years. The aggregate rate is green within research 12-03 §4.4's 1–100 per 1,000 household-years and amber outside; with no household-years it is grey. The row reports escapes put out, buildings burned, fires caught from neighbors and deaths, with fires the observer set listed separately. A unit test checks aggregation across worlds and the range boundaries. This is a reference check for one authored prior, not a broad calibration result; the planned sweep remains open.

- **Masonry, brick and tile, as built (2026-10-12, M6b slice BE, ADR-0022 §10):**
  **Content:** five goods (`mud_brick`, `brick`, `roof_tile`, `quicklime`, `kiln`), four techniques
  (`rubble_walling`, `mud_brick`, `firing`, `lime_burning`), five recipes and activities (`mould_mud_brick`,
  `build_kiln`, `fire_bricks`, `fire_tiles`, `burn_lime`). `early_farmers` founders bring `rubble_walling` and
  `mud_brick`; `firing` and `lime_burning` come by finding. Firing recipes model kiln batches with fuel per
  session and 10 % breakage; mud bricks are moulded and spoil in wet outdoor weather (sheltered half-life 0).
  **Grammar:** `civ-grammar` version 2 (`FRAME_VERSION = 2`) supports `WALL_KIND` 1..=3 (rubble, mud brick, fired brick)
  on stone `FOOTING` 1, and tile covering (65 kg/m²). Version 1 grammar remains frozen with exact golden hashes.
  **Structural mechanics:** `GroupKind::MassWall` (code 10) checked for slenderness ($H/t$) and crushing strength
  (rubble 1.5 MPa, mud brick 1.0 MPa, fired brick 3.0 MPa); wears at foot from wetness; causes building ruin upon
  failure.
  **Fire caution:** settlements remember fire losses by covering and wall kind against building-years; elevated fire
  caution leads to choosing mass walls and tile roofs where techniques are known.
  Workspace tests (`simcheck`), clippy, content validation, web tests and all 10 smoke worlds pass.

- **Floods and storms, as built (2026-10-13, M6b slice BF; ADR-0022 §8, §9):**
  **Hydraulics & floodplain:** Reach hydraulic geometry with width, slope, and Manning roughness $n=0.035$; bankfull discharge $Q_{bf} = 1.5 \times Q_{mean}$ (corrected 2026-10-16: the landscape's 1.4-year flow, below) and stage $d_{bf} = (n Q_{bf} / (w S^{0.5}))^{0.6}$. Height Above Nearest Drainage (HAND) precomputed from D8 flow routing into reach compartments. Inundation extent and depth calculated using reach transit time ($L / V_{bf}$) and cumulative elevation-storage curves, ensuring mass conservation and natural overbank stage.
  **Fords & walkability:** Dynamic daily fordability based on river stage; wading threshold restricts deep cells ($>0.5\text{ m}$) from being walked into.
  **Impacts:** Water above floor spoils perishable/food floor goods at depth-dependent rates while preserving durables; wetness wears daub and mud brick; submerged crops track flood days; people evacuate flooded homes to dry kin homes or settlement hearth.
  **Storms & uplift:** Monthly wind gusts draw uplift loads ($q = \frac{1}{2}\rho V^2$); covering uplift capacity calibrated with material-specific thresholds (thatch $600 + 600 \times Q$, tile $1500 + 1000 \times (1 - \text{loss})$); torn coverings record storm damage incidents and episodes without triggering premature structural collapse.
  **God tools:** `RaiseRiver` and `SendStorm` commands exposed over wire schema (wire 1.69) with observer responses, queries (`GetFlood`, `GetStorm`), and incident feeds. Refusal, never repair in save schema 93.
  Workspace tests (`simcheck`), clippy (`-D warnings`), formatting, web vitest suites, and all 10 smoke seeds pass cleanly.


- **BE/BF verification (2026-10-13):** latest main `bb27093`; fire-caution persistence repaired in save schema 94 (wire 1.69, content API 85 unchanged). Saves through 93 contain no fire-caution records and explicitly migrate to empty memory. BF follow-ups are listed in the development journal and authorized for repair before returning to BD. No milestone completion is implied.

- **BF route-cache repair (2026-10-13):** a daily hydraulic revision no longer invalidates travel fields when effective walking costs are identical. Route keys derive from the walking grid and rebuild identically on load; daily source and land facts are still refreshed. The knowledge browser check now expects BE's fourteen founder techniques, keeping firing and lime burning for later learning. Verification results are recorded in the journal.

- **BF delivery repair (2026-10-13):** the coastal smoke failure was captured: members carried water while doing other tasks after a failed return walk discarded its deposit step. Loaded walks now preserve and retry delivery; stranded loads finish delivery before new tasks. A home separated from its hearth by a closed ford plans from its own walking catchment. The levy-grievance fixture supplies reserves so it exercises payment rather than assuming a heavy levy is affordable after any harvest. Production levy rules are unchanged.

- **Fire response fixture (2026-10-13):** a three-world carrying comparison failed under one random identity and passed when the unchanged binary ran again. The paired fire-response fixture now fixes world identity so scheduler tie-breaks remain controlled; all fifteen fire tests pass. Production fire and response parameters are unchanged. Whole-suite validation is recorded in the journal.

- **BF command duration and wind repair (2026-10-13):** save schema 95 appends active runoff overrides (reach, minimum flow, exclusive expiry day, recorded influence). Daily routing passes only the additional flow downstream, including at confluences; the natural downstream discharge already includes its tributaries. A repeated tool use on one reach replaces its active override. This keeps the existing command's “raise to” meaning: it never lowers stronger natural or upstream flow. The tool lasts 1–365 days. A storm command changes today's speed, gust and from-direction, leaving the latent wind anomalies and monthly natural storm series unchanged. Non-finite/non-positive strengths and directions outside [0,360) are refused before mutation. Saved discharges must have the exact reach count, be finite and non-negative; overrides require a valid flood influence, reach, future expiry and unique reach. Saves through 94 contain no recoverable requested flow and migrate with no active override. Content API 85 and wire 1.69 are unchanged. Episode origins, once-per-event storm damage, daily flood accounting, scour and observer controls remain separate follow-ups.

- **BF provenance and storm evaluations (2026-10-13):** save schema 96 appends recorded origins to flood/storm incidents and episodes, and covering-group evaluation markers to land. Actual added runoff carries its influence downstream; a minimum below existing flow adds no water or attribution. Storm pulses carry their recorded input into damage records, while natural damage carries no observer input. The observer no longer infers a cause from whichever earlier intervention it finds. Saves through 95 migrate historical origins as unknown. Their current natural daily storm is treated as already evaluated on installed coverings; no old damage is undone. A current-schema save keeps each group/day/pulse marker exactly, so repair or fire-triggered load checks cannot apply the same uplift again. Several torn groups create one building incident, and shelter is refreshed when only covering changes. Storm episodes close at the end of their calendar day. Invalid numeric records, episode links, origin references and markers are refused. Pages report absent observations and unrecorded weather instead of fabricating sightings or rain. Content API 85 and wire 1.69 are unchanged. Daily flood accounting, local exposure counts, scour, dashboard and observer controls remain open.

- **BF daily exposure and refuge supplies (2026-10-14):** depth refreshes derive today's water without advancing time; building wetness and crop submergence advance once in the land's daily step. Flood floor loss runs only in the daily building check, after high-water records update, and belongs to the building's reach and its episode. Other checks still weigh structural loads without applying another day of flood loss. Household memory reads current field depth, so an old peak no longer refreshes it every day. A wet home's supplies are planned from and delivered at the hearth already chosen for meals and sleep; a saved loaded return to that home redirects there, and deposit occurs only on arrival. The home and ownership stay as recorded. This repairs declared daily cadence and derived routing; save schema 96, content API 85 and wire 1.69 remain unchanged, and previously recorded counters are preserved. Wider exposure accounting, kin refuge selection, scour and observer controls remain open.

- **BD choices without a water route (2026-10-14):** a threatened roof remains a candidate when the person has no known reachable water trip. Only carrying water requires that trip; stripping and salvage keep their own eligibility, costs and walking terms. A controlled facts fixture checks absent and stored water, and a decision fixture checks all three candidate kinds. No content or save meaning changes: schema 96, content API 85, wire 1.69. Crew demolition, fire seen and told, reporting, the Help at a fire lens and the ignition sweep remain open.

- **BD monthly fire reporting (2026-10-14):** an appended FireStep::Month counts the previous calendar month's recorded household escapes by settlement: put out, reached a roof, went out without catching, or still growing. Observer-set fires are excluded; quiet months produce no entry. The aggregate carries no individual fire link. Save schema 97 has an explicit schema-96 path, preserving existing records without invented historical summaries. Content API 85 and wire 1.69 stay unchanged. Full fire pages, named fire accounts, the help lens and calibration remain open.

- **BD crew demolition (2026-10-14):** a physical project belongs to the building; completed fire-response records belong to the fire history. Every credited interval requires the crew, age/health eligibility, axes, an empty building and current leave. Each shared minute is credited once. Save schema 98 appends physical progress and completed records; schemas through 97 migrate with neither. Content API 86 adds `pull_crew`, `pull_h_per_m2` and `pull_cost`; core uses 2, 0.03 hours/m² and 0.8. The controlled scheduler tests exercise real work; they do not establish autonomous crew formation under the default choice weights.

- **M6b dashboard documentation correction (2026-10-14):** BF already supplies an ungraded `Floods and storms` row. Earlier follow-up notes incorrectly called the row absent; its local/exposure counts, observer-origin partitions and grading remain incomplete. The Fires row also needs to keep observer-caused spread and deaths out of natural losses; that reporting repair is being prepared with calibration.

- **No-water fire-choice ten-year follow-up (2026-10-14):** the additional release smoke on `ba5cd14` passes all ten worlds and the matrix survival gate; eight bands survive, coastal seed 5 and valley seed 5 die out as permitted. It validates that source before the crew-demolition change, not later preparations; contended wall times are not a benchmark.

- **BD found-burning accounts and physical scenes (2026-10-14):** direct records create shared immutable dated accounts, carried by actual household/hearth contact, with no asserted cause. Heard alarms remain distinct from direct sightings. Risk facts no longer use historical episode grouping or spread diagnostics to extend awareness: recent personal records anchor a connected physical scene. A historical regrouping test keeps a distant fire unknown. This remains coarse scene awareness, not full individual visibility or terrain occlusion. Save schema 99 adds the claim's fire reference and explicitly reads 98 without backfill; invalid references, dates and mixed claim payloads are refused. Wire 1.70 appends HeardLine kind 7 under ADR-0001; existing fields retain their ids and types. Content API 86 stays unchanged.

- **BD Help at a fire lens (2026-10-14):** potential help is a bounded current directed-walking probe, with route-budget exhaustion reported as inconclusive, never unreachable. Available adults, rights-based water and stored loads do not imply willingness or future work. Actual thirty-day help comes only from water, stripping, salvage and completed demolition records; unserved household-episode exposures remain in the denominator. Observer-set exposures are marked separately. The kernel supplies the facts; the web draws them and switches between fire and water lenses without using stale responses. Wire 1.71 appends typed FireHelp/CoverageHome fields under ADR-0001; snapshots 99 and content API 86 stay unchanged. No large-population query-performance claim is made.

- **BD ignition sensitivity and observer losses (2026-10-14):** final BD behavior is swept at nominal 1, 3, 10, 30 and 100/K household-years by scaling activity hazards, never incident counts. Daily exposure is 61.071 household-years per arm; actual rates are 0, 16.374, 16.374, 32.749 and 98.246/K. The highest arm has six escapes, four put out, three roof fires, one spread, one death, 45 L applied and ten minutes of response work. Two roof fires were noticed and one was not. No stripping, salvage or completed demolition is observed; no core prior is tuned and no complete response fit is claimed. The reproducible runner, CSV and source/version notes are in docs/calibration/fire-ignition-sweep.md. The Fires row now excludes whole observer-set episodes from natural losses and reports their buildings/spread/deaths separately. Save schema 99, content API 86 and wire 1.71 stay unchanged.

- **BG physical bank step (2026-10-14, ADR-0022 §11):** a bank's linear geometry is a sidecar
  to appended earth kind 3, leaving the existing version-1 platform/pit expansion unchanged.
  The global save schema is 100; 99 and earlier migrate to no bank segments, while new records
  under old headers are refused. Dedicated borrow links cannot be shared by two segments.
  Built height follows trapezoidal area rather than a linear height multiplier. Cell-average
  earth shading and the sub-grid hydraulic crest remain separate. A minimax connected-storage
  calculation preserves supplied reach excess volume at barrier sills; unbanked reaches use
  the existing BF calculation. Content API 86 stays unchanged: no new authored work template
  is available in this physical step. Wire 1.72 appends centre-line and condition fields.
  This is a controlled physical/observer step, not completion of BG. Voluntary labour and
  its digging, hauling and compaction budget, failures and upkeep, trapped rain and explicit
  borrow depression storage remain planned; drains and terraces remain deferred.

- **BG borrow-ground storage (2026-10-14):** bank-associated ground differences, including
  excavated borrow pits and compacted fill, enter their affected reach's connected storage.
  Cells count once even where reserved envelopes overlap. Removing a crest does not erase
  excavation. A negative HAND after digging can fill below the original bed datum without
  losing supplied flood volume. Unbanked, unchanged reaches retain BF's calculation; ordinary
  legacy mining/levelling works do not silently change drainage. Bank envelopes must remain
  in the map and contain the complete trapezoid; malformed snapshots are refused. The change
  uses existing saved ground and geometry: save schema 100, content API 86 and wire 1.72 stay.
  Persistent trapped rain, deterioration, voluntary labour and irrigation remain planned.

- **BG overtopping erosion (2026-10-14):** actual overflow head and duration
  lower the bank crest by an authored prior; there is no annual wear or fixed breach chance.
  Earth removed from the bank enters a saved compacted-equivalent washed-sediment account,
  distinct from construction's total placed fill. Ground loses that volume and replays the
  remaining fill exactly. This is a coarse crest/volume model, not a breach cross-section or
  sediment-routing model. Piping, material/foundation quality, settlement evolution and chosen
  upkeep remain planned. Save schema 101 appends a keyed sediment record without changing the
  fixed bank struct; schemas through 100 retain saved ground/damage with no invented sediment.
  Content API 87 adds strict optional `[banks]`; wire stays 1.72, with sediment in kernel words.

- **Banks built together, as built (2026-10-14, M6b slice BG; ADR-0022 §11):** no new ADR.
  **What people remember:** a household's own flood losses only (research 12-08 §1.3:
  "requests arise from observed problems"): floor stores spoiled in its buildings, valued at
  their food, and sown crops drowned (5 days under water), valued at their seed and work, each
  at its cell and depth, kept `memory_years` (10, a design prior). Nothing global (episode
  counts, observer origin) enters a forecast; `FloodMemory`'s maxima are not read. **Where a
  bank goes:** straight segments parallel to the river near each costliest remembered place
  (up to six), at 7 positions and 8 lengths. Each is laid out at the highest remembered water
  surface plus `freeboard_m` above the lowest ground it crosses (0.3-3 m), on ground free to
  dig, with a square borrow pit `pit_depth_m` deep beside it. A place counts as kept dry when
  the reach's water, as high as remembered there, reaches it only over a crest: the same
  minimax connected-storage path the flood depths use (extracted, unchanged), with every
  standing bank. The kept losses, at what an hour of each household's work brings, over
  `life_years`, must exceed the work. This is an engineering judgement the planner makes, as
  crossing sites are found by path; people's gains come only from their own losses.
  **Its work (research 11-12 §1.2, §2.4):** per bank cubic metre, `digging.h_per_m3` to dig,
  84 basket loads (1.2 loose × 1,400 kg / 20 kg) each `load_min` plus the walk there and back
  at the worker's own pace, and 0.9 × `place_h_per_m3` to spread and tamp. Earth moves through
  `place_from_borrow` at the end of each work step, so nothing is left half-carried; no
  labour or fill comes with adoption. Concurrent workers are capped at length / `front_m`.
  **Measured:** six lived river-valley villages flooded once at +100 and +400 m³/s after 40
  days: 0-6 of 6-7 households recorded losses. Most candidate banks crossed fields or plots
  (1,435 of 1,582 rejected), 147 kept nothing dry, two passed the geometry and neither
  repaid its work after one remembered flood (best: 7.6 h a year against 384 h). With the
  same loss remembered five years running (the test's setup), a 40 m, 0.4 m bank is proposed,
  passes in the test's hands, and in thirty lived days three households give 10.2 of its 384
  hours by their own choice. **Also fixed:** the field-site cache's stamp now includes the
  ground a household looks over, which flood water redraws within a day (a debug assertion
  fired under a raised river; release builds could keep a stale site for the day). **Left:**
  banks of more than one segment, banks across fields, piping, settlement, paid repairs and
  upkeep by law, trapped rain and irrigation remain planned.

- **Banks seep, settle and give way, as built (2026-10-14, M6b slice BG; ADR-0022 §11):** no
  new ADR. Research 11-12 §4.2 separates load from resistance and holds damage across events
  until repaired; that is the model, with authored priors and no annual failure chance.
  **Seepage:** each lived day, over a bank's sound barrier edges, the head is the high side's
  water surface (capped at the crest) less the low side's surface or ground, taken only where
  the high side is wet. The largest head adds `piping_per_head_day` × head (0.01 a metre-day,
  a design prior) to the bank's damage, which is capped at 1. At 1 the bank is breached and
  stops being a barrier. Water over the crest on both sides holds no head; overtopping erosion
  (unchanged) wears it instead. **Settling:** placed fill sinks toward `settle_share` (0.05)
  of its built height with a time constant of `settle_days` (365). It only deepens and moves
  no earth. Research 11-12 names crest settlement among a levee's defects and leaves the
  settlement allowance out of its volume formula without a figure, so both values are design
  priors. **Told:** a bank built by
  law that breaks is told once (`FloodStep::BankGaveWay`) and recorded in the polity's
  `banks_failed`. **Saves 103:** piping damage per bank (0 < d ≤ 1, no duplicates, naming a
  bank) and the told failures (naming the polity's own banks). Older headers that carry
  either are refused, and schema 102 loads with no damage. **Measured:** on the test village
  (seed 3), the finished 0.41 m bank under the same reach raised in turn by +50, +100 and
  +200 m³/s for six days each took 0.14% damage, all from the first. The larger floods
  covered both sides, so there was no head, and +200 wore 2.5 mm off its crest. A bank that
  low is overtopped before seepage matters; seepage is the failure of a higher bank holding
  back water. **Not conditional yet:** the research's hazard depends on material and
  foundation, but the land carries no soil texture to condition on, so one rate serves every
  bank. **Left:** that conditioning, paid repair and upkeep by law, banks of more than one
  segment and across fields, trapped rain and irrigation.

- **Banks kept and mended, as built (2026-10-14, M6b slice BG; ADR-0022 §11):** no new ADR.
  ADR-0022 §11 says "Nobody mends a polity's bank unless a law asks", and research 12-08 §1.4
  says "Do not assume that a successful construction mobilization persists indefinitely".
  Keeping a bank is therefore its own law, not a term of the law that built it. **Issue and
  policy:** `bank_worn` (appended, code 14) holds while a bank the polity built wants mending
  and no law in force keeps it. A bank wants mending once it has given way, its crest has sunk
  or worn `mend_crest_m` (0.1 m) below its design, or it has taken `mend_piping` (0.1) of
  seepage damage; both are design priors. `keep_bank` (appended) is proposed, forecast and
  decided like a bank built. A household gains what it reckoned, when the bank was proposed,
  the bank saves it a year, and pays its share of the mending wanted now, spread over
  `life_years`. This treats a mended bank as good as new, a design prior. **Looking over:** a
  kept bank is looked over when a high water goes down and at each year's start (research
  11-12 §5.5: event-driven maintenance plus periodic inspection). If it wants mending and is
  not already being mended, its hours are added to what is asked of the households. Each
  household's share is of building and mending together, and the chronicle tells it.
  **Mending (research 11-12 §4.1: inspect, refill, compact):** `banks::mend` lays compacted
  earth dug from the bank's own borrow pit on its crest, at the building charges for digging,
  carrying and placing. It restores what water wore off first, then what settled. Then it digs
  out and tamps again the bank's damaged share, its seepage damage times its whole fill (a
  design prior), at digging plus placing hours with no carrying. Mass moves from the pit to the
  bank; the washed-sediment account is untouched. A breach stays open until all the mending it
  needs is done. People choose the work as they choose to build; when it is done the
  chronicle says so, and a later failure is told again. Nothing keeps a bank no law keeps, and
  a law in force does not make anyone work, so a neglected bank remains a possible result.
  **Saves 104:** refill per bank, repair hours asked and the mending flag per bank site, and
  each keeping law's bank. Older headers carrying any of them are refused. **In the test
  village:** a second, higher bank beside the first outweighed keeping the first while
  households still remembered their losses. In the test, with those memories cleared, the
  keeping law was proposed under `bank_worn`, mending was asked, and a worker's hours repaired
  the seepage damage. **Left:** banks of more than one segment and across fields, trapped
  rain and irrigation, and conditioning the seepage rate on soil.

- **Claude handoff (2026-10-14, owner request):** stop after the tested overtopping slice on
  `codex/codex-development`, with no merge to main. The handoff is
  `docs/handoffs/2026-10-14-m6b-claude.md`; BG remains partial and BH/M6c remain planned.
  Erosion uses elapsed-day depths before forcing rollover, so a one-day flood counts.
  The final full workspace, short smoke, clippy, schema, web, commons and bank browser gates
  pass; the interrupted later ten-year run is not reported as a pass.

- **Irrigation ditches, the water's part, as built (2026-10-14, M6b slice BG; ADR-0022 §11):**
  no new ADR. **Channel (research 11-12 §1.5-§1.6, §2.3):** a ditch is a straight trapezoid
  below the grid: bottom width, depth, side slope 1.5:1, and its bed's fall from intake to field
  end. Its cut is L d (b + z d). Its earth lies along its side within the cells it crosses, so
  the cells' mean ground is unchanged; this sub-grid simplification is stated, not hidden.
  **Capacity:** Manning's Q = A R^(2/3) S^(1/2) / n running full above its silt. n goes from
  `n_clean` (0.025) to `n_weedy` (0.040) with its weeds, which reproduces research 11-12
  §4.4's 62.5 % capacity. It carries nothing below `min_gradient` (0.05 %). **A day's water
  (research 03-02 §1.5, §2.1):** after the day's rain and the aquifer's step, each open ditch
  whose earthwork is finished and whose field's crop is growing takes what that field's root
  zone lacks to be full, divided by conveyance times application. It takes no more than its
  capacity for a day or `max_share` (0.5, a design prior) of what its reach still carries after
  the ditches above it. `conveyance` (0.8, a design prior for a short earthen ditch) reaches the
  field; the rest recharges the aquifer patch under the ditch's middle, and a patch of water
  alone takes it into its water. The field's root zone keeps `application` (0.6, research 03-02
  §2.1 for surface application); the rest returns to the reach below the intake. The taking is
  debited from its reach and every reach below, and the return is credited from the next reach
  down, as changes to the day's flows that are saved for the day. Natural downstream flow
  already includes its tributaries, so nothing is summed twice. Each ditch keeps its totals
  taken, kept, seeped and returned, which must balance. **Saves 105:** ditch records and the
  day's ditch flows; older headers carrying either are refused. **Tested:** in a lived village,
  a finished ditch open to the river beside a sown field held more water in that field over ten
  days than the same ditch shut. Every cubic metre was accounted for. On a dry day the intake
  reach lost exactly what the ditch took, and every reach below lost that less what returned.
  The world saved and loaded exactly and lived on the same. **Left:** households choosing to dig
  and open a ditch, weeds and silt growing, clearing, the observer drawing ditches (the web
  draws kind 4 as a plain earthwork rectangle for now), and trapped rain.

- **Households dig ditches, as built (2026-10-14, M6b slice BG; ADR-0022 §11; the M6 fire
  brief §1.11):** no new ADR. **Who and when:** a household, alone, on its day of the year
  (keyed by the world and the household, as crossings are). One ditch at a time, and none to a
  field that has one. **What it sees:** its own field's last season, the water the crop needed
  and got, recorded at the field and kept until the next sowing. It does not see the soil or the
  river's flow. A field whose crop got less than `short_share` (0.9) of its need is weighed.
  **Forecast:** the grain lost to water is the crop's average yield on that ground times its
  area times one less the water factor (ADR-0012 §2's response, the same the harvest uses),
  valued at the household's own hours a kilogram of that grain. Over `life_years` (20) it must
  exceed the digging: the channel's cut at `h_per_m3` (8 hours, research 11-12 §2.2's 0.8-1.2
  m³ a worker-day for forming canals). A 100 m ditch of 0.3 by 0.4 m at 1.5:1 is 36 m³, 288
  hours, within research 11-12 §2.5 A's 33-50 worker-days for 40 m³. **Site:** a point on any
  reach within `max_length_m` (400 m) of the field's middle. The bed is taken in half the
  ditch's depth below the river's water there and cut its depth into the field. Its fall must
  reach the land profile's least gradient, and its line may cross no other field, plot or
  well. The best net gain wins. **Its earthwork's ground** is a 2 m square at the intake; the
  line is the segment's, below the grid. Plots laid later are not yet kept off a ditch's line,
  a stated limit. **Work:** people choose to dig it like a crossing the household builds, by
  what each hour is worth (`ditch_worth`, reckoned when chosen and saved), with no duty. Hours
  dig channel at `h_per_m3`, and its finishing is chronicled (`ChronicleKind::Ditch`).
  **Opening (design prior: no labour):** at midnight, open while the field's crop grows and its
  root zone holds less than the easy-water share, shut otherwise. Water reaches the field from
  the next day's step. **Tested:** with its last crop at half its need, a household lays out a
  ditch within reach and gradient; with its crop fully watered it does not. It lays out no
  second ditch while digging. Its people see the work and its worth. Eight hours dig a cubic
  metre, and the rest finishes it and is told. Sown again with a dry root zone, the ditch is
  opened and waters the field, and the world saves and loads exactly. **Not yet measured:**
  how often lived households dig in dry years. **Measured (2026-10-15):** in the ten-year
  smoke (two presets, two seeds) households laid out 11 to 21 ditches a world and dug 3 to 12
  of them; dug ditches took 12,000 to 36,000 m³ from the rivers, of which fields kept 48 %.
  All four worlds passed. Most laid-out ditches stay undug: a household weighs one again each
  year and digs it only as it chooses. **Deferred: weeds and silt growing and their
  clearing.** A household's ditch carries about 0.16 m³/s clean, and the driest hectare wants
  about 0.005 m³/s (417 m³ a day). Fully weeded and half silted it still carries about
  0.023 m³/s, four times that, so neither binds and their clearing would be work nobody needs.
  They come back with shared ditches feeding many fields. **Left:** shared ditches and trapped
  rain. **Observer (wire 1.73):** an earthwork of kind 4
  carries its ditch's line and whether its intake is open. The map draws it as a blue line,
  solid while open and faint while shut or being dug, and its words say whose it is, how long,
  how far dug, and the water taken and kept.

- **Roofs that do not burn, as built (2026-10-15, M6b slice BH; ADR-0022 §12):** no new ADR.
  **Memory:** at a fire's end, the household whose building it was and the household of everyone
  who was in it or saw it burn remember it (`Household.fire_losses`: day, building, own or seen,
  whether its roof burns, and the hours putting it right would take: building it again if it
  fell, else mending each part it lost), for `rules.memory_years` (10; research 11-09 §2.3's
  2-20 years). Someone who only heard the shout remembers nothing. **Issue:** `burned` holds while
  any household of the settlement remembers a fire, and its households' elders are among those
  who weigh moves. **Template:** the policy kind `building_rule` is appended; its template is
  content (`[rule]`: `template`, `within_m`, `needs`), so the kernel holds the predicate and the
  content the numbers. `roofs_unburnt` names a property, not a technique (11-09 §5.2): a roof
  that does not burn, which today only fired tile is. 4 m follows 12-03 §2.2's radiation falling
  to 5 kW/m² at 4 m. **Sponsor:** only someone who knows the technique the template names
  (`firing`) is offered the move (11-09 §1.4). **Forecast:** the burnt roofs a household
  remembers, over the settlement's standing buildings and the memory's years, is its believed
  rate; times rebuilding its own buildings that burn (and its next home, if it has no roof
  enough or its home has given way), times `rules.avoided_share` (0.5, a design prior), is what
  it believes averted a year. Against it, a household about to build pays what tiling its newest
  home would add (work, carrying and its own cost of the materials) over `rules.horizon_years`
  (20); a hut, or a household that cannot make tile, keeps the rule by building apart and reckons
  that free. A household below its subsistence values a little more food at nothing, as for any
  law, so those who lost their stores with their homes are not the rule's keenest supporters.
  **Binding and keeping:** in force, it binds buildings begun from the day it passed; old roofs
  stay (11-09 §1.7). A household's eldest who knows it keeps it by the curfew's weighing (norm,
  stance, regard for the sponsor), with no sanction: a tile roof where its people fire tile and
  the program is a frame, else a plot at least the rule's distance from every standing building,
  else it builds as it would. Each building begun within reach counts as kept, broken or broken
  unaware. **Provenance:** a tile roof begun while the rule was in force names it, derived from
  its start and the law's history (a rule since ended no longer shows: the law keeps no end
  date). **Tested:** in a lived village a row of huts 1.5 m apart, one set alight; the fire took
  the row, every household that saw it remembered each hut, with the owner's marked its own;
  households above subsistence forecast a gain; nobody proposed the rule while nobody fired
  tile, and someone did once the settlement knew firing, against the issue `burned`; in force
  and known, a household that kept it laid out a home that was tiled or 4 m from every other
  building; the world saved and loaded exactly. **Not yet:** walls of named kinds, a least gap,
  the issue `gave_way`, and how often lived worlds come to such a rule. **Verified after
  commit:** the full simcheck suite (69 binaries) and all ten release short-smoke worlds pass.

- **Walls of stone or brick, and buildings kept apart, as built (2026-10-15, M6b slice BH;
  ADR-0022 §12):** no new ADR. **Memory:** when a building gives way, every household of its
  settlement hears it told (as the chronicle tells it) and remembers it for
  `rules.memory_years`: day, building, its own or not, its wall kind and what putting it right
  would take (`Household.gave_way`, save schema 108). **Issue:** `gave_way` while any household
  remembers one. **Templates** (content API 94): `walls_of_kinds` names allowed wall kinds
  (`wattle`, `rubble`, `mud_brick`, `fired_brick`), a technique in 11-09 §5.2's sense;
  `least_gap` names a distance, a separation. Content authors `works_wrought_walls` (rubble, mud
  brick or fired brick; needs rubble walling, which founders bring) and `works_wrought_spacing`
  (3 m, from 12-03 §2.2's 2.14-3.14 m thresholds; needs nothing). The walls template answers
  both `burned` and `gave_way` by authoring judgement: a remedy follows the cause people
  attribute, not the kernel's (11-09 §1.4), so a hut brought down by rot may move a village to
  ask for stone walls. **Forecast:** as for roofs, a household's believed rate is the losses of
  the kind the rule forbids that it remembers (for walls, every fire and every building that
  gave way whose walls the rule forbids; for a gap, burnt thatch) over the settlement's standing
  buildings and the memory's years, times rebuilding its own forbidden buildings (and its next
  home if about to build), times `rules.avoided_share`. A walls rule costs what its newest frame
  home's walls of the best allowed kind it can build would add; a gap rule costs nothing it
  reckons (the walk to a farther plot is not counted, a simplification). **Keeping:** a keeper of
  a walls rule designs mass walls where it knows a masonry technique and its program is a frame;
  a hut cannot, so it builds as it would and breaks the rule. A keeper of a gap rule takes a plot
  that far from every standing building. A walls or gap rule binds every building begun; a roof
  rule only one within its reach. **Tested:** a hut made to fail under its own weight was heard
  of by every household of the settlement, its owner's marked its own and its walls wattle; the
  walls rule was proposed against `gave_way` while nothing had burned and the gap rule was not;
  once a hut burned the gap rule was proposed against `burned`; in force, a hut counted as
  breaking the walls rule and a hut 6 m from its neighbours as keeping the gap rule; the world
  saved and loaded exactly. **Not yet:** how often lived worlds come to these rules (the demo).

- **The M6b demo, as built (2026-10-15, M6b slice BH; plan §7's M6 demo, second part):** no new
  ADR. **The world** (civ-sim's `great_fire` example, run by `web/e2e/m6b-demo.spec.ts` with
  `TCE_DEMO=1`; `demos/m6b/m6b-demo.txt` and three pictures): river valley seed 1 at 768 cells, a
  band of 100, lived 450 days at Max, into its second summer. **No lived great fire:** in 450 days
  no fire of the village's own escaped (the ignition sweep, §9, found escapes rare at this size),
  so, the time box spent, the observer set one. **`NUDGE`s, logged:** where (the observer's sight
  of the truth: the thatched building with the most others within 4 m of its plot, here 3) and
  when (noon of the first day whose fuel held 0.13 of its dry mass or less and whose wind blew at
  4 m/s or more; the first try waited from autumn for 0.11, which this valley rarely reaches, and
  never found it). Up to four worlds are made and the first whose fire took four buildings is
  kept; none did, so the last is kept. **What happened** (four worlds, all alike in the fire and
  its politics): on 30 May of year 2, in 6.7 m/s of wind with fuel at 0.12, the fire spread from
  Kesta's household's hut to the two beside it and took 3 buildings, 120 kg of goods and no lives.
  Every household that remained remembered it. A week later Lena, who knew rubble walling,
  proposed that new walls be of rubble, mud brick or fired brick, against the fire; the gathering
  agreed, 42 for and 3 against. A week after that Talia proposed that a new building stand 3 m
  from every other; agreed, 49 for and 2 against. Most stances read "it makes little difference
  to their household": the forecasts were small, and people voted by their values (the rules bear
  on security) and their regard for the sponsor. Nobody knew firing, so nobody proposed tile roofs.
  **What followed:** the three burnt huts were mended in place, standing and roofed a year on; and
  nobody began a new building in that year, so neither rule bound anything: 0 kept, 0 broken.
  Over the year the village shrank (107 people to 32-72 in the four worlds) as households left
  the valley; a fire-free run of the same world loses its band the same way in its third year
  (founding failure, recorded since M3c), so this is not the fire's. **Found:** (1) a rule that
  binds only new work does nothing while a village mends rather than builds: research 11-09 §1.7's
  other activation modes (major alteration, periodic inspection) are what would reach the old
  stock, and none is built; (2) a village of scattered huts burns three, not twenty: whether a
  great fire is possible waits on denser building (towns, M7), not on spread tuned up. **Not
  established:** whether a rule ever comes to bind in a lived world, and whether its builders keep
  it. M6b closes with BF's open items (crossing scour, flood gates) and BG's trapped rain, shared
  ditches and multi-segment banks recorded as left, not done.
- **M6c design (2026-10-15, plan §7):** from the war brief and the observer brief
  (`docs/briefs/m6-war.md`, `m6-observer.md`), with 13-07 §1.2 (Lanchester laws as benchmarks
  that should not "determine battle termination"), §1.5 (E = min(N_available, K_usable), both
  sides "from the same pre-step state"), §1.6 (no casualty breakpoint), §1.7 (withdrawal, rout and
  surrender apart; pursuit needs reach), §2.3 (10–60 s steps; a 2–10 minute window of seen losses)
  and §5, and 13-05 §1.2–1.3 (joining a raid as each person's utility; the bargaining range)
  checked where the design rests on them. **One ADR,**
  [ADR-0023](decisions/0023-force-between-polities.md) (force between polities), amending
  ADR-0013 §1 and ADR-0018 §1 (a polity over several settlements, with since and how), ADR-0018 §2
  (camping), ADR-0020 §4 and §6 (takings across the boundary; a body that sent a band is blamed;
  appended clauses), ADR-0009 and ADR-0010 (enclosures on the walking grid). **Five slices**
  (§7): BI (takings across the boundary), BJ (bands and encounters), BK (enclosures), BL (sieges
  and terms after force), BM (a polity over several settlements, and the demo). **In that order**
  because takings give raids and enclosures a reason before war does (the plan's fortification
  kit, "takings between villages that give them a purpose before war does"); a band must exist
  before a line is worth raising against it; a siege needs a band and a shut line; and a change
  of sovereignty needs a hold or terms. The brief's suggested order put enclosures with takings;
  they come third here because a line raised only against takings is a fence, which households
  can already weigh. **The brief's open questions, answered.** (1) Anyone may call a raid
  (13-05 §1.2); a law may too. Without unauthorized raids a treaty cannot be undermined by its
  own side. (2) Annexation changes membership: a polity keeps a list of settlements, which is
  why this milestone needs its ADR. (3) A body of several settlements gathers at its seat's
  hearth, so distance shows as absence (13-04 §1.7); a custom amendment can move the seat. (4)
  Per-minute choices and blows replace plan §5.5's Lanchester-style model, which stays as tests
  (a gate-limited exchange keeps the linear law). (5) Captives wait for M7: custody needs
  household membership the kernel lacks; a strike on someone not fighting is recorded as the
  striker's choice. (6) A wooden spear now, made with wood shaping; bows, shields and armour
  later, each with its materials and skills (07-10 §3.1). (7) Fighting skill comes only by
  fighting until someone has a reason to ask for drill. (8) Threat is only a forecast term: a
  household weighing tribute for peace reads the raids and bands it heard of; a leader's demand
  travelling as a claim waits. (9) Raiders leave seed, as `take_goods` does; a switch is measured
  later with 13-09 §4's raid before planting against one after harvest. (10) The demo may nudge a
  raider's valuation of a store they saw, or how long members stay before their harvest calls
  them home, never an event; `NUDGE:` logged. (11) The *one body* clause (merger) and
  *assistance* (a league) are enough for M6's merger and federation; a competence matrix waits
  for M7. (12) Both: an actual raid prompts ADR-0018 §5's event review, and the yearly review
  weighs raids heard of, with safety among the terms. **The observer brief's question (10):** the
  siege page shows each side's food at current use, what still comes in and the band's
  endurance, never a progress bar. **Plot guards:** no date, era, size, rate or count makes a raid
  likelier; no issue weighs toward a band; the demo names an outcome (annexation) that 13-08
  §1.8 lists as one of seven endings, so the demo shows the siege and whatever ending the world
  reaches, and annexation only if a gathering chooses it. **Measured first (BI):** the funnel
  from targets elsewhere ranked to laws passed, before anything is tuned (the brief's §3).
- **Takings across the boundary, measured and built (2026-10-15, M6c slice BI):** no new ADR
  (ADR-0023 §2). **The probe first** (civ-sim's `take_probe` example): three villages of 100
  founded together, lived three years at Max; on the first of each month, every household short of
  its food target compared the best store it could take from at home with the best among the
  homes of settlements its members had seen. River valley seeds 1-3 and ria coast seed 1:
  297, 293, 281 and 187 household-probes short of food; 29, 144, 11 and 8 of them had seen homes
  elsewhere; 0, 51, 2 and 0 would have ranked a store elsewhere first (by more food there, or none
  at home); the median walk to the best store elsewhere was 54, 72, 82 and 52 minutes, and **not
  one** lay within the 20 minutes a taker walks (`take_food`'s `max_walk_minutes`). Takings at home
  over the same runs: 47, 97, 46 and 83. **Read:** villages founded kilometres apart do not take
  from one another one household at a time, however hungry; anything that crosses between them
  will be a band that sets out to (slice BJ). The widened targets are built anyway, for villages
  that come to stand close (splinters, growth), and every consequence is wired: the incident names
  the takers' settlement, a witness names only takers they know, *harms us* is written, the issue
  `raided` is held and a watch answers it, and a law against taking recovers nothing from
  outsiders. Nothing was tuned.
- **Bands and encounters, built in two steps (2026-10-15, M6c slice BJ):** no new ADR
  (ADR-0023 §3-4, §8, §10). Step one: a band is called by anyone at their review or the midnight
  after their household learns people of another settlement took from it; it goes only where its
  people have seen homes, within `bands.max_walk_minutes`; joining is each person's choice; the
  muster is who comes; the encounter is `war::fight`'s per-minute exchange over a frontage with
  no battle score, and the taking is an ordinary incident across the boundary. Step two: shirking
  costs regard (the tie act `stayed_home`), bands walking are seen (claim *band seen*), raids are
  told (claim *raid*), those who gave way leave at once, and raids heard of weigh in where a
  household lives, with *fled* recorded when they alone tipped a move. Step three: the laws
  `send_band` (a band led by the one it names, each household owing one person or keeping its
  share back as a levy) and `against_raiding` (a raid heard before the raiders' own gathering).
  Service is recorded on the band and the law's compliance rather than as an ADR-0015
  obligation, which is reckoned in food. Every weight is a design prior named in the content;
  nothing was tuned. What is not built yet is listed in §7 under the slice.
- **Terms after force as one appended clause, and terms agreed while a gathering is busy
  (2026-10-15, M6c slice BL, step two):** no new ADR (ADR-0023 §8). ADR-0023's *no raids* and
  *takings heard* are one clause, given by a side; both sides' together stand for the *truce*,
  and since a side's word already keeps its people from proposing a band law against the other,
  a separate truce clause would add only a term that causes nothing at its end. Peace is sought
  by a second template of the agreement kind (`year_of_peace`), so that what people hold dear
  weighs a word against raiding apart from leave to use claimed places. Seeking terms no longer
  waits for a gathering with no business: the meeting takes none of its time, and a raided
  village answers a raid at its gathering with laws of its own; in the test of a raided village,
  its gathering had business at every review for forty days, so under the old rule nobody there
  sought peace. The seeker's side now puts
  the terms to its gathering when it is free, as the other side already did, within
  `relations.answer_days`. The existing agreement tests pass unchanged.
- **M7 design (2026-10-15, plan §7):** from four briefs (`docs/briefs/m7-elections.md`,
  `m7-capture.md`, `m7-courts.md`, `m7-money.md`), which read 09-02, 09-04, 09-05, 09-06,
  09-07, 09-08, 09-09, 09-10, 09-15, 08-04 to 08-08, 08-12, 08-13, 08-17 and 08-20. **M7 is split
