  in four** (§7), as M5 and M6 were, because its contents are four kinds of work: M7a councils
  and elections, M7b courts and precedent, M7c trade laws, guilds and capture, M7d credit and
  money. **In that order** because the demo's captured "assembly" is a seated body (M7a) whose
  seats and votes M7c's merchants work on; courts (M7b) reuse M7a's seats and methods for
  forums, and come before capture so that a captured assembly's laws can be reviewed; money
  comes last because coin needs metal and a polity that spends, neither of which exists, and
  because the money brief finds that credit in goods comes before coin (08-06, executive
  recommendation; 08-07 §4), against plan §5.3's ladder, which M7d's ADR will settle. **One ADR
  now,** [ADR-0024](decisions/0024-seats-offices-and-elections.md) (seats, offices and
  elections); M7b, M7c and M7d are designed when reached, one ADR each expected. **The elections
  brief's open questions, answered:** (1) one body: a seated body is a `Membership` of the one
  deciding body, so ADR-0013 §1 stands; (2) open stances by default, secret as a body value;
  (3) the council forecast's prior (the n eligible the sponsor knows who stand highest in
  counsel) is accepted and named as a design prior; (4) a seated body amends itself by its own
  rule, and the electorate's ratification waits; (5) households weigh the evenings a council
  saves them; (6) no party record, a label only; (7) terms of 6, 12 or 36 months in content,
  12 the default template; (8) seats may be apportioned by settlement; (9) strategic voting is
  off; (10) compliance keeps its present terms, no per-authority legitimacy; (11) offices stay
  unpaid in M7a, and patronage's selective benefits come with M7c; (12) any demo nudge is a
  prior, time-boxed and logged as `NUDGE:`, never an event. **Plot guards:** no population,
  date or era makes a council likelier; the smoke's finding that villages of about 50 never
  amend may stand as a result. The demo names two outcomes (a captured assembly's tariff, a
  struck-down curfew); each part's demo shows what its world reached, nudging only priors.
- **M8 design (2026-10-17, plan §7):** from four briefs (`docs/briefs/m8-scale.md`,
  `m8-transport.md`, `m8-planning.md`, `m8-building.md`), which read 01-01, 01-02, 01-03, 01-04,
  01-08, 01-11, 14-02, 14-03, 12-05, 12-06, 10-07, 07-08, 11-12, 14-13, 10-04, 10-05, 08-19,
  10-08, 08-11, 11-02, 11-03, 11-05, 11-06, 11-09, 11-10, 11-13 and 03-07. **M8 is split in four**
  (§7), as M5–M7 were: M8a scale, M8b ways, modes and traffic, M8c planning and land, M8d
  buildings and earthquakes with the demo. **Scale first**, because every other part has to run at
  a city's size and because cost today grows faster than the people (exponents 1.5–1.7: six
  searches scan the world and filter by settlement); then ways, since planning reserves corridors
  and land value needs travel times; then planning, since tall buildings need land worth building
  up for; buildings and the demo last. **One ADR now,**
  [ADR-0028](decisions/0028-scale-and-the-m8-gate.md) (scale and the gate); M8b–M8d are designed
  when reached, one ADR each expected. **The gate, amended:** the scale brief's arithmetic puts
  10k at a year a minute 150–190× from today's extrapolated cost and 50k 880–1,400×, against
  levers of about 7–140× and 15–470×; M8 gates 10k (three settlements of about 3,334 on the
  default map, a whole second year at Max) on the target PC, measures the demo's 30k, and moves
  50k to M9's aggregate LOD. If 10k misses after M8a's time-boxed slices, the gate is amended to the
  figure reached, with evidence. **The briefs' open questions, answered where M8a needs them.**
  *Scale brief:* (1) 10k is gated, 30k measured, 50k M9's. (2) Measured headless on the target
  PC; this container measures every slice, the target's number is the owner's to run and is
  marked not yet measured until then. (3) Three settlements of about 3,334, the second year whole.
  (4) ADR-0011's approximations and those ADR-0028 §6 adds under Gate B. (5) Tie-breaks keyed by
  event identity wait for M9's settlements side by side. (6) No lightweight settlements in M8.
  (7) The web observer is M8's measure of drawing at 60 fps; Unreal's on its own track. (8) Pause
  is answered within a tick at Max (the host lives a day in chunks). (9) A buyer weighs every
  seller, as built. (10) The appearance seed waits for Unreal. *Transport, planning and building
  briefs:* answered when their parts are designed; three of their findings bear on the order and
  are recorded now. **The demo names its outcome:** plan §7's "a 30k-person planned capital next
  to an organic port town" is a world's shape, not something the engine may author; M8d designs
  it as worlds founded large enough for a city (setup, as ADR-0018's founding groups are), where a
  plan law may or may not pass, time-boxed with nudges of priors logged. **Homes cannot reach a
  city's ground:** a home is placed within `HOME_REACH_SECONDS` (300 s) of the hearth, about 28 ha,
  some 2,800 people at 100 a hectare; M8c must lift it. **Pack animals and carts need livestock**,
  which the content has none of: M8b builds the handcart and the dugout, and a husbandry design
  is recorded as a gap before draught animals. **Bench, not yet clean:** the last measurement
  (slice BD, 1,447.4 s a year for 3×1,000) predates M6c and M7; slice CF measures again.
- **M8b design (2026-10-17, plan §7):** from the transport brief (`docs/briefs/m8-transport.md`),
  one ADR, [ADR-0029](decisions/0029-ways-modes-and-traffic.md). **The brief's open questions,
  answered:** (1) no beasts in M8: pack animals and ox carts wait for a husbandry design, and the
  only wheels are hand-pulled; (2) wet ground does not slow walkers in M8 (it would change every
  world; with drainage); (3) congestion is queues at bottlenecks, not time-bucketed edge
  capacity; (4) Accelerated mode lives the same events, cohorts only as a declared approximation
  if they cost too much; (5) a trail becomes a way only when someone works on it; (6) a way
  carries its own grade profile and routing's ground is unchanged; (7) upkeep only by law, a
  frontage duty one bundle a law may name; (8) consignments for boats, carts and trips past the
  day, a porter's hand load within a day staying in the hand; (9) the demo's port town needs a
  navigable trunk river and dugouts, not sail; (10) payload priors where the reports' tables
  overlap (handcart 150 kg, dugout 400 kg), marked as design priors; (11) tolls in M8 on the
  duty machinery, late; vehicle classes and time windows later; (12) the dashboard measures
  waits by place, person-trips and tonne-km by mode, and travel time by occupation and purpose,
  with no tolerance until a run is seen. **Order:** ways first (the records every other slice
  stands on), then bottlenecks for walkers (they exist today at crossings and gates), boats
  (within reach of today's techniques, and the river is where loads first pay), handcarts on
  ways, works on ways, and where to live last. Plan §5.4's transport row is amended by the ADR.
- **M8c design (2026-10-18, plan §7):** from the planning brief (`docs/briefs/m8-planning.md`),
  one ADR, [ADR-0030](decisions/0030-planning-and-land.md). **The brief's open questions,
  answered:** (1) one `Plan` kind whose templates compose operations (an orthogonal
  subdivision, public sites, an extent, an orientation rule), further operations appended as
  vocabulary; (2) no sale or lease of land in M8, ADR-0007 standing, so land value shows in
  fees, ground rent, compensation and households' receipts; (3) *taken* is offered, for ground
  reserved once its crop is in, at the cost of a grievance, and no clause ever clears a standing
  home; (4) site choice changes every world, and its slice records new baselines; (5) the
  household's own walk reckoning replaces `HOME_REACH_SECONDS`, out to the walk it accepts to a
  field; (6) a keeper is a new office per plan with a tenure; (7) removal is a remedy, only for a
  building begun after the plan on its reserved ground; (8) zoning in M8 is district uses on a
  plan and two nuisance rules, dimensional districts after v1; (9) a plan needs laying out by
  cord and stake, a technique like any other; (10) no settlement is founded under a plan: the
  demo's planned capital must pass by law in a world founded large (M8d), or not at all; (11) the
  Land row shows densities with denominators, payments by channel, plans' shares and reckoned
  values by walk, with no tolerance until a run is seen. **Order:** site choice first (every
  later slice needs a household to compare plots, and it lifts the reach), then the plan law and
  its reservations, assembly and allotment, compliance, use and nuisance rules, and land value
  and density last. **Height** moves to M8d with grammar v3's storeys, as a household's choice
  in hours; plan §5.1's "how tall (land value, tech)" is amended by the ADR.

- **M7b design (2026-10-16, plan §7):** from the courts brief (`docs/briefs/m7-courts.md`),
  which reads 09-07, 09-06, 09-02, 09-05, 09-04, 06-05 and 06-09. **One ADR,**
  [ADR-0025](decisions/0025-forums-precedent-and-review.md) (forums, precedent and review):
  a forum is a law (*hear cases*) naming what it hears, its seat (one holder, a panel by lot,
  or a membership) and its rule; precedent is the saved case and the remembered finding;
  a limit is a law above laws, a predicate over laws' own fields from a closed set the kernel
  reads; review is a power a forum's law grants; rulings are carried out and known as anything
  else. **Four slices** (§7): BR (a forum by law), BS (precedent), BT (limits and review), BU
  (rulings carried out and the demo). **The brief's open questions, answered:** (1) the
  gathering's findings since M4 are precedent (09-07's opening); (2) all three seats, content
  offering each; (3) limits are a closed set in code, parameterized by content: daylight work
  (a curfew's hours) and a levy's share in v0; (4) review is a power a forum's law grants, apart
  from any limit; (5) standing comes from bearing a law, so challenges are abstract, and pleas
  within a case wait; (6) curfews keep no sanction; (7) an appended norm, *abide by findings*;
  (8) the bundle stays fixed; (9) no rehearing in v0; (10) one forum at the seat; (11) after a
  time-boxed week without a strike-down, nudge the weight a household puts on hours a curfew
  keeps it home, or the cost of proposing an amendment, logged as `NUDGE:`; (12) land and debt
  wait for M7d. **Plot guards:** no date, era or size makes a forum, a limit or a challenge
  likelier; no content limit may be aimed at curfews alone; a world without a *hear cases* law
  gives the same digests as before.
- **M7c design (2026-10-16, plan §7):** from the capture brief (`docs/briefs/m7-capture.md`),
  which reads 09-09, 09-10, 08-17, 08-12, 08-08, 08-13 and 08-18. **One ADR,**
  [ADR-0026](decisions/0026-organizations-privileges-and-trade-policy.md) (organizations,
  privileges and trade policy): duties and embargoes are laws whose taxable event is the
  purchase at another settlement's door; organizations by stake are a kind of ADR-0017's
  faction; a privilege (licence or staple) is a law naming an organization, breached by a posted
  offer and brought as a case; the keeper's diversion, relief by favour, the collector and patron
  gifts are corruption and patronage; closure is a run of amendments; capture and drag are derived
  and measured. **Five slices** (§7): BV (trade laws, after a probe of volume), BW (organizations
  by stake), BX (privileges and the barred), BY (corruption and patronage), BZ (closure, capture
  diagnostics, the demo). **The brief's open questions, answered:** (1) the purchase at the
  door; (2) duties in kind to the store until M7d; (3) a kind of faction; (4) members across
  settlements, privileges per polity; (5) a duty may exempt resellers or a named organization's
  members, a sponsor's vocabulary; (6) breaches are cases, heard by a forum whose law hears
  privileges, else the gathering; (7) only gifts recorded as a patron's enter stances
  (`w_owed`), so the general help balance stays unread; (8) open acclamation stays, no secret
  ballot in M7; (9) relief by favour, recorded; (10) a staple or an exempting duty passed by a
  body carried by members and those who owe them counts, and the demo says what happened;
  (11) measure first: three settlements and fetching to resell, both existing; (12) nepotism is
  measured against the kin share among the eligible. **Plot guards:** no authored
  organization; no issue weighs toward a trade law; no meter enters a choice; a world without
  any of the new records gives the same digests as before.
- **Rivers left their banks for weeks every year, fixed (2026-10-16, found while probing M7c
  slice BV):** villages of 40 to 120 founders emptied in their second to fourth winter. **Measured:**
  a monthly ledger of seed 1's food (river valley, a band of 40) showed harvests near plan
  (about 477 days of food a person in year 2) but each wet season's flood spoiling 25–47 days of
  food a person in a month, seed among it, so the next sowing shrank (55 then 43 days of seed),
  harvests fell (477, 371, then less) and the village left in month 51. Eating was not the cause
  (about 2,100 kcal a person a day once settled). **The cause:** bankfull discharge was 1.5 × each
  reach's mean (as built in slice BF), a misreading of research 03-02 §2.1, where 1.4–1.5 is the
  *recurrence in years* of the bankfull flood. Rivers by the day are flashy (seed 1's flow against
  its mean: median 0.08, 90th percentile 2.4, yearly peaks 9–20), so 1.5 × the mean was passed on
  36–66 days a year in river valley 1 and 2 and ria coast 1. **The fix:** each landscape's
  climatology routes its 300 years of daily surplus as the world's water does (the ground's share
  as an even base flow, the rest through the runoff store) and takes bankfull as the yearly peak
  reached once in 1.4 years (`BANKFULL_RECURRENCE_YEARS`, the median of the Ohio sites):
  6.3 × the mean in river valley, 5.3 × on the ria coast. Floodplains are derived, not saved, so
  saved worlds take the new banks when loaded; no schema or content change. **After:** days
  above bankfull 0–19 a year in the same worlds (most years have a short flood, as a 1.4-year
  flood should); seed 1's band lives six years at 41–47 people with 340–600 days of food a
  person, seed 2's at 46 with 720. Seed 3's still empties, in month 26: a high water peaking at
  27 × the mean in its eleventh month stood up to a metre deep in its homes for days and took
  about half the food on their floors (within the 03-07 depth-damage envelope: 0.33–0.49 of the
  most at half a metre), on top of a thin first harvest. A rare flood, not a yearly one; left to
  stand as the world's variance. `tests/levees.rs` raises its flood to 150 m³/s over bankfull,
  not 100 over the natural flow, to keep one flood short of repaying a bank. Crossings scour at
  the same bankfull and now stand longer. **Not changed:** a flooded floor's stores still spoil a
  share a day while the water stands (ADR-0022 §9); the smoke runs 30 days, so nothing in the
  routine checks would have caught this, and the long-run check stays the dashboard.
- **2026-10-16 — a lean-village polity test failed once under load.** During slice CB2's checks,
  `a_village_whose_food_will_not_last_proposes_and_its_gathering_decides`
  (`kernel/crates/civ-sim/tests/polity.rs`) found no common store decided within its scene's 30
  days while a four-year release run of the capture example shared the machine; it passed 11 of
  11 runs alone, its file 3 of 3, and the whole suite alone afterwards. The scene is seeded, so a
  load-dependent outcome would mean something read from time, scheduling or unordered iteration
  reaches a decision. **Not yet investigated:** reproduce under load and bisect the first day the
  digests differ; fix the source, never the test.
  - *Again, 2026-10-17 (slice CE3a's chain):* the same test failed the same way in the full
    suite. Time-boxed: alone it passed in 12 s; four filtered copies at once under six spinning
    processes passed (about 40 s each), and three copies of the whole file (its six tests in
    parallel) under the same load passed (about 122 s each). The kernel reads no clock (no
    `Instant` or `SystemTime` outside the host), has no process-wide state but a grid id counter
    and per-thread search caches keyed by grid, and the one threaded search (landmarks) writes
    each job's result by its index. **Still not found:** what the suite run differs in (its other
    test binaries run before it, not beside it); next, keep the failing run's digests.
  - *Found, 2026-10-17 (slice CE5):* not load at all. A world made by `Sim::create` draws a
    fresh identity from the OS each run, and the identity seeds the scheduler's tie-breaks (the
    order of an instant's events), so one seed lives a different life each run; the M7d demo's
    seed 1, run twice, made its first loan on day 234 and on day 229. The polity test, and 26
    other test files, made their worlds that way, so each run of the suite drew new lives and this
    scene's gathering sometimes decided outside its 30 days. **Fixed:** every test now makes its
    world with a fixed identity (`Sim::create_for_tests`, as the newer tests already did), and so
    does the capture example; a world's own identity still orders its own life, and the
    observer's new worlds keep a fresh one. The other demo examples keep `Sim::create`, so their
    recorded runs are each one draw among many.
- **Fix: a household short of water worked until dusk and ran dry overnight (2026-10-19, found
  by slice CX part 3's chain):** the smoke failed once, "1 households have no water" in
  `ria_coast` seed 5, and passed on two reruns. **Found:** the smoke's worlds draw a fresh identity
  each run (above, slice CE5), so a probe lived that seed under 40 fixed identities: 2 ended their
  30 days with one household dry, the same three-person household both times. Traced through its
  last day, it held 30 L at dawn against 60 L a day, fetched one load at 13:20, and its people
  prepared a field until the light left, ate and went to the hearth; nobody fetched in the dark, so
  its water ran out before midnight. The rule that sends someone for water "in the last of the
  light" when what is at home would not last the night only acts when someone decides then, and
  work by daylight was sized to end 20 minutes before dark wherever it was, so a long session
  carried everyone past that light. **Fixed:** while what is at home would not last until
  morning, work by daylight (fields, gathering, digging, building and every site's work) is sized
  to the light less the trip to water and a meal, so whoever works is home while the trip can
  still be made; the trip's sum is the one the fetch already weighed (`decide::night_water`).
  **Tested:** the bound alone (short, enough, dark, no water known); the 40 identities, none dry.
  **What it changed** (behaviour, not saves): the bench's village of three settlements, 30 days in
  both modes, ends with the same 3,022 people and 625 buildings and 609 fields against 606; a
  person-day's farming 2.467 hours against 2.483 and building 0.960 against 0.988, fetching water
  unchanged at 0.109; every section that people's days write changes digest, and days are as long
  within the runs' spread (4,462 ms against 4,505 at the median, by the minute; 3,723 against
  3,449 at Max). **Tests changed** (their scenes, not what they check): the two errand scenes in
  `tests/fetch.rs` now give the buyer hoes for every hand, since its people, living another
  morning, reached the seller's door needing a hoe and bought one, and one trip makes one deal,
  its own need first; and the field pledge scene in `tests/credit.rs` keeps every law of debts
  heard from being proposed, since its gathering now passed one, and a case's time to pay
  reopened the loan, before the pledged field lay between crops (the courts have their own
  tests).
- **The smoke's dry household again, and a failing world's identity (2026-10-24, found by slice
  DY part 4b's chain):** the smoke failed once, "1 households have no water" in `ria_coast` seed 3,
  and passed on rerunning the same build; no smoke world knows gas making, so DY's changes nothing
  there reads. A probe lived that seed's 30 days under 40 fixed identities and found no dry
  household. The cause stays open: the smoke drew the identity and never printed it, so the world
  could not be replayed. **Changed:** a failing smoke world now prints its identity among its notes
  (`identity <hex>`), so the next one can be lived again exactly with that identity.
- **M8d design (2026-10-19, plan §7):** from the building brief (`docs/briefs/m8-building.md`),
  one ADR, [ADR-0031](decisions/0031-tall-public-buildings-and-shaking.md). **The brief's open
  questions, answered:** (1) `trussed_roof`, `storeyed_frame` and `tied_masonry`, none known to
  founders, each requiring `jointed_frame`; (2) the tool takes a lateral share of weight, and the
  observer's panel speaks in intensity words behaviour never reads; (3) one strength over the map
  in v0, no epicentre; (4) no natural earthquakes until worldgen has a tectonic source; (5) no
  ground amplification; (6) the existing collapse shares serve shaking, with whoever is inside at
  that minute; (7) no storey let to another household in M8; (8) no value bears on ornament;
  (9) a hall is proposed only for a loss measured first; (10) polities own buildings, not
  organizations; (11) no fire after shaking yet; (12) shaking has a dashboard row of its own,
  kept out of the structural failures row by origin. **Order:** a time-boxed probe of why no frame
  is built now that land costs, then grammar v3 with no behaviour change, gravity for tall and
  wide, the lateral mode and the tool, what follows a shaking, public buildings, style over seven
  traits, and the M8 demo with the gate. **Scale:** the demo's two settlements are founded at the
  largest size that lives within the time box; plan §7's 30,000 is recorded as reached or not.
- **Framing found by building (2026-10-19, M8d slice CZ, ADR-0031 §2):** NUDGE: half of those
  raising huts would find `jointed_frame` in 300 qualified hours (1 % of their building hours
  counting), about once a generation in a village that builds; research 07-07 WO02 places fitted
  joinery with wood shaping and layout but gives no rate. A design prior, to be measured against
  the ten-year smoke and the demo.
- **Design priors for gravity in version 3 (2026-10-19, M8d slice CZ, ADR-0031 §2):** NUDGE:
  a mass wall's restrained height over its thickness past 27 cannot stand
  (`MOST_SLENDERNESS`, EN 1996-1-1 §5.5.4's limit; research 11-05 gives height over thickness
  only as a vulnerability scale, stable below about 4-6 and much poorer above 9-12), and a
  truss's heel joint holds 20 kN against the roof's thrust (`TRUSS_JOINT_N`, a pegged and
  notched joint; no report gives a figure). Both are design priors, to be revisited if the
  checks they set decide what is built.
- **Design priors for masonry under shaking (2026-10-20, M8d slice DA, ADR-0031 §3):** NUDGE:
  a mass wall's bed joints resist sliding with friction 0.55 and cohesion 0.08 MPa
  (`MASONRY_FRICTION`, `MASONRY_COHESION_PA`; research 11-05 §2.5 reports one air-lime rubble
  calibration of μ = 0.558 and c = 0.0815 MPa), and a cracked wall keeps its friction but loses
  its cohesion. Revised in slice DA's fourth part: the research asks joints to be calibrated by
  kind, so cohesion is a share of the masonry's strength in compression from content
  (`MASONRY_COHESION_SHARE` 0.054, which gives the calibration's 0.08 MPa for the core's 1.5 MPa
  rubble, 0.054 MPa for mud brick and 0.16 MPa for fired brick in lime), and the same cohesion
  stands for the joints' bond in bending, which holds a sound wall out of its plane beyond rocking
  (`c·t²·L / 3Nh`; EN 1996's flexural strengths are of the same order). Design priors, to be
  revisited if the four-way sweep or the demo orders construction against what the reports say.
- **What the four-way sweep found (2026-10-20, M8d slice DA's fourth part, ADR-0031 §3):**
  NUDGE: two storeys of 30 cm walls meet, before one gives way, about 0.15 (mud brick), 0.15
  (rubble) and 0.19 (fired brick) of their weight sideways tied at each floor, and half of that
  untied, which sits in the range at which unreinforced masonry is damaged; but a frame of twelve
  20 cm oak posts a storey meets about 10 of its weight, so a timber frame never falls by
  shaking. Posts are checked only as cantilevers in bending; the frame's joints, which ADR-0031
  §3 names and research 11-05 says fail first, are not yet checked. Recorded, not tuned: the
  joints wait for the storeyed frame's check, and the demo should not read frames' survival as a
  finding.
- **Design priors for the rules after a shaking (2026-10-20, M8d slice DB, ADR-0031 §5):**
  NUDGE: the core's height rule names rubble and mud brick, a storey, and leaves fired brick in lime
  out, an authoring judgement from the sweep's order (fired brick holds most). The floor a height
  rule takes is valued at the work its newest home took times the share of its storeys above the
  limit: the work of making that floor again elsewhere, ignoring the ground it would take (ADR-0030
  §1's plot costs are not reckoned here). A builder keeping it builds the same bays a storey lower
  rather than wider, so a kept rule costs floor, not ground. Each revisited if the demo (DE) shows
  no household weighing height at all. And a household sizes a frame's members by the most caution
  any wall or system technique its people know calls for, not only the one the design ends up
  using (the wall kind is chosen inside the design), so a rubble failure also stiffens a wattle
  frame's posts a little; accepted while one caution scalar sizes every member.
- **Design priors for a storehouse raised together (2026-10-20, M8d slice DC's second part,
  ADR-0031 §6):** NUDGE: a household believes a storehouse would avert the rules' avoided share
  of the common store's measured spoiling a year (the mean of the years kept), split equally among
  the households, as for a rule's avoided losses; and it weighs the work over the rules' horizon
  of years, not the granary's own life. The work is the program's first shape's hours with its
  materials carried, at a middling skill when done. A building a polity raises is held in the
  polity's own id, owner of its plot and building, rather than a keeper household's: every
  household lookup then passes it by (upkeep, storage, inheritance, wealth, home work), which is
  what ADR-0031 §6 asks ("its upkeep falls to nobody unless a law asks it"); taste and the "seen
  elsewhere" review pass it by too until style reaches it (DD). Each revisited if the demo (DE)
  shows no storehouse proposed where stores spoil.
- **Design priors for a hall against the rain (2026-10-20, M8d slice DC's third part, ADR-0031
  §6):** NUDGE: rain takes `wet_attend` = 1 point from coming to a gathering in the open, the
  custom's whole own pull (`attend_base` = 1), so on a wet day only those with something at stake
  come; nothing measures how much rain thins an outdoor assembly, so it is a prior to revisit if
  the demo (DE) shows no gathering ever rained off, or every wet one. The loss a hall answers is
  only the hours given to a gathering that failed for want of a quorum, valued at the polity's
  mean hour; delay to what it would have decided is not weighed. The hall's size (four 3 m bays,
  6 m wide) is a design prior. Its gathering still meets at the hearth, the hall standing within
  80 m of it: the walk there is not changed.
- **Design priors for a watch tower (2026-10-20, M8d slice DC's third part, ADR-0031 §6):**
  NUDGE: a fire is seen late when nobody knew of it within 10 minutes of its covering catching
  (an escape grows into a roof in 2-15 minutes and a roof burns through in about an hour); a
  fire caught from a neighbour is left out, its conflagration's first fire carrying the loss. The
  loss is the whole work of putting its building right, not the part a sooner sighting would have
  saved. From the tower one sees 500 m against 150 m on the ground, standing within 4 m of its
  centre; a watch round begins there. These are kernel constants (`LATE_NOTICE_MIN`,
  `TOWER_SIGHT_M`, `AT_TOWER_M`), revisited if the demo (DE) shows no tower ever proposed where
  fires burn unseen, or one that never helps.
- **Who is noted at a crowded source (2026-10-21, M9b slice DJ):** design prior: a household
  notes at most 150 other households drawing at a source in a day (`uses::NOTED_AT_SOURCE`), the
  nearest to it in household order, which for founders follows where they live about the hearth.
  Research 04-04's outermost personal-network layer (about 150, a pattern and not a limit) gives
  the scale of those one tells apart among many at the water; the suspicion of a source
  (ADR-0021) reads only those seen there for some days. Before it, a settlement of 2,000
  households at one river held four million such pairs and folded them every midnight. Where no
  more than 151 households draw at a source in a day nothing changes: the suite passes as before
  and the bench's 2×200 digests are unchanged; a settlement as large as M8's 10,000 lives
  differently.
- **Gate C's first evaluation and the household day's priors (2026-10-21, M9a slice DI,
  ADR-0032 §5):** NUDGE: a household-resolved day's people turn in two hours after sunset (the
  middle of the four-hour evening a decision reads; with the evening's end the night was 7.8 h
  against Detailed's 8.8 h) and are weighed at sunrise, midday and an hour after sunset. Seven
  evaluations of Gate C (each about five minutes) took the household day from leisure +75 %, sleep
  −100 % and food +17–30 % to every aggregate within a few points of its tolerance; the rest is

- **Design priors for water mills (2026-10-22, M10a slice DR):** NUDGE: a wheel is set at half a
  metre of fall or more and 50 m from any other, grinds eight hours a day and is reckoned to ask
  100 hours a year of upkeep (dressing the stones, clearing the race) in its owner's choice,
  though that upkeep is not yet worked; the toll is a sixteenth of the flour. Without the upkeep
  a household grinding 600 kg a year beside a working mill would set a second for the toll it
  saves. Each revisited if the M10 demo shows mills nowhere where grain is ground by hand at
  scale, or one beside every household.

  (slope 0.05–0.6, 5 m or more above a channel), 0.3 to a square kilometre that qualifies,

- **Design priors for setting an engine (2026-10-22, M10a slice DS):** NUDGE: building an

  household weighs an engine only at its yearly line review, for the line from the pit it digs

- **Design priors for the locomotive (2026-10-23, M10b slice DW, first part):** NUDGE: an engine

- **Smoke draws a different world each run (2026-10-23):** the smoke command creates each world
  with a fresh identity, and the identity orders same-instant events, so a rare draw can fail a
  check one run in many (once, river valley seed 2: a household without water at the instant
  checked; 60 fixed identities probed afterwards were all watered). Whether that check should
  pass a household mid-refill is left open until it recurs.
- **Design priors for wagons on a line (2026-10-23, M10b slice DV, third part):** NUDGE: a pushed

  across ground up to 40 % between cells, weighing a step's earth beyond the ruling grade as half

- **Design priors for laying track (2026-10-23, M10b slice DV, second part):** NUDGE: timber track
  takes 50 kg of timber a metre (rails and sleepers of about 0.07 m³) and 1.5 hours to hew and lay,
  on a bed half a metre wider than the gauge each side; grading moves earth at 10-07 §2.2's 2.3
  hours a cubic metre; lines are searched over ground no steeper than 5 % and graded from there. The
  bed is the midpoint of the grade's upper and lower envelopes, which balances cut and fill only
  roughly; spoil and borrow, and grading's change to the map's ground, wait. Revisited when the M10
  demo shows a line laid.
- **Design priors for the wagonway (2026-10-23, M10b slice DV, first part):** NUDGE: a wagon on
  timber rails rolls at C = 0.005 (the brief's figure; no report gives rail's resistance), runs on a
  metre's gauge, is held back down 1 % by its pusher, and carries 2 t on 0.5 t; wooden railways are
  found at an e50 of 100,000 hours, as far techniques are. Track turns at most 45° a cell, ADR-0034
  §2's rule standing for a curve's least radius at the grid's scale. Revisited when the M10 demo
  shows a line laid.
- **Design priors for the lamp by choice (2026-10-23, M10b slice DU, fourth part):** NUDGE: an hour
  lit is worth an hour of home making to a household that can make a lamp, and it keeps fuel for 30
  hours of light (a week of evenings). Neither is measured; 12-09 §3.1 has light as a purchased
  service, which waits for a market in tallow. Revisited when the M10 demo shows households with
  lamps.
- **Design priors for dark sight (2026-10-23, M10b slice DU, third part):** NUDGE: a figure is made
  out by starlight at about 10 m (`dark_sight_m`), and a fat lamp's light (1 lux at a metre,
  research 11-13 §2.2) reaches 3 m from the home it burns in (`lit_m`); neither is measured. Dark
  sight waits for the world's first lamp lit, as ADR-0034 §9 chose. Revisited when the M10 demo
  shows takings by night where lamps are lit.
- **Design priors for work by lamplight (2026-10-23, M10b slice DU, second part):** NUDGE: only
  making at home runs after dark by a lamp (`max_walk_minutes = 0` stands for indoors; building a
  kiln or a furnace at the door counts, a field does not), and a lamp's escape rate is a lit
  hearth's, 2.0e-6 an hour a person, capped at `worked_per_hour` so it stays within the hazard's
  existing bound. 12-03 gives no rate for lighting apart. Revisited when the M10 demo shows
  households holding lamps and their fires.
- **Pumping by a wheel, and coke, deferred to the works (2026-10-22, M10a slice DS):** Both since
  built in slice DT (coke and the blast furnace its fourth part, wheels at pits its fifth); an
  engine pumping water back up to a wheel stays deferred, as no wheel yet wants for water. ADR-0033
  §7 names three ways a flooded pit is drained: by hand, by a wheel, or by an engine. DS built hand
  and engine; a wheel pumping a pit, and an engine pumping water back to a wheel (the brief's
  complement, 07-06 §5.5), wait for the works (slice DT), where a powered station drives more
  than millstones. Coke waits for the same slice's blast furnace, as nothing yet would burn it.
- **Design priors for the household day (2026-10-20, M9a slice DG, ADR-0032 §2):** NUDGE: the
  day is scored once at sunrise; waking minutes are the day less the middle of the content's
  sleep range and three meals; a walk's length in the day's sharing is reckoned straight off trail
  (its time when walked is the route's); asking and buying are taken at most once a day, and a
  claim on new ground, a home or a workshop once; at most 8 trips for water a household-day;
  company is one draw a member-day against the pool of the settlement's residents who kept it
  that day. Each is revisited by Gate C (slice DI).
- **M10 design (2026-10-22, plan §7):** from four briefs (`docs/briefs/m10-power.md`,
  `m10-rail-gas.md`, `m10-services.md`, `m10-money.md`), which read 07-06, 07-12, 07-05, 08-08,
  08-10, 08-03, 07-08, 12-09, 12-05, 12-06, 12-03, 12-04, 05-05, 06-08, 07-11, 05-04, 08-06, 08-07,
  08-13 and 08-20 against the code; three ADRs,
  [ADR-0033](decisions/0033-power-fuel-and-the-works.md),
  [ADR-0034](decisions/0034-rail-and-gas-light.md) and
  [ADR-0035](decisions/0035-services-letters-and-notes.md). **What the briefs found in the code:**
  hearths burn any fuel good by the kilogram in catalogue order, and there is no charcoal, coal or
  iron; firms use their owners' tools though ADR-0006 §5 decided otherwise; pits never reach ground
  water; landmarks are built over all walked ground though ADR-0028 §4 decided per region (the
  30 % of ADR-0032's DN amendment); ways keep wear whatever their modes; sight is the same by night;
  nothing holds literacy, records, healers or schools; tending reaches only the carer's own
  household; childbirth is one flat draw; custody and runs were deferred in M7d (CC2) for want of
  deposits; no lived world has struck coin; a money nobody uses is never accepted; valuing a money
  scans every market's trades per decision. **The briefs' open questions, answered:** no textiles
  or draught animals in M10 (wagonways are pushed by people); hearths may burn coal; charcoal draws
  a patch's increment, then its stock; works are owned by household firms, organizations by stake
  or polities, with no new partnership; far techniques are found by discovery or introduced by the
  observer, never imported; a works and a line do not hold a settlement Detailed, and a ride is a
  block; track is cells with a turn rule, on open ground; dark sight equals day sight until a world
  has lamps, and a lamp comes before gas; fares are posted terms; light changes the evening, not
  bedtime; services are paid on a new `Fee` channel; letters are techniques in one script a world;
  records are saved entities; kin tend unasked, others on a call; smallpox only by the observer's
  hand; one health officer; acceptance is learnt for coin and notes only; notes need writing and,
  if no deposits are wanted, begin with a polity's issue; legal tender is a law; fiat is a derived
  label. **Order:** the routing groundwork first (it speeds every many-settlement world), then
  power, rail and light, services and letters, money last (it needs letters), and the demo.
- **M9 design (2026-10-20, plan §7):** from the brief (`docs/briefs/m9-lod.md`), which reads
  01-04, 01-03 and 03-03, one ADR, [ADR-0032](decisions/0032-resolution-per-settlement.md).
  **Plan §4.5 amended:** the aggregate model keeps every person, household, tie, debt, office and
  asset as one record at every resolution and changes only how a settlement's day is computed;
  cohorts with people synthesised on focus would delete what no lifting recovers (01-04 §1.1),
  and are a later lever, built only if the household day misses M9's figure. **Why a household
  day:** M8 ended at about 5 ms a person-day against 1.6 µs for a year a minute at 100k; half a
  day is deciding (14.5 decisions a person-day), so a lighter person who still decides each
  activity saves 1.3–1.5× at most. A household-resolved settlement scores each household once at
  midnight with the live `decide::candidates`, shares its members' waking hours by the softmax's
  probabilities, and applies each block through the behaviour's own effect function in household
  id order, planning in parallel. **The brief's open questions, answered:** (1) blocks that leave
  home lay wear along cached routes; (2) `Visit`, `Fetch` beyond the settlement, `Carry`, `Band`
  and the fire behaviours are not taken while household-resolved, and a settlement holds Detailed
  while a fire burns, a band is out, a siege line stands or a gathering is called; (3) focus
  decides, with 30 days' hysteresis, and the observer may pin; worlds of three settlements or
  fewer stay wholly Detailed; (4) Gate C compares a year on Gate B's fixtures, with a ten-year
  horizon on the smoke seeds reported ungraded until its tolerances are set; (5) "skip to" is a
  host command over the same machinery (plan §8's first question: kept); (6) the climate forcing
  acts on the whole map, which has one weather series; (7) cohorts only if the gate misses;
  (8) M9's gate is 100,000 people in ten or more settlements, all but one household-resolved, at
  ≥ 0.1 simulated years a real minute on the container (1.64 s a day), memory recorded against
  plan §4.6, amended to the figure reached if it misses (ADR-0028 §1's rule). **Settlements side
  by side** (ADR-0028 §3's deferral) are not built: parallel planning of household days uses the
  cores without splitting every table by settlement. **Order:** the switch that changes nothing
  first (01-04 §4.10), then the core behaviours, the rest, Gate C, many settlements, the observer,
  skips, climate and the demo.
- **The M8 demo and the gate (2026-10-20, M8d slice DE, ADR-0031 §8, ADR-0028 §1):** two
  groups of 500 lived three years (`demos/m8/m8-demo.txt`). No household built a frame though 24
  knew framing: a first home is the cheapest covering shape (a hut), and a new home is begun only
  when spare goods times the kernel's `HOUSE_INVESTMENT_SHARE` pay for all of it, which no
  household reached in three years; the polities raised the only frames (two granaries, a hall
  and part of another). Not nudged: the share is a kernel constant, not a content prior, so moving
  it would be a model change made for a demo. Open for M9: whether a household should build in
  steps (a frame begun and finished as means allow, as homes were in M1), or weigh a frame's
  room against a hut's per hour of upkeep, so wealth reaches building over a lifetime rather than
  in one purchase. A shaking at 0.4 of each building's weight felled no hut or one-storey frame,
  so rules after a shaking were not exercised by the demo (slice DB's tests exercise them). The
  plan of streets was rejected at both settlements' first gatherings and passed at the port
  after three years. The gate: 10,000 at 0.0031 simulated years a real minute on the container
  (53.5 s a day; M8c measured 40 s a day over the same span's first 30 days with fewer
  buildings), the demo's 1,000 at 0.049; the gate is amended to these figures (ADR-0028 §1) and
  the target PC remains unmeasured. M8 is closed with v1's milestones; M9 (aggregate LOD) is the
  scale answer.
- **Design priors for a front (2026-10-20, M8d slice DD, ADR-0031 §7):** NUDGE: ornament runs
  to two hours of craft a square metre of front, a coat of daub takes 0.25 h and lime wash 0.15 h
  a square metre of wall, setting a front out about its middle two hours a bay; the front's
  tradition is a tenth of the walls open, 0.1 h of ornament, about half daubed and few
  symmetrical, with spreads of 5 %, 0.2 h, 0.5 and 0.4 between bands. "Could build" is knowing the
  program's technique, and lime burning for a lime wash. A building is seen `sight_m` times its
  eaves over the highest within 30 m (never under 2 m), one to four times. Each revisited if the
  demo (DE) shows fronts converging or drifting nowhere, or towers moving no taste.
- **Design priors for what a building raised together shows (2026-10-20, M8d slice DC's fourth
  part, ADR-0031 §6):** NUDGE: a raising stalls after 120 days with no work (a season's work
  missed); its users are every adult of its polity; each sees at most the eight households that
  gave most (a bound on the evidence written, not a model of attention), a full share being the
  work over its households' number; the four acts weigh half a gift (provision), as work seen
  (craft) and one unit of counsel either way. Each revisited if the demo (DE) shows no sponsor's
  standing moving by the buildings they put forward.
- **A test helper leaves state a load derives otherwise (2026-10-20, M8d slice DA):**
  `Sim::place_building_for_tests` leaves state a load derives otherwise: a save taken right after
  it does not resume exactly (the shaking test reloads once after placing). To be fixed.
- **Why no frame is built, probed (2026-10-19, M8d slice CY's first step, ADR-0031 §6):** read
  from the code, so it holds for every world. **Nobody can come to know framing:** founders bring
  the roundhouse, wood shaping, rubble walling and mud brick, but not `jointed_frame`, and its
  content tries toward it in no work (`tried_in = []`), so a world has it only by the observer's
  knowledge tool; without it no longhouse, granary or workshop, and so no second storey, is ever
  open to a household (`programs_for`). **Land does not reach the choice of what to build:** a
  household picks its program and shape first (`build::first_home`, `new_home`: coverage of
  members and goods, then the most floor its means and time buy, in labour and hauling hours),
  and only then weighs where (ADR-0030 §1); plot fees, ground rent and walks never make a
  smaller footprint or a taller shape the better buy, and a home that finds no ground is left
  unbuilt rather than tried smaller. **Width is fixed** (the longhouse's design 5 m, bays of
  2.5 m), so a frame grows only by bays and lofts. **What follows for M8d:** slice CZ gives
  framing a way to be found where it grows from (trying it in building homes, its rate a design
  prior logged as such, research 07-07 WO02) rather than founders who know it; weighs each home
  shape with the hours of the ground its footprint takes, so land enters the choice and a smaller
  footprint can win; and lets width vary within a program's range. The demo may still introduce
  framing by the observer's tool, recorded as an intervention. Grammar version 3 (CY) changes no
  behaviour, so it can come first.
